clauses.subject: clause-id
clauses.statement: A clause id is three dot-separated segments — contract, operation, subject — each matching `[a-z0-9-]+`. A clause item writes the subject alone; its file and section supply the rest.

clauses.subject: contract-segment
clauses.statement: The first segment is the file's front-matter `contract`, which names an entry of `spec/terms/contract.toml` listing that file.

clauses.subject: operation-segment
clauses.statement: The second segment is the `## ` section holding the item: an operation registered in the contract's fragment and listed in the front-matter `owns` of exactly one of the contract's files.

clauses.subject: subject-segment
clauses.statement: The third segment is a slug of at most 40 chars, unique within its operation. It is a name, not a registry entry.

clauses.subject: ids-are-stable
clauses.statement: An id changes when a fact changes obligor. Moving an operation between two files of one contract rewrites no id.

clauses.subject: malformed-id
clauses.statement: A clause id violating the shape, or a clause item under a section its file does not own, raises `SpecMalformedId`.

clauses.subject: duplicate-id
clauses.statement: A clause id appearing in two items raises `SpecDuplicateId`, naming both locations.

clauses.subject: file-headings
clauses.statement: A contract file carries front matter with `contract` and `owns`, one `# ` title matching its contract entry, one `## <operation>` section per owned operation in `owns` order, then an optional `## Shapes`.

clauses.subject: lede
clauses.statement: An operation section opens with a lede: one paragraph stating what the operation covers. The lede is the operation's only description; its fragment entry carries no gloss.

clauses.subject: clause-list
clauses.statement: After the lede, one contiguous list holds the section's clauses, each item `` - `<subject>` — <statement> `` on one line, optionally followed by its Why on a two-space-indented `*…*` line.

clauses.subject: after-list
clauses.statement: Prose, diagrams, tables, scenarios and unsettled lines follow the clause list and state no obligation.

clauses.subject: scenario
clauses.statement: A `#### Scenarios` list under an operation holds items `` - `<clause id>`: WHEN <trigger>, THEN <outcome> `` or a backticked `tests/fixtures/` path; the lock file attaches each to its clause.
clauses.why: because an example is the test an implementer writes first, and a rule without one leaves the agent to invent it

clauses.subject: bad-scenario
clauses.statement: A scenario naming a clause outside its operation, or holding neither a WHEN/THEN sentence nor a fixture path, raises `SpecScenario`.

clauses.subject: kind-is-computed
clauses.statement: A clause is a refusal when its statement names an error its fragment assigns to it, a limit when its fragment assigns it a named bound, and a behavior otherwise. The checker writes the kind into `spec/spec.lock.json`.

clauses.subject: statement-words
clauses.statement: A clause statement holds at most 40 words, a `{{id}}` reference counting as one.
clauses.why: because one item states one obligation; a longer item is two clauses or carries rationale

clauses.subject: file-length
clauses.statement: A contract file holds at most 900 lines.
clauses.why: because a file past that splits by adding a path to its contract entry, which renames nothing

clauses.subject: bad-anatomy
clauses.statement: A missing, extra or out-of-order `##` section, a missing lede, a broken clause list, a malformed item, a title differing from the registry, a file over its length or an overlong statement raises `SpecAnatomy`.

clauses.subject: fragment
clauses.statement: Each contract owns `spec/terms/<contract>.toml`, holding its operations, and its errors and named bounds each with a gloss.

clauses.subject: one-error-one-clause
clauses.statement: An error entry names the one clause raising it. That clause's statement names the error, and no other clause statement does; a second site reaches the condition by `{{id}}`.

clauses.subject: bound-entry
clauses.statement: A named-bound entry carries its owning clause, a value, a unit from `spec/terms/unit.toml` and a basis: `chosen`, `measured:<benchmark>` or `standard:<name>`. The owning statement carries the value followed by the unit.
clauses.why: because an unmeasured number presented as a measurement is a hypothesis stated as fact

clauses.subject: unregistered
clauses.statement: An unregistered error after `raises`, an entry naming a missing clause, an error absent from its clause or present in another, and a malformed bound raise `SpecRegistry`.

clauses.subject: pointer
clauses.statement: `{{<clause id>}}` is the one way a statement reaches a fact another clause owns. The lock file records every pointer as an edge.

clauses.subject: dangling
clauses.statement: A `{{id}}` naming no clause raises `SpecDanglingReference`.

clauses.subject: no-literature
clauses.statement: A spec file carries no hyperlink to an external document and no path under `references/`; either raises `SpecExternalLink`. Literature lives in `references/`, which cites clause ids.
clauses.why: because the contract is judged by behavior, and a citation invites arguing from authority

clauses.subject: why-cell
clauses.statement: A clause's Why is absent, one or more record ids such as `P3` or `A-store`, or `because` followed by at most 30 words stating the deciding criterion. A refusal carries a Why.

clauses.subject: record-threshold
clauses.statement: A decision earns a section in its contract's ADR when two or more clauses depend on it, it spans contracts, or it names a revisit trigger; otherwise it lives in a `because` cell.

clauses.subject: record-anatomy
clauses.statement: A principle `P<n>-<slug>.md` carries `# <id> — <title>`, a `**Status:**` line, then Context (optional), Decision, Options, Consequences, Revisit (optional), in at most 400 words.
clauses.why: because a principle argues one rule every contract obeys, and the length of the argument is part of its quality

clauses.subject: contract-adr
clauses.statement: A contract's decisions live in one `A-<contract>.md`: `# A-<contract> — <title>`, a `**Status:**` line, then one `## <decision>` section per decision, each holding its options table in at most 250 words.
clauses.why: because one file per contract puts every decision beside the clauses it governs, and a fresh corpus has no history to keep apart

clauses.subject: options-table
clauses.statement: A principle's Options and each ADR section hold one table headed `Option`, `Lost on`, `Cost` with two to five rows. One row is marked *(chosen)* with `—` as Lost on; every other row names the criterion it lost on.

clauses.subject: unsettled-line
clauses.statement: An unknown is one line where it applies: `unsettled:`, a question ending `?`, `owner:` and a handle, `affects:` and a `<contract>.<operation>`. Another form, or a heading `Open questions`, `Out of scope` or `See also`, raises `SpecUnsettled`.

clauses.subject: orphan-record
clauses.statement: A record no Why cites, a Why naming no record, and a record breaking its anatomy raise `SpecRecord`.

clauses.subject: status-is-computed
clauses.statement: `spec/status.md` is the sole statement of which clauses the tree demonstrates. No authored file says whether something is built.

clauses.subject: pin
clauses.statement: `spec/pins.toml` maps a clause id to one artifact: a `test` function path, a `theorem` constant under `formal/` or an `item` path. A refusal or a limit takes a test or a theorem.

clauses.subject: verdict
clauses.statement: An unpinned clause computes `committed`; a pinned clause computes `performed` when its artifact's final path segment is defined under `crates/`, `tools/` or `formal/`, and `broken` otherwise. A test carrying an `#[ignore]` attribute computes `broken`.

clauses.subject: tag-pin
clauses.statement: A line `// spec: <id>@<rev>` among the comments and attributes above a test function under `crates/` or `tools/` pins clause `<id>` to that test; `<rev>` is the first 8 hex digits of the statement's SHA-256.
clauses.why: because a pin written beside its test travels with every move and rename, and the digest records which wording the test demonstrates

clauses.subject: lean-tag
clauses.statement: A line `-- spec: <id>@<rev>` above a Lean `theorem` or `lemma` under `formal/`, past comments, docstrings and attributes, pins clause `<id>` to that theorem, with `<rev>` as in {{corpus.state.tag-pin}}.
clauses.why: because a theorem's pin then moves with the proof, and a reworded clause marks the proof stale

clauses.subject: theorem-beside-test
clauses.statement: A clause carries at most one theorem pin and one test pin, and computes `performed` when both perform: the theorem proves the model, the test ties the model to the code.

clauses.subject: stale-pin
clauses.statement: A tag whose `<rev>` differs from the digest of its clause's current statement raises `SpecStalePin`, and its clause computes `broken`.
clauses.why: because a reworded clause no longer says what its test was written to demonstrate

clauses.subject: unfinished-test
clauses.statement: A pinned test holding a body line that opens with `todo!`, and a pinned Lean declaration holding `sorry` or `admit`, compute `broken`.
clauses.why: because a placeholder demonstrates nothing, whether it panics at run time or proves by assumption

clauses.subject: scaffold
clauses.statement: `contextful-spec scaffold <contract>.<operation> --package <path>` writes one tagged test per refusal and limit clause of the operation into `<path>/tests/integration/`, its body a `todo!` naming the error or bound, and rewrites no existing function.

clauses.subject: scaffold-lean
clauses.statement: `contextful-spec scaffold <contract>.<operation> --lean <file>` appends one tagged theorem per clause of the operation, its statement the docstring and its proposition and proof `sorry`, and rewrites no existing theorem.

clauses.subject: coverage-floor
clauses.statement: `spec/pins.toml` carries a per-contract floor of pinned clauses. A live count below its floor raises `SpecCoverageRegression`.
clauses.why: because deleting a failing pin must not read as progress

clauses.subject: bad-pin
clauses.statement: A pin naming no clause, a tag above no declaration, an item pin on a refusal or limit, a broken pin, and one clause pinned to two tests or two theorems raise `SpecBrokenPin`.

clauses.subject: roadmap
clauses.statement: `spec/roadmap.md` names operations as `<contract>.<operation>` or `<contract>.*`. A name resolving to no operation, an operation claimed by two milestones, or a milestone lacking its `Reach:` or `Acceptance:` line raises `SpecRoadmap`.

clauses.subject: acceptance
clauses.statement: A milestone's `Acceptance:` line names one test under `crates/acceptance/`; that test computes `absent` when undefined, `open` when ignored, and `passing` otherwise.

clauses.subject: acceptance-first
clauses.statement: A milestone holding a pinned clause while its acceptance test computes `absent` raises `SpecAcceptanceMissing`.

clauses.subject: deferred-depth
clauses.statement: A milestone carrying a `Depth: operation` line admits only refusal and limit clauses; a behavior clause of an operation it schedules raises `SpecDeferredBehavior`.
clauses.why: because an unopened milestone fixes what it refuses and bounds, and its behavior is written against the code that opens it

clauses.subject: generated
clauses.statement: `spec/status.md`, `spec/targets.md`, `spec/cards/` and `spec/spec.lock.json` are regenerated by `contextful-spec state` and `contextful-spec extract`. A committed copy differing from regeneration raises `SpecStaleRender`.

clauses.subject: lock-file
clauses.statement: The lock file carries every clause with its segments, computed kind, statement, Why and location, each operation's lede, the per-file `owns` map, the registry and the pointer graph.

clauses.subject: card
clauses.statement: `contextful-spec state` renders `spec/cards/<contract>.md` per contract: each operation with its lede and clause count, each refusal as error and gloss, each bound as value, unit and basis, all naming their clause.

clauses.subject: dated-prose
clauses.statement: The words `planned`, `not yet`, `currently`, `today`, `shipped`, `implemented`, `previously`, `used to`, `legacy`, `TODO`, `FIXME` and `WIP`, and an ISO date, raise `SpecDatedProse` in any authored file.
clauses.why: because build state is computed, and a dated sentence is stale the day it lands

clauses.subject: counterfactual
clauses.statement: The words `will`, `would` and `shall` raise `SpecCounterfactual` in a contract file or a guide.
clauses.why: because a contract states present behavior, and a record's Options is where a path not taken is described

clauses.subject: banned-vocabulary
clauses.statement: The nouns `seam`, `load-bearing`, `wedge`, `rung`, `land-grab` and an unbackticked `axiom`, a word whose digest `spec/terms/refused-names.toml` lists, a bare `#<digits>` and a pull-request link raise `SpecBannedWord`.

clauses.subject: local-path
clauses.statement: A path beginning `/Users/`, `/home/`, `$HOME/` or `~/` raises `SpecLocalPath`.

clauses.subject: fence
clauses.statement: A diagram is a fenced `mermaid` block; box-drawing characters outside a fence raise `SpecAsciiDiagram`.

clauses.subject: boundary
clauses.statement: A diagram draws a contract, party, process or trust zone as a container — a flowchart `subgraph` or a sequence `box` — holding its components. A flowchart node naming a contract or a boundary raises `SpecDiagramBoundary`.

clauses.subject: node
clauses.statement:
A flowchart node names one thing in at most 5 words: its label holds no `·`, `
`, `,`, `;`, `: ` or error identifier, is no operation name, and sets no article second. A breach raises `SpecDiagramNode`.
clauses.why: because a box of bundled attributes or a verb hides the things and what flows between them; operations, limits and errors ride the edges

clauses.subject: shape
clauses.statement: A node labelled with a snake_case identifier or a phrase ending `table`, `store`, `log` or `queue` is a cylinder `[( )]`, and a label ending `?` is a decision `{ }`. A breach raises `SpecDiagramShape`.
clauses.why: because one shape meaning one kind lets a reader tell data from the parts acting on it at a glance

clauses.subject: edge
clauses.statement: A flowchart edge points one way; its label holds at most 5 words and no `·`, and an edge touching no decision node carries one. A breach raises `SpecDiagramEdge`.
clauses.why: because an unlabelled line says two things relate without saying how, and a two-way line hides which side acts

clauses.subject: decision
clauses.statement: A decision node asks a question or names a condition in at most 8 words and no error identifier, has an incoming edge, and has two or more outgoing edges each labelled with a distinct outcome. A breach raises `SpecDiagramDecision`.
clauses.why: because a branch without a guard on each exit leaves the reader to guess which path a case takes

clauses.subject: branch
clauses.statement: A non-decision node with an outgoing edge labelled `yes` or `no`, an outgoing error identifier beside another exit, or two exits opening `if`, `when`, `over`, `under` or `else` raises `SpecDiagramBranch`; a branch is a decision node.
clauses.why: because a condition hidden in edge labels off a box reads as parallel flow

clauses.subject: connected
clauses.statement: Every flowchart node, or a subgraph enclosing it, is an edge endpoint. A breach raises `SpecDiagramOrphan`.
clauses.why: because an unconnected element asserts nothing about the system

clauses.subject: unique-label
clauses.statement: No two nodes of one flowchart carry the same label; a second mention reuses the node id. A breach raises `SpecDiagramDuplicate`.
clauses.why: because one label naming two nodes leaves the reader to decide whether they are one thing

clauses.subject: layout
clauses.statement: A flowchart header declares `LR`, `TB` or `TD`, no subgraph declares `direction`, subgraphs nest at most 2 levels, and the chart holds at most 20 nodes and 25 edges. A breach raises `SpecDiagramLayout`.
clauses.why: because one reading direction keeps the flow followable, and a chart past that size or depth is two diagrams

clauses.subject: sequence
clauses.statement: A sequence diagram declares each participant it messages and messages each it declares, and holds at most 6 participants, 15 messages, 2 messages from a participant to itself and fragments nested 2 levels. A breach raises `SpecDiagramSequence`.
clauses.why: because a sequence diagram shows one scenario's interactions, and branching logic past that belongs in a flowchart

clauses.subject: message
clauses.statement: A sequence message label holds at most 8 words and a note at most 12 words. A breach raises `SpecDiagramMessage`.
clauses.why: because a message names one call; its parameters and bounds belong in clauses

clauses.subject: state
clauses.statement: A state diagram has one top-level `[*]` start reaching every state, every state has an outgoing transition, `[*]` counting as a target, and a transition label holds at most 6 words. A breach raises `SpecDiagramState`.
clauses.why: because an unreachable or dead-end state is a lifecycle the system cannot run

clauses.subject: file
clauses.statement: Each deployment provider's target profile is `spec/targets/<provider>.toml`: named shapes, exactly one marked default, each with a kind, the profiles it hosts, an optional per-invocation wall-clock cap, its exclusions and the primitive filling each role.

clauses.subject: roles
clauses.statement: A shape fills eight roles — cron tick, reconciler, durable orchestrator, single-writer catalog, object store, hot-path query face, heavy compute and secrets — and may fill a realtime run projection.

clauses.subject: incomplete
clauses.statement: A shape leaving a role unfilled, or a target file marking other than one default shape, raises `SpecTargetIncomplete`, naming the provider, the shape and the role.
clauses.why: because an unfilled role surfaces only when a deploy reaches it, on someone else's account

clauses.subject: cap-unrecorded
clauses.statement: A shape whose cap sits at or below the {{topology.deploy.wall-clock-cap}} bound and whose exclusions omit `first-time-backfill` or `component-connector` raises `SpecTargetCapUnrecorded`.
clauses.why: because the exclusion is the difference between a refused dispatch and a job killed mid-run

clauses.subject: function-profile
clauses.statement: A function-class shape listing a profile other than `edge` raises `SpecTargetFunctionProfile`, naming the provider and the shape.
clauses.why: because {{topology.package.edge-eligibility}} admits the edge profile alone on a function-class target

clauses.subject: page
clauses.statement: `contextful-spec state` renders `spec/targets.md` from the target files: per provider, a role table across its shapes and a diagram of its default shape.
clauses.why: because a diagram drawn by hand beside the data it shows drifts from it

clauses.subject: file
clauses.statement: Each contract has one guide, `spec/guide/<contract>.md`: front matter `contract`, one `# ` title equal to the contract's registry title, then prose of at most 700 words outside diagrams.

clauses.subject: non-normative
clauses.statement: A guide holds no clause item and names no registered error; it reaches a rule by `{{id}}`. No contract file links a guide.
clauses.why: because a rule restated in teaching prose is a second home that drifts from the first

clauses.subject: bad-guide
clauses.statement: A contract without a guide, a guide breaking its shape or length, a guide holding a clause item or an error name, and a contract file linking a guide raise `SpecGuide`.

clauses.subject: workspace
clauses.statement: One Cargo workspace compiles both halves. Neither half ships as its own binary, package scope or release; "read path" and "run path" name a boundary, not a product.

clauses.subject: read-path
clauses.statement: The read path holds data at rest and its retrieval: the context store, the catalog, query and ranking, memory queries, bucket sync, and the capability check a record passes before it lands.

clauses.subject: run-path
clauses.statement: The run path holds execution: the journal, the scheduler, cursor commit, awakeables, and every connector invoked as a journaled step. It owns no store and no ranking.

clauses.subject: three-crossings
clauses.statement: Exactly three contracts cross between the halves: the connector interface world, the columnar-part-plus-manifest layout, and the capability-token format. No general internal call surface joins the halves.

clauses.subject: crossing-version
clauses.statement: Each crossing carries its own version and a conformance suite both sides run. A member added to a crossing passes a security review before admission.

clauses.subject: undeclared-crossing
clauses.statement: A run-path crate reaches a read-path crate only through a crate carrying one of the three crossings; {{assurance.gate.crate-graph}} checks every edge.

clauses.subject: run-path-droppable
clauses.statement: A build linking no execution core, scheduler or component host serves reads of data a full daemon produced, over the identical part-and-manifest layout and connector contract.

clauses.subject: cli-binary
clauses.statement: The system ships one command binary, `contextful`, and one package scope, `@contextful/*`. The smallest deployable build is a profile, not a crate.

clauses.subject: mediation
clauses.statement: Every function returning or releasing a stored row takes the enforcement stack's admission value as a parameter ({{assurance.gate.row-token}}), so a row path that skips enforcement does not type-check. No operator switch disables mediation.

clauses.subject: enforcement-span
clauses.statement: The enforcement stack spans both halves: capability allowlists and the journal on the run path; the statement guard, visibility semi-join, row and column restriction, masking and the audit chain on the read path.

clauses.subject: semantic-layer
clauses.statement: Enforcement interprets no content. Retrieval, memory synthesis, the analyst surface and inference placement interpret content and reach enforcement through the three crossings alone.

clauses.subject: one-tree
clauses.statement: Laptop through cluster runs from one source tree. A single-node or edge deployment runs no external queue, cache or coordination process; a multi-node deployment adds one shared database.

clauses.subject: connector-pillar
clauses.statement: A connector is an interface world run in a sandboxed component host that mediates every capability. A native connector, the first-party path for stateful sources, satisfies the same schema, record and cursor contract.

clauses.subject: open-store
clauses.statement: Table data sits in columnar parts with a JSON manifest and a rebuildable catalog on plain object storage, readable by standard SQL tooling. No proprietary container or opaque blob holds table data.

clauses.subject: inference-egress
clauses.statement: Model access leaves the process through one operator-configured endpoint speaking OpenAI-compatible HTTP. The one provider-shaped step serializes a tool's parameter schema into the provider's envelope.

clauses.subject: vendor-sdk
clauses.statement: The dependency audit raises `VendorSdkLinked`, naming the crate and the dependency, for a crate declaring a model-vendor SDK or a second outbound path to a model.

clauses.subject: local-first
clauses.statement: Pipelines need no network beyond their sources, and bucket sync is opt-in per deployment. The engine makes no control-plane callback, no license check, and sends no telemetry to its authors.

clauses.subject: script-runtime
clauses.statement: A JavaScript runtime linked into any profile raises `ScriptRuntimeLinked`. The authoring surface is a build-time compiler emitting a serialized, content-hashed plan.

clauses.subject: memory-substrate
clauses.statement: Synthesized memory's episode, fact, entity and preference tables are ordinary store tables, and its synthesis pipeline is an ordinary run-path workflow on the same journal, cursor and retry machinery.

clauses.subject: two-spines
clauses.statement: The run record answers what happened on the write side and the request ledger on the read side. No third surface merges them.

clauses.subject: crate-map
clauses.statement: Seventeen crates compose the workspace. `contextful-cli` is the binary and wires every adapter per profile by dependency injection.

clauses.subject: crate-map-drift
clauses.statement: A `crates/` package absent from the crate tree under `## Shapes`, or a {{topology.package.crate-map}} count differing from that tree's entries, raises `CrateMapDrift`, naming the package or both counts.
clauses.why: because a package added without a map entry otherwise passes every other gate

clauses.subject: domain-crate
clauses.statement: `contextful-core` holds the pure domain types and the port traits every adapter implements, performs no I/O, and links into every profile.

clauses.subject: domain-impurity
clauses.statement: `contextful-core` declaring an async runtime, a component host, an HTTP client or a columnar-format implementation raises `DomainCrateImpurity`, naming the dependency and the feature that pulled it.

clauses.subject: dependency-direction
clauses.statement: A dependency edge from `contextful-core` toward an adapter crate raises `TopologyDependencyInversion`, naming both crates and the manifest line.

clauses.subject: profile
clauses.statement: Three profiles compile from the workspace, each a Cargo feature bundle selected at build time: `contextful-edge`, `contextful-full`, `contextful-control`. Each links the dependencies its role names and nothing else.

clauses.subject: fixed-at-build
clauses.statement: No run-time detection widens a running binary into another profile's feature set. Build, release and automation tooling links into no profile.

clauses.subject: edge-profile
clauses.statement: `contextful-edge` is the read replica: it pulls native connectors, syncs parts and manifests from a bucket, and serves a read-only SQL replica. It links no scheduler, script runtime or component host.

clauses.subject: edge-eligibility
clauses.statement: The edge profile is the one profile a function-class target hosts. Execution on such a deployment runs on a worker target.

clauses.subject: full-profile
clauses.statement: `contextful-full` is the daemon: the durable-execution core, the in-process scheduler, the component host, the SQL query face, transforms, the full-text and vector sidecars, the tool server, and `pg-catalog`.

clauses.subject: control-profile
clauses.statement: `contextful-control` is the self-hosted control plane: team state, the edit-time configuration document and identity. It materializes canonical TOML on apply and is the one profile linking the CRDT library.

clauses.subject: component-host
clauses.statement: A component connector runs where a component host is linked: the full profile and the container or worker shapes built from it. The edge profile runs native connectors.

clauses.subject: host-missing
clauses.statement: Dispatching a component connector on a profile with no component host raises `ComponentHostMissing`, naming the connector and the profile, with no fallback to a similarly named native source.

clauses.subject: crdt-leak
clauses.statement: The CRDT library in the resolved dependency graph of the edge or full profile raises `ProfileDependencyLeak`, naming the profile and the path that pulled it. A daemon or replica reads materialized text.

clauses.subject: store-write-engine-free
clauses.statement: `contextful-context` resolved without its `read` feature and reaching `duckdb` or `libduckdb-sys` through a normal dependency raises `StoreWriteLinksEngine`, naming the package and the path that pulled it.
clauses.why: because a host that lands, folds or scans a store and serves no read otherwise links a bundled SQL engine it never calls

clauses.subject: transport-optional
clauses.statement: `contextful-outbound` resolved without its `transport-ureq` feature and reaching `ureq`, `hyper`, `reqwest`, `rustls` or `curl` through a normal dependency raises `TransportStackLinked`, naming the path that pulled it.

clauses.subject: decode-network-free
clauses.statement: `contextful-decode` reaching `contextful-outbound`, `ureq`, `hyper`, `reqwest`, `rustls`, `curl` or `tokio` through a normal dependency raises `DecodeLinksNetwork`, naming the path that pulled it.

clauses.subject: exchange-optional
clauses.statement: `contextful-policy` links the external-assertion stack, `jsonwebtoken` and `rsa`, only under its non-default `exchange` feature, which only the binary may enable, and only alongside wiring {{authority.exchange.surface}}. Another `crates/` package whose resolved graph reaches either raises `ExchangeDependencyLeak`, naming the path.
clauses.why: because an embedder admitting credentials with no identity provider then links no RSA code, and `rsa` carries a timing advisory with no patched release

clauses.subject: sqlite-adapter
clauses.statement: `contextful-sqlite` alone declares the SQLite binding and enables no link feature itself; only `contextful-cli` turns on its `bundled` feature. Any other declaration or enablement raises `SqliteLinkForced`, naming the manifest line.

clauses.subject: store-sqlite-free
clauses.statement: `contextful-context` reaching `libsqlite3-sys` through a normal dependency, with its default features, raises `StoreLinksSqlite`, naming the path that pulled it.

clauses.subject: unsupported-shape
clauses.statement: A target profile claiming a shape its provider does not provide raises `TargetShapeUnsupported`, naming the shape and the missing primitive.

clauses.subject: wall-clock-cap
clauses.statement: A target capping per-invocation wall clock at 15 min hosts neither a first-time backfill nor a component connector, and its target profile records both exclusions.

clauses.subject: parity
clauses.statement: One declaration run on every control-plane target produces byte-identical table parts, compared against the reference target inside each target's object store after a 24 h soak.

clauses.subject: parity-divergence
clauses.statement: A byte difference from the reference output raises `ParityDivergence`, naming the target, the table and the first differing part.

clauses.subject: posture-mismatch
clauses.statement: A probe answer outside its descriptor's gate, or an unreachable hostname, raises `HostnamePostureMismatch` with the hostname, the declared gate and the observed response, and fails the deploy.

clauses.subject: probe-table
clauses.statement: A probe table entry absent from the descriptor set, or a descriptor with no probe entry, raises `ProbeTableDrift` before the deploy runs, naming the hostname and the side missing it.

clauses.subject: unknown-field
clauses.statement: A descriptor decodes with excess properties refused; an unmodelled key raises `DescriptorUnknownField`, naming the key and the contract version.

clauses.subject: unconfigured-gateway
clauses.statement: A routing hop with no store configuration answers `503` on every route and raises `GatewayUnconfigured`.

clauses.subject: issuer-key
clauses.statement: The engine's HTTP face refuses to start without a verification key that resolves and parses, raising `IssuerKeyUnusable` and naming the input; no generated key substitutes.

clauses.subject: container-readiness
clauses.statement: A retrieval container reaches readiness within 8 s of a cold start, before its snapshot-set hydration completes.

clauses.subject: primitive
clauses.statement: Coordination rests on one property: a linearizable conditional write. No component depends on a stronger one, and the tree ships no consensus implementation or external coordination service.

clauses.subject: inventory
clauses.statement: The single-writer operations are the lease row, the cursor compare-and-swap, {{store.fold.pointer-commit}}, a lease acquisition, a leased pipeline's commit-log entry, the bucket manifest commit and a configuration apply's version claim. No other operation needs a single writer.

clauses.subject: lease-row
clauses.statement: A lease row is keyed by a pipeline, a source partition, a table's compaction or a deployment's cadence, and carries a holder, an expiry instant and a fence taken by one conditional update.

clauses.subject: catalog-clock
clauses.statement: The catalog evaluates a lease row's expiry against its own clock, never a caller-supplied instant.

clauses.subject: fence-advances
clauses.statement: Each acquisition of a lease row increments its fence, and release keeps the fence, so the fence never repeats for a key.

clauses.subject: fenced-commit
clauses.statement: A commit under a lease is a conditional write predicated on the holder's fence; a predicate matching nothing is {{store.lease.stale-fence}}.

clauses.subject: cursor-cas
clauses.statement: A cursor compare-and-swap is one conditional update predicated on the stored version, read back by its affected-row count.

clauses.subject: cadence-lease-ttl
clauses.statement: A cadence lease is granted for 90 s.

clauses.subject: cadence-lease-renewal
clauses.statement: The reconciler renews a cadence lease every 30 s while its applied document schedules a dispatchable unit.

clauses.subject: cadence-fallback
clauses.statement: A deployment's fallback cron fires only after taking the cadence lease itself, so one fire holds the current fence.

clauses.subject: catalog-port
clauses.statement: Every catalog backend is reached through the `Catalog` port, and code above the port names no backend. Swapping a backend is a wiring change in `contextful-cli`.

clauses.subject: backends
clauses.statement: Single-node self-hosting uses a local catalog file owned by one process; a self-hosted cluster uses Postgres via `pg-catalog`; a managed edge deployment uses per-object SQLite; a managed cloud deployment uses managed Postgres.

clauses.subject: weak-backend
clauses.statement: A catalog backend whose conditional update is not linearizable refuses at open with {{surface.apply.weak-conditional-backend}}.

clauses.subject: cluster-availability
clauses.statement: Cluster availability is the shared database's availability. The engine adds no replication and no failover protocol between daemons.

clauses.subject: air-gap
clauses.statement: Single-node and edge deployments reach no process outside themselves for coordination, and run air-gapped with only their sources reachable.

clauses.subject: components
clauses.statement: A store holds Parquet table data, JSON run and snapshot manifests, one pointer object per table, and two SQLite catalogs, `derived.sqlite` and `machine.sqlite`. Parquet, manifests and pointers are canonical.
clauses.why: because a catalog that is both a rebuildable cache and a commit point resurrects half-published snapshots on rebuild

clauses.subject: store-root
clauses.statement: A project's store sits at `.contextful/context/<project>/`, holding both catalogs, `config.toml`, `cursors/` and one `tables/<t>/` directory per table.

clauses.subject: table-directory
clauses.statement: A table directory holds `schema.json`, `_pointer.json`, `data/snapshots/<id>/`, `data/runs/<run-id>/<node-id>/` and `requests/`.

clauses.subject: snapshot-id
clauses.statement: A snapshot id is `snapshot-` followed by a nanosecond value zero-padded to 20 chars, equal to the greater of the commit instant and the previous id plus one.
clauses.why: because a wall clock that steps backwards breaks lexical order equalling commit order

clauses.subject: part-name
clauses.statement: A data file is `part-<ordinal>.parquet`, the ordinal zero-padded to five digits and unique within its directory.

clauses.subject: staging
clauses.statement: A fold in flight writes under `data/snapshots/<id>.staging/`, and no file list resolves inside it.

clauses.subject: run-manifest
clauses.statement: A run commits by conditionally creating `_manifest.json` in its node directory, carrying `{run_id, table, node_id, parts, committed_at, pipeline_id?, cursor?, fence?}`, where `node_id` equals the enclosing segment.

clauses.subject: uncommitted-run
clauses.statement: A node directory holding no `_manifest.json` is in flight and its parts join no file list; a leased pipeline's run also waits for its commit-log entry.

clauses.subject: cursor-in-commit
clauses.statement: A pipeline's committed position is the cursor inside its newest commit: the newest commit-log entry for a leased pipeline, the highest run-manifest cursor otherwise. `machine.sqlite` caches it.
clauses.why: because a position committed apart from its rows re-lands the batch after a crash between the two writes

clauses.subject: snapshot-manifest
clauses.statement: A snapshot's `_manifest.json` carries `{snapshot_id, parent, table, created_at, includes_runs, primary_key, order_by, row_count, valid_time?, indexes, fence}`, and each entry of `parts` and `indexes` carries its `key_version`.

clauses.subject: table-pointer
clauses.statement: `tables/<t>/_pointer.json` names the table's current snapshot and the fence that published it. A snapshot is readable only when the pointer or a chain of `parent` links from it reaches it.

clauses.subject: manifest-default
clauses.statement: A field added to a manifest carries a default value.

clauses.subject: manifest-unreadable
clauses.statement: A run manifest or a reachable snapshot manifest that fails to parse raises `StoreManifestUnreadable`, naming the table and the file, and the table answers no read until it parses.

clauses.subject: schema-file
clauses.statement: A table's schema is `schema.json` in Arrow JSON form; each arriving batch's schema merges into it and the merged result replaces it.

clauses.subject: immutable-files
clauses.statement: A run file is written once and never edited, a snapshot directory is immutable, and a fold writes a new snapshot.

clauses.subject: derived-catalog
clauses.statement: `derived.sqlite` is a cache: `contextful context rebuild-catalog` reconstructs it from the pointers, the manifests they reach, every committed run manifest and every `schema.json`. It is never synced and commits nothing.

clauses.subject: machine-catalog
clauses.statement: `machine.sqlite` holds one machine's journal, cursor cache and lease rows. It is never synced, never rebuilt and never replaced by a pull.

clauses.subject: catalog-ports
clauses.statement: The store reaches `machine.sqlite` through {{topology.coordinate.catalog-port}} and `derived.sqlite` through the `DerivedCatalog` port, both traits in `contextful-core`; `contextful-sqlite` implements both, and a host implements either over its own connection.

clauses.subject: unknown-table
clauses.statement: A table name no `schema.json` in the tree declares raises `StoreUnknownTable`, never an empty result.

clauses.subject: node-segment
clauses.statement: The `<node-id>` run-path segment and the node id in a ledger filename keep two machines writing one logical run id in disjoint files.

clauses.subject: node-id-order
clauses.statement: A process resolves its node id once: `CONTEXTFUL_NODE_ID`, then `[node] id`, then a random `node-<8 hex>` generated once and persisted.

clauses.subject: node-id-state-path
clauses.statement: A generated node id persists under `$CONTEXTFUL_STATE_DIR`, else `$XDG_STATE_HOME/contextful`, else the platform user-state directory, outside the store root.
clauses.why: because a copied store carrying its identity makes two machines one holder

clauses.subject: node-id-shape
clauses.statement: A node id longer than 64 chars or outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` raises `StoreNodeIdInvalid` at process start, before any path, key or lease carries it.

clauses.subject: node-id-shared
clauses.statement: A node id declared in a control-plane configuration raises `StoreNodeIdShared`.
clauses.why: because a control-plane snapshot applies to every machine reconciling it, making one id many holders

clauses.subject: node-id-local
clauses.statement: A machine with no writable state directory takes the reserved node id `local`.

clauses.subject: table-block
clauses.statement: A table block declares any of `primary_key`, `order_by`, `write_mode`, `replicate`, `subject_id`, `class`, `policy`, `visibility`, `valid_time`, `view`, `cluster_by`, `partition_by`, `retain_runs`, `columns`, `agent_description`, `agent_hint` and `example_queries`; an unset key is absent from the canonical serialization.

clauses.subject: column-types
clauses.statement: `columns` maps a column to a type spelled as {{store.reconcile.typed-landing}} reads it; every landing into the table, a pipeline run included, lands that column in the declared type.
clauses.why: because a JSON value alone cannot say it carries bytes or a vector

clauses.subject: two-genres
clauses.statement: A table holds items, landed by connectors, or artifacts, synthesized and tagged by an open kind string the engine does not enumerate. Both append, dedupe on content and carry a timestamp.

clauses.subject: unkeyed-union
clauses.statement: A table declaring no `primary_key` reads as the byte-identical union of its committed runs.

clauses.subject: dedup-view
clauses.statement: A table declaring `primary_key` reads through `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY <pk> ORDER BY <order_by> DESC, _ingested_at DESC, _run_id DESC, _row_seq DESC) = 1` over its current snapshot, if any, unioned with the committed runs that snapshot omits.
clauses.why: because a keyed table read as a union before its first fold inflates every aggregate silently

clauses.subject: order-by-default
clauses.statement: `order_by` names the column picking the surviving row per key, and defaults to `_ingested_at`.

clauses.subject: order-by-unknown
clauses.statement: An `order_by` naming a column neither declared nor injected raises `StoreOrderByUnknownColumn` at validation, before the first batch.
clauses.why: because an ordering column absent from every file reads as null and picks survivors arbitrarily

clauses.subject: key-unknown
clauses.statement: A `primary_key` naming a column neither declared nor injected raises `StoreKeyUnknownColumn` at validation, before the first batch.
clauses.why: because a key column absent from every file partitions every row into one group and collapses the table to a single row

clauses.subject: write-mode
clauses.statement: `write_mode` is `append`, the default, keeping the last write per key and retiring no key, or `replace`.

clauses.subject: replace-frontier
clauses.statement: Under `replace`, a read covers the newest run carrying the source's complete state plus every run committed after it.

clauses.subject: replace-retains
clauses.statement: A replacing run leaves the runs it displaced on disk until `retain_runs` passes, writes no erasure receipt and walks no lineage.

clauses.subject: empty-run
clauses.statement: A run landing zero rows commits a manifest with no parts and replaces nothing; a table with no rows registers as a zero-row relation over its declared and injected columns.

clauses.subject: fold-coverage
clauses.statement: Validation warns, naming the table, where a key is declared and no enabled compaction job covers the table.

clauses.subject: read-side-keys
clauses.statement: A declaration key changes what a read returns and rewrites no committed part; a key added after rows land applies from the next read.

clauses.subject: underscore-namespace
clauses.statement: Column names beginning `_` belong to the engine; the injected set and the reserved optional set are its whole content.

clauses.subject: injected
clauses.statement: The engine injects `_ingested_at` as a non-null Parquet `TIMESTAMP(UTC, NANOS)`, `_run_id`, `_batch_seq` as int32 where a batch scope exists, `_site_id`, and `_authored_by` where an authenticated subject authorized the write, replacing any producer value.
clauses.why: because a string instant does not sort by time once fractions or offsets appear

clauses.subject: row-seq
clauses.statement: The engine injects `_row_seq`, a non-null int64 numbering a run's rows from 0 in batch order, replacing any producer value.
clauses.why: because a run's rows share `_ingested_at` and `_run_id`, and keeping the last write per key needs an order among them

clauses.subject: no-placeholder
clauses.statement: A path with no batch scope or no authenticated subject omits that column instead of writing nulls.

clauses.subject: optional
clauses.statement: A producer sets any of `_modality`, `_lang`, `_provenance` and `_prompt_hash`, and each surfaces in the provenance envelope where present.

clauses.subject: modality
clauses.statement: `_modality` takes one of text, image, audio, structured or mixed; another value fails validation of its batch.

clauses.subject: lang-and-provenance
clauses.statement: `_lang` carries a BCP-47 tag; `_provenance` carries the evidence rows the row derives from, addressed by the identity the source table keys on.

clauses.subject: prompt-hash
clauses.statement: `_prompt_hash` is `sha256:<hex>` over the prompt template, not the rendered prompt.

clauses.subject: column-name
clauses.statement: A producer column inside the `_` namespace and outside the optional set raises `StoreReservedColumnName` at reconciliation, before any Parquet.

clauses.subject: table-namespaces
clauses.statement: The engine reserves two table namespaces: the durable run record, and the prefix the visibility engine mirrors access data under.

clauses.subject: table-name
clauses.statement: A pipeline declaring a table inside a reserved namespace raises `StoreReservedTableName` when its manifest is assembled, naming the reservation.

clauses.subject: ledger-suffix
clauses.statement: A table name ending in `__requests` is reserved to request-ledger relations and refuses as {{store.reserve.table-name}}.

clauses.subject: ledger-path
clauses.statement: A run's request ledger is `requests/<run-id>.<node-id>.parquet`, disjoint per run and per writing node.

clauses.subject: ledger-append
clauses.statement: Appends to one run's ledger file serialize under a lock on it, and an append returns once its rows and the rename are synced to disk.

clauses.subject: ledger-fold
clauses.statement: Each fold pass merges a table's committed ledger files into `requests/folded-<snapshot-id>.parquet`, and a replica carries ledgers with their table.
clauses.why: because one ledger file per run per node per table grows listing and diff cost without bound

clauses.subject: ledger-retention
clauses.statement: A ledger row is collected 365 d after its run committed.

clauses.subject: explicit-file-list
clauses.statement: Every read hands `read_parquet` an explicit sorted file list resolved from the pointer and the manifests, never a glob; a stray file joins nothing.

clauses.subject: union-by-name
clauses.statement: Every read passes `union_by_name=true`; a column resolves to the common supertype of the files carrying it, and the generated relation casts no column but a vector, per {{store.reconcile.half-width}}.

clauses.subject: lattice
clauses.statement: The type lattice holds one promotion, `Int64` with `Float64` to `Float64`; a JSON type absorbs `Utf8`.

clauses.subject: incompatible
clauses.statement: Any other pair of types observed for one column raises `StoreSchemaIncompatible` at the write, naming the column, the stored type and the arriving type.

clauses.subject: float-loss
clauses.statement: An `Int64` value above 9007199254740992 loses precision once a `Float64` batch lands on its column.

clauses.subject: binary-and-vector
clauses.statement: The lattice holds `Binary`, `FixedSizeBinary(n)` and a `FixedSizeList` of `Float32` or `Float16` at dimension n; none takes a promotion, so a width, item or dimension change meets {{store.reconcile.incompatible}}.

clauses.subject: typed-landing
clauses.statement: A producer declares these types; a JSON batch carries bytes as padded base64 and a vector as a number array of its dimension, and any other value meets {{store.reconcile.incompatible}}.

clauses.subject: stored-type
clauses.statement: A column `schema.json` holds as a binary or vector type lands a later undeclared JSON value in that type, so a run after the first needs no declaration.

clauses.subject: half-width
clauses.statement: A `Float16` vector stores each element at half width in Parquet. The engine reads its elements as `FLOAT`, either binary type as `BLOB`, and a vector as an `ARRAY` of its dimension through one relation cast.

clauses.subject: key-widening
clauses.statement: A primary-key column takes no `Float64` promotion: the widening batch raises `StoreKeyWidened` before any Parquet, as does a fold meeting a key already reconciled to `Float64`.

clauses.subject: additive
clauses.statement: An unseen column joins the merged schema, and files written before it read it as null.

clauses.subject: no-invented-column
clauses.statement: A scan invents no column: an ordering column absent from every file enters through a zero-row branch, and a column added after a table's first rows projects as a literal null.

clauses.subject: first-sight
clauses.statement: A destination creates a table on the first schema it sees and merges each later schema into `schema.json`.

clauses.subject: fold-never-narrows
clauses.statement: A fold backfills nulls and widens types; it narrows no type and drops no column.

clauses.subject: no-history
clauses.statement: Reconciliation keeps the current shape alone; a past widening is attributed from the run files.

clauses.subject: reserved-set-versioned
clauses.statement: Adding an injected column advances the semantics version, whose fingerprint recipe names the column.

clauses.subject: pass
clauses.statement: A pass selects the committed runs the current snapshot omits, dedupes by key or unions, reconciles the schema, sorts by `cluster_by`, partitions, writes Parquet and every declared sidecar into staging, then commits by {{store.fold.pointer-commit}}.

clauses.subject: valid-time-line
clauses.statement: A keyed table declaring `valid_time` partitions on the key together with the valid-time line and keeps one row per line.

clauses.subject: includes-runs
clauses.statement: A snapshot's `includes_runs` names each run it folded as `<run-id>/<node-id>`, the run's own directory; a run committed afterwards reads on top of it.

clauses.subject: triggers
clauses.statement: A pass fires at 50 runs committed on a table, 6 h after the table's previous pass, or on `contextful context compact <table>`.

clauses.subject: retention
clauses.statement: `retain_runs` defaults to 7 d; a folded run, a superseded snapshot and its sidecars are collected once older than the window.

clauses.subject: result
clauses.statement: A pass reports each table as folded, nothing-landed or failed, and a nothing-landed table does not stop the pass.

clauses.subject: collection-failed
clauses.statement: A collection that fails reports its failure: beside `folded` when the pass published, since the snapshot stays published, and as `failed` otherwise; either way the command exits non-zero.

clauses.subject: unknown-table
clauses.statement: A pass naming a table no `schema.json` declares halts the command with {{store.lay-out.unknown-table}}.

clauses.subject: compaction-lease
clauses.statement: A pass holds the table's compaction lease and stamps its fence into the snapshot manifest and the pointer.

clauses.subject: pointer-commit
clauses.statement: A pass publishes by replacing `_pointer.json` conditioned on the ETag it read at pass start, with `If-Match` on an object store and a version-checked rename on a filesystem.

clauses.subject: partial-snapshot
clauses.statement: A reader observes a snapshot and every declared sidecar together or neither; a commit exposing one without the other raises `StorePartialSnapshot`.

clauses.subject: lost-pointer
clauses.statement: A pass whose pointer replace loses its condition publishes nothing, and its staged snapshot is collected.

clauses.subject: staging-collected
clauses.statement: A staging directory, and a snapshot directory no pointer chain reaches, are collected by the next pass and read by nobody.

clauses.subject: non-blocking
clauses.statement: A statement running during a pass reads the snapshot the pointer named when it started; statements starting after the commit read the new one.

clauses.subject: supersedes
clauses.statement: A new snapshot supersedes the previous one without deleting it, and a bounded read reaches the older one until retention collects it.

clauses.subject: kinds
clauses.statement: Five index kinds exist: Parquet footer zone maps, a sorted-Parquet sparse-map primary-key lookup, an HNSW vector graph, a Tantivy full-text index, and opt-in per-column bloom filters.

clauses.subject: declaration
clauses.statement: A sidecar is declared per table with a kind, a `column` and builder parameters; the vector kind takes model, dimension, metric, `m` and `ef_construction`.

clauses.subject: paths
clauses.statement: A vector sidecar sits at `indexes/vec-<col>-<model>/zone=<label>/` and a full-text sidecar at `indexes/fts-<col>/`, inside the snapshot directory it indexes.

clauses.subject: identity
clauses.statement: A sidecar's identity is `(column, builder, builder-version)`; two builders over one column coexist, the caller picks at query time, and `derived.sqlite` records each builder.

clauses.subject: rebuild
clauses.statement: Swapping a builder rebuilds the sidecar, leaves the Parquet untouched, and callers on the existing identity read through the cutover.

clauses.subject: not-in-file-set
clauses.statement: `indexes/` joins no table's file set; a snapshot reader lists only the parts its manifest names.

clauses.subject: dies-with-snapshot
clauses.statement: Collecting a snapshot collects its sidecars in the same step.

clauses.subject: candidate-ids
clauses.statement: A sidecar yields candidate identifiers, not rows; they re-join through the enforced relation before a top-K is final.

clauses.subject: vector-by-fold
clauses.statement: The fold builds a vector sidecar for a table carrying an embedding column under a single-column primary key.

clauses.subject: column-absent
clauses.statement: An index over a column the reconciled schema lacks raises `StoreIndexColumnAbsent` at manifest validation, before the pass that builds it.
clauses.why: because an index over a missing column builds empty and reads as no match

clauses.subject: clustering
clauses.statement: `cluster_by` sorts rows within a file lexicographically over its columns in declared order; zone maps then skip row groups with no manifest entry and no sidecar.

clauses.subject: partitioning
clauses.statement: Partitioning is off unless `partition_by` declares it.

clauses.subject: partition-type
clauses.statement: A `partition_by` column typed binary or vector raises `StorePartitionColumnType` at validation, before any Parquet.
clauses.why: because bytes name no directory that keeps two distinct values apart

clauses.subject: partition-warnings
clauses.statement: Planning warns, naming the column, where a partition specification projects more than 1000 partitions or a median partition below 16 MiB.

clauses.subject: tenant-outermost
clauses.statement: A multi-tenant table carries the tenant identifier as its outermost partition column.
clauses.why: because a dropped tenant predicate then reads nothing instead of every tenant

clauses.subject: tenant-verbatim
clauses.statement: A tenant value is written and compared byte for byte, with no trimming, case folding or Unicode normalization; a percent-escaped directory name is representation alone.

clauses.subject: two-clocks
clauses.statement: Transaction time is `_ingested_at`; valid time is a declared pair of the table's own columns. The engine infers no pair and stamps no second transaction clock.

clauses.subject: valid-time-declaration
clauses.statement: `[pipeline.tables.valid_time]` declares `from` and an optional `to`; a table declaring `from` alone treats each row as valid from that instant onward.

clauses.subject: valid-time-type
clauses.statement: A declared valid-time column whose type is not a timestamp raises `StoreValidTimeNotTimestamp` at declaration.

clauses.subject: instant-comparison
clauses.statement: Every bound compares instants as timestamps, never as strings; a date-only literal resolves, where it is built, to the start of the next day, exclusive.

clauses.subject: as-of
clauses.statement: `as_of` resolves each table to the newest reachable snapshot created at or before it, plus the committed runs at or before it that snapshot omits, inside the table's FROM-source.
clauses.why: because filtering the current files by ingest stamp returns different rows before and after a fold

clauses.subject: as-of-unretained
clauses.statement: An `as_of` earlier than the oldest retained snapshot of a table whose history has been collected raises `StoreAsOfUnretained`, naming the oldest answerable instant.

clauses.subject: valid-as-of
clauses.statement: `valid_as_of` wraps the same inner source with `from <= valid_as_of AND (to IS NULL OR to > valid_as_of)` over the declared pair.

clauses.subject: valid-time-undeclared
clauses.statement: A `valid_as_of` read against a table declaring no pair raises `StoreValidTimeUndeclared`, naming the table.

clauses.subject: pin-bound
clauses.statement: A read carrying `as_of` and a build pin resolves each table named by both by {{read.resolve-pin.earlier-bound-wins}}.

clauses.subject: unbounded-latest
clauses.statement: A read carrying neither bound resolves each table to its current snapshot plus the committed runs it omits.

clauses.subject: beneath-enforcement
clauses.statement: Both bounds apply beneath the row predicate, the column mask and the tenant filter, narrowing what enforcement admits and widening nothing.

clauses.subject: covering-versions
clauses.statement: Over an unkeyed table a valid-time bound returns every version whose interval covers the instant.

clauses.subject: echo
clauses.statement: A bounded read echoes `contextful.bounds` as `{as_of?, valid_as_of?, inclusive}`, each instant in RFC 3339 UTC with nine fractional digits and a `Z` suffix; an unbounded read omits it.

clauses.subject: key-binding
clauses.statement: At-rest encryption is per project, off unless `[encryption] key_source` names `env:<NAME>` or a key-management service.

clauses.subject: key-unbound
clauses.statement: A `key_source` naming a binding the process lacks raises `StoreEncryptionKeyUnbound` at startup, with no cleartext fallback.

clauses.subject: cipher
clauses.statement: Parquet, footers included, encrypts through Parquet modular encryption; every sidecar and ledger file encrypts with AES-256-GCM under a per-file data key wrapped by the project key.
clauses.why: because a cleartext vector graph admits nearest-neighbour search over the embedding space

clauses.subject: password-kdf
clauses.statement: A password-derived project key uses Argon2id with 64 MiB memory, 3 iterations and 4 lanes.

clauses.subject: transport-separate
clauses.statement: At-rest encryption covers files and TLS covers bucket transport; a cleartext endpoint carries no encrypted-at-rest claim.

clauses.subject: redacted-index
clauses.statement: An index declared over a column redacted at write time raises `StoreIndexOverRedactedColumn` at manifest validation.

clauses.subject: at-rest-scope
clauses.statement: A stolen bucket credential yields ciphertext Parquet and sidecars, no write-time-redacted content, and no key material.

clauses.subject: rotation
clauses.statement: Rotation writes forward: new files take the new key version, published files keep theirs until collected, and a key version retires once no retained file names it.

clauses.subject: prefix-escape
clauses.statement: A key resolving outside the prefix raises `SyncPrefixEscape`, naming the key and the prefix.

clauses.subject: prefix-unbound
clauses.statement: An unset variable named by `prefix_from` raises `SyncPrefixUnbound` at startup, with no bucket-root fallback.

clauses.subject: prefix-overspecified
clauses.statement: Declaring `prefix` and `prefix_from` together raises `SyncPrefixOverspecified`.

clauses.subject: in-flight
clauses.statement: A second push of one store on one machine raises `SyncPushInFlight`, naming the holder of the push guard.

clauses.subject: wire-format
clauses.statement: A push uploads each file it owns, or no node owns, whose digest the bucket lacks under `<prefix>/<project>/<path>` by a conditional put; machine catalogs, `config.toml`, locks, staging directories and table pointers stay local.

clauses.subject: schema-cas
clauses.statement: A table's `schema.json` commits by merging into the bucket's copy through the one-promotion lattice and replacing it on the ETag read; no copy overwrites another.
clauses.why: because two nodes landing different columns into one table both keep them

clauses.subject: manifest-commit
clauses.statement: A push commits when the bucket manifest, `<prefix>/manifest.json` listing each key's sha256, size and owner, replaces the copy it read under `If-Match` on that copy's ETag.

clauses.subject: digest-mismatch
clauses.statement: A downloaded object whose digest differs from its entry raises `SyncObjectDigestMismatch` and is discarded.

clauses.subject: convergence
clauses.statement: When a named key disappears mid-download, the pull re-fetches the manifest and retries the shortfall, up to 3 attempts.

clauses.subject: unconverged
clauses.statement: Exhausting those retries raises `SyncPullDidNotConverge`, naming the key that kept moving, and writes no pointer.

clauses.subject: pointer-last
clauses.statement: A pull writes a table's pointer only after every Parquet part of the snapshot it names is home, so no reader meets a pointer ahead of its data.

clauses.subject: tombstone-applied
clauses.statement: A pull deletes the local copy of each key a tombstone names and no entry lists.
clauses.why: because a deletion that never reaches a consumer resurrects once its tombstone ages out

clauses.subject: pointer-advance
clauses.statement: A pull advances a local pointer only to a bucket pointer carrying a higher fence, or the same fence and a later snapshot, and verifies every advancing table before writing any pointer.

clauses.subject: schema-merge
clauses.statement: A pulled `schema.json` differing from the local copy merges into it column by column through {{store.reconcile.incompatible}}'s lattice rather than replacing it.
clauses.why: because rows landed locally carry columns the bucket's copy may lack

clauses.subject: inconclusive
clauses.statement: An unsupported-method response, a forbidden response or a transport error raises `SyncProbeInconclusive` and counts as capability not demonstrated.

clauses.subject: unproven
clauses.statement: Declaring `cas` against a backend the probe did not demonstrate raises `SyncCoordinationUnproven` and stops the push.

clauses.subject: sentinel
clauses.statement: The probe creates a sentinel under `_contextful/cas-probe/` and demonstrates `cas` when a second create and a stale `If-Match` both fail and a current `If-Match` replaces it, deleting the sentinel after.

clauses.subject: network-volume
clauses.statement: A filesystem bucket whose mount type is not apfs, hfs, ext4, xfs, btrfs, zfs, tmpfs or overlay resolves `single-writer` without the sentinel, naming the mount type, and a declared `cas` there meets {{store.probe.unproven}}.
clauses.why: because the bucket's advisory lock is not a guarantee across the clients of a network share, and a sentinel run from one client cannot observe another

clauses.subject: tombstone-owner
clauses.statement: A tombstone whose owner differs from the owner of the entry it names raises `SyncTombstoneForeign`, and the merge keeps the entry.

clauses.subject: tombstone-ttl
clauses.statement: A tombstone leaves the manifest 30 d after its `deleted_at`.

clauses.subject: retries
clauses.statement: `[sync] push_retries` bounds the re-commit loop, defaulting to 5 attempts.

clauses.subject: exhausted
clauses.statement: Exhausting those retries raises `SyncManifestRebaseExhausted`, reports every uploaded object as already in the bucket, and asks for a re-run.

clauses.subject: cursor-recency
clauses.statement: Resolving a cursor by whichever copy was written last raises `SyncCursorConflict`; a cursor resolves through its commit.

clauses.subject: scoped-union
clauses.statement: A merge takes each local entry this writer owns or no node owns, and from the remote every other entry; a remote entry it owns and no longer holds leaves with a tombstone.

clauses.subject: ownership
clauses.statement: A key's owner is read off the key: a run directory's node segment, a request-ledger file's node, or a commit log's node directory. Every other key is unowned and propagates no deletion.

clauses.subject: ttl
clauses.statement: A lease is granted for 10 min.

clauses.subject: renewal
clauses.statement: A holder renews every 200 s by `If-Match` replace on the ETag it holds.

clauses.subject: clock-skew
clauses.statement: Bucket leasing assumes the clocks of two machines differ by 30 s or less, and every expiry judgment reads the judging machine's monotonic clock.
clauses.why: because correctness rests on the fence, and the skew bound only sets how early a holder stops committing

clauses.subject: held
clauses.statement: A run finding an unexpired lease raises `LeaseHeld`, naming the holder and the expiry, is skipped, and is attempted again at the next reconciliation tick.

clauses.subject: stale-fence
clauses.statement: A commit-log create, pointer replace or catalog `UPDATE` losing its condition to a higher fence raises `LeaseFenced`, and the run or snapshot it carried stays unreadable.

clauses.subject: not-held
clauses.statement: Releasing a lease another node holds raises `LeaseNotHeld` and leaves the object untouched.

clauses.subject: cursor-kind
clauses.statement: A cursor whose kind takes no lease reaching `cursors/` raises `LeaseCursorKindMismatch`.

clauses.subject: local-node
clauses.statement: A bucket lease attempted under the node id `local` raises `LeaseNodeIdLocal`, logging the variable that sets a node id; that machine keeps the machine lease.

clauses.subject: acquire
clauses.statement: Acquisition creates the lease object under `If-None-Match`, or replaces an expired or released one under `If-Match` on its ETag, the fence one past the object's.

clauses.subject: pointer-fence
clauses.statement: Taking a table's compaction lease raises the fence stored in its bucket pointer, so a publish carrying a lower fence loses its condition.

clauses.subject: network-volume
clauses.statement: Taking a compaction lease on a bucket {{store.probe.network-volume}} resolves to `single-writer` meets {{store.probe.unproven}} naming the mount type, and writes no lease object and no pointer fence.
clauses.why: because a conditional put holding on one machine only lets two machines each take the lease

clauses.subject: commit-log
clauses.statement: Under a machine lease, a run commits by creating the next `cursors/<pipeline-id>/<node-id>/<seq>.json`, and an acquisition creates one carrying its fence; a manifest marked `logged` is readable once that log records it.

clauses.subject: write-refused
clauses.statement: A write verb against a replica raises `ReplicaWriteRefused`, naming the canonical store.

clauses.subject: partial-parquet
clauses.statement: A replica holding a strict subset of a snapshot's Parquet raises `ReplicaPartialParquet` at refresh and leaves that snapshot unpublished.

clauses.subject: missing-index
clauses.statement: A query needing a sidecar or a partition the replica lacks raises `ReplicaMissingIndex`, naming the refresh that supplies it.

clauses.subject: sensitive-refused
clauses.statement: A refresh requesting a replicate-off table raises `ReplicaSensitiveTable`; the consumer reads through the proxying face.

clauses.subject: connection-views
clauses.statement: Ahead of a statement the engine opens a connection and issues one create-or-replace view per table the manifests name, each scanning {{store.reconcile.explicit-file-list}}. No view directory exists on disk.

clauses.subject: engine
clauses.statement: The executor is an embedded columnar SQL engine, linked into every profile that serves reads, reading Parquet natively in standard SQL. An external process reads the same files with the engine uninstalled.

clauses.subject: quiet-table
clauses.statement: A quiet table registers as {{store.declare.empty-run}}. A read of it returns an empty result, never a missing-relation fault.

clauses.subject: bare-name
clauses.statement: A bare table name in any read — a caller statement, a template body, a ranking arm, a file preview — resolves to the caller's registered relation, which carries the caller's restriction.

clauses.subject: tool-set
clauses.statement: The face exposes a closed tool set: `context.describe`, `context.query`, `context.execute_query` for templates, `context.files` and `context.file` over committed data files, and `corpus.retrieve` for ranked reads across a prefix.

clauses.subject: describe-payload
clauses.statement: `context.describe` returns row count, schema fingerprint, description, per-column hints, declared indexes, partition scheme, `limits.max_rows`, zone label, lexicon and example queries.

clauses.subject: advertised-is-enforced
clauses.statement: A table's published `limits` block lists a bound exactly when the engine applies it.
clauses.why: because a published number and a delivered guarantee cannot disagree when one derives from the other

clauses.subject: template-projection
clauses.statement: Every manifest template projects into a tool named by its identifier, whose declared positional parameters form a typed schema with every field required.

clauses.subject: file-listing
clauses.statement: `context.files` returns store-root-relative paths for the tables the caller reads, and a table outside that set contributes no path.

clauses.subject: file-preview-target
clauses.statement: `context.file` resolves a path to its `(table, run_id)` and reads it through that table's registered relation. A snapshot part, a traversal, an absolute path or a ledger file raises `FilePreviewNotATable`.

clauses.subject: ledger-relation
clauses.statement: Each table's per-run request ledger registers as the child relation `<table>__requests`, holding identifiers, connector, method, host, status and timing of mediated outbound calls.

clauses.subject: scoped-ledger
clauses.statement: The child relation registers on the owner read alone: a credential carrying no tenant scope, over a table carrying no row policy. Naming a closed ledger raises `LedgerNotTenantScoped`, stating what closed the relation.

clauses.subject: lexicon-surface
clauses.statement: The describe payload carries the store's numeric-identifier and badge vocabulary. Aliases, time-window phrases and distillation examples stay on the serving side.

clauses.subject: reserved-relation
clauses.statement: The engine's reserved table namespaces register like any other relation, with no privileged path underneath.

clauses.subject: single-read-only-statement
clauses.statement: Admitted text parses to exactly one read-only SELECT. Attach, copy, install, load, pragma, set, any schema change, any data modification and a piggybacked second statement raise `StatementNotReadOnly`.

clauses.subject: engine-own-parse
clauses.statement: The guard walks the syntax tree the engine itself serializes for the statement; read-only-ness is a property of that tree, not a keyword blocklist.
clauses.why: because guard and executor cannot disagree about what a text means when they share one parse

clauses.subject: relation-allowlist
clauses.statement: Every base relation names a view registered for this caller or a common table expression the statement declares. A bare file path is a base relation and falls under this rule.

clauses.subject: whole-tree-walk
clauses.statement: The walk covers the entire tree — select-list subqueries, union arms, pivot sources — and a common-table-expression name resolves only within the scope that declares it and the scopes beneath.

clauses.subject: unregistered-relation
clauses.statement: A base relation naming nothing this connection registered is refused by {{authority.refuse.ungranted-table}}, echoing what the statement asked for and no relation of another caller.

clauses.subject: table-function
clauses.statement: A table function anywhere in the tree, and a schema-qualified reach into a system catalog, raise `TableFunctionRefused`.

clauses.subject: statement-provenance
clauses.statement: Admission binds on who authored the text. Operator text — the local command line, template bodies, engine-composed reads — runs raw; capability-token caller text is gated. The raw surface is reachable from no network face.

clauses.subject: quoted-identifiers
clauses.statement: Every schema- or manifest-derived identifier is double-quoted where rendered, admitting any UTF-8 vendor field name as an identifier and never as an expression.

clauses.subject: template-declaration
clauses.statement: A template declares an identifier, one SQL statement, positional parameters written `name:type` over integer, float, string, timestamp and boolean, and an optional row ceiling.

clauses.subject: template-relation-shape
clauses.statement: Manifest validation and face startup refuse a template whose SQL names anything but the store's own tables as plain identifiers, or whose identifier collides with a built-in tool prefix, raising `TemplateNamesForeignRelation`.

clauses.subject: template-binding
clauses.statement: A missing, unknown or type-mismatched argument raises `TemplateArgumentRejected` ahead of execution, with no coercion. Placeholders cover exactly the declared parameters.

clauses.subject: startup-time-check
clauses.statement: Template checks are caller-independent and run once at startup; a request pays nothing for them.

clauses.subject: one-projection
clauses.statement: The command line's JSON output, the HTTP face and the tool protocol serialize one projection: `columns`, `rows`, `truncated`, and the optional restriction, resolved-build, provenance, retrieval and time-bound blocks.
clauses.why: because a guarantee landing on one transport and missing on another is worse than a guarantee on none

clauses.subject: row-ceiling
clauses.statement: A per-table row ceiling published as `limits.max_rows` bounds rows delivered, applied at execution with an over-fetch of 1 rows. It bounds no work performed.

clauses.subject: truncation-is-exact
clauses.statement: `truncated` is set exactly when the over-fetched probe row is present, never by comparing a returned count against a requested limit.

clauses.subject: cell-encoding
clauses.statement: SQL NULL is JSON `null` and nothing else is. Non-finite floats are `"NaN"`, `"inf"`, `"-inf"`; temporal values are ISO-8601 strings, intervals ISO-8601 durations; an enum is its label; any other container is its text form.

clauses.subject: bytes-and-vectors
clauses.statement: Binary is padded base64, and a fixed-size float array, a vector column included, is a JSON array holding each element as a float cell.

clauses.subject: wide-number-shape
clauses.statement: A column's JSON encoding follows its SQL type alone: integers of 32 bits or fewer, finite floats and decimals of 15 digits or fewer are numbers; wider integers and decimals are exact decimal strings.
clauses.why: because a wire type that varies with the values on one page breaks a typed client on the next

clauses.subject: type-is-the-cell
clauses.statement: No separate type list rides the envelope; a cell's JSON type is the declaration.

clauses.subject: zero-rows-is-success
clauses.statement: Fewer rows than the requested limit, zero included, is a success.

clauses.subject: match-count
clauses.statement: Match counts ride outside the internals opt-in, reporting how many rows the ranker scored as matching in the same call.

clauses.subject: coverage-is-a-count
clauses.statement: A claim that the corpus lacks coverage of a subject comes from a count over the table with no recency truncation, taken after the full-scan fallback, never from a ranked top score.
clauses.why: because min-max normalization pins the best row at 1.0 and IDF lifts one incidental rare-term mention

clauses.subject: internals-opt-in
clauses.statement: Executed SQL, engine name, applied limit, row count and elapsed milliseconds ride a separate object returned only under `internals: true`, on every read tool and the HTTP face.

clauses.subject: operator-metadata
clauses.statement: Operator-surface table metadata carries column count and backing file list; a row count is an ordinary count query, never a stored field.

clauses.subject: in-band-error
clauses.statement: On the tool protocol a refusal arrives in-band, as a protocol error object or a result flagged as an error under transport success.

clauses.subject: paths-stay-inside
clauses.statement: An ordinary read's result carries no store path. Provenance arrives as columns naming table, run, connector version, ingestion instant and authoring subject.

clauses.subject: ranked-call
clauses.statement: `corpus.retrieve({prefix, query, query_embedding?, kinds, limit, as_of})` returns the top rows across the item and artifact genres under one prefix, each with a snippet and full provenance. It composes the query surface and memory recall and stores nothing of its own.

clauses.subject: relevance-floor
clauses.statement: A row reaches a caller when its lexical score is null, at least the floor, or its vector score is positive. The floor is 2 tokens for queries of 3 tokens or more, else 1 tokens; a caller minimum overrides.

clauses.subject: content-tokens
clauses.statement: The query text is lowercased and split on non-alphanumeric characters. Stop tokens drop, non-ASCII runs of two or more characters stay, and survivors deduplicate in order.

clauses.subject: token-length-floor
clauses.statement: An ASCII run shorter than 2 chars leaves the content-token set.

clauses.subject: token-cap
clauses.statement: The content-token set holds at most 12 tokens. An empty set omits the relevance predicate.

clauses.subject: script-split-matching
clauses.statement: An all-lowercase-alphanumeric token matches on an ASCII word boundary with an optional plural suffix; a token with any non-ASCII character matches by containment.
clauses.why: because no ASCII word boundary occurs beside an ideograph

clauses.subject: plural-suffix-floor
clauses.statement: A token under 4 chars takes no optional plural suffix.

clauses.subject: text-free-table-scores-null
clauses.statement: A table with no snippet-worthy text column scores lexically null, never zero, and its rows enter by vector score alone.

clauses.subject: candidate-window
clauses.statement: The candidate window is 8 times the requested limit or 200 rows, whichever is larger. Candidates equal to the window report that the ranking saw a recency-ordered slice.

clauses.subject: reserved-columns-project-null
clauses.statement: Reserved projected columns — modality, language, prompt hash, kind — render null for a table lacking them, and its rows stay in the union.

clauses.subject: unsatisfiable-arm-drops
clauses.statement: `filter` binds caller-named columns. A table lacking a named column drops its arm, never emitting it unfiltered.
