clauses.subject: engine-resolved-date
clauses.statement: The engine resolves each table's publication column itself, outside the caller's filter.

clauses.subject: filter-budget
clauses.statement: A filter's membership list holds at most 256 entries, with its condition count and total byte size bounded alongside.

clauses.subject: filter-budget-refusal
clauses.statement: The budget is checked over the whole filter ahead of building any arm; an oversized or malformed condition raises `FilterBudgetExceeded` for the whole read.

clauses.subject: row-key-dedup
clauses.statement: A ranked read keeps one row per `(table, row key)`, newest ingestion first. The row key is the declared content-hash column, else null, never a digest over projected values.

clauses.subject: row-key-stays-internal
clauses.statement: The row key is absent from the outer projection.

clauses.subject: dedup-is-gated
clauses.statement: The deduplicating window function runs under the same condition as the relevance floor, and a browse-shaped read skips it.

clauses.subject: snippet
clauses.statement: A snippet concatenates up to three text columns: label-priority columns — title, summary, description, thesis and kin — first, then prose-worthy columns in schema order.

clauses.subject: identifiers-never-snippet
clauses.statement: Content hashes, URLs, identifiers and instant-valued columns never qualify for a snippet.

clauses.subject: sidecar-generates-candidates
clauses.statement: The vector sidecar arm adds its top results to the recency window, each re-joined by {{authority.compose.vector-arm}}. Per-row scores equal the exact path's.

clauses.subject: sidecar-oversampling
clauses.statement: One probe requests 4 times the limit or 64 rows, whichever is larger, and 4 times that where the request carries restriction context.

clauses.subject: sidecar-size-cap
clauses.statement: A sidecar holding more than 64 MiB of stored vectors stays unloaded and the arm takes the exact scan.

clauses.subject: sidecar-falls-back
clauses.statement: Any sidecar precondition failure — no snapshot, no matching sidecar, a multi-column or masked key, a dimension or manifest mismatch, an unreadable dump, mixed producers — falls back to the exact scan.

clauses.subject: gain-never-loss
clauses.statement: For one reader the accelerated arm returns a superset of the exact path's rows. Two readers with one query on one snapshot can recall different rows.

clauses.subject: three-legs
clauses.statement: Ranking runs exact cosine similarity over the candidate set, BM25 over a full-text index, and a weighted fusion of the two.

clauses.subject: fusion
clauses.statement: Fusion computes `w_vec · clamp(cosine, 0, 1) + w_lex · minmax(bm25)` with default weights 60 percent and 40 percent. A document absent from one leg scores zero there; ties break by identifier.

clauses.subject: lexical-leg-matches-only
clauses.statement: The BM25 leg ranks a disjunction of should-clauses; a document matching no term is absent. An empty query, candidate set or result yields an empty ranking that falls back to recency order.

clauses.subject: flat-window-full-credit
clauses.statement: A lexical window with no score spread awards every present document full credit.

clauses.subject: question-window-is-a-tier
clauses.statement: A question's timeframe projects a per-row in-window flag against the resolved publication column, and the flag leads the ordering. An out-of-window row sorts down and stays.

clauses.subject: window-anchor-tolerance
clauses.statement: A publication instant more than 24 h past the question's anchor sets the in-window flag false. A null or uncastable value sets it false too, and a basis field names which case applied.

clauses.subject: ordering-casts-first
clauses.statement: Ordering compares publication values as `TIMESTAMPTZ` instants, casting a text value before any comparison.
clauses.why: because a text comparison of two date spellings orders strings, not instants

clauses.subject: retrieval-block
clauses.statement: The `contextful.retrieval` block reports window, candidates_prefloor, candidates, matched, returned, in_window, deduped, padded, floor and since. Each row carries an integer score bounded by the content-token count, the in-window flag and the basis label.

clauses.subject: internal-score-stays-internal
clauses.statement: The lexical engine's own float score never crosses to a caller.
clauses.why: because a corpus-relative number drifts under a consumer's threshold as the corpus changes

clauses.subject: absent-block
clauses.statement: The retrieval block is omitted from every non-ranked statement and from a build with no ranker, and an absent block differs from one reporting zero matches.

clauses.subject: degradation-not-error
clauses.statement: Without the lexical backend linked, ranking substitutes a token fallback scoring each query token over the snippet, recency breaking ties. The result differs in order and still answers.

clauses.subject: fallback-counts-tokens
clauses.statement: Under the fallback every matching token contributes, ranking hyphenated, spaced and possessive phrasings equivalently.

clauses.subject: caller-embedding
clauses.statement: A supplied `query_embedding` adds per-row cosine fused with the lexical leg; omitting one leaves every projected column as the lexical-only path. Without the vector backend it scores only rows the recency window recalled.

clauses.subject: lexical-index-cache
clauses.statement: The full-text index is keyed on a fingerprint over the candidate documents and cached in a FIFO of 64 entries. A changed snapshot, table set or time bound changes the fingerprint.

clauses.subject: widened-window-statistics
clauses.statement: Lexical term statistics come from the widened candidate window, so an accelerated arm can order rows differently from the exact path.

clauses.subject: hot-local-parquet
clauses.statement: The retrieval container syncs the current snapshot set to local disk and memory-maps it; object storage stays out of the per-query path.

clauses.subject: cold-start
clauses.statement: A cold retrieval container meets {{topology.publish-hostname.container-readiness}}; a container holding no snapshot adds a whole-store pull before its first answer.

clauses.subject: result-key
clauses.statement: A cached result keys on the policy subject (token scope, inference zone, incognito state), the token id and revocation epoch, the resolved snapshot ids, the bounds echo, the pin map and the statement hash.
clauses.why: because a hit crossing a restriction, snapshot, bound or revocation serves rows the caller is not owed

clauses.subject: cache-is-opt-in
clauses.statement: The result cache is opt-in per table at a short time to live and off for a table tagged private.

clauses.subject: snapshot-invalidates
clauses.statement: A committed snapshot invalidates every entry keyed against the tables it folds. A statement in flight during a fold reads {{store.fold.non-blocking}}.

clauses.subject: keep-warm-is-per-deployment
clauses.statement: A deployment with active traffic keeps its retrieval container warm; one declining keep-warm takes a cold first read.

clauses.subject: pin-parameter
clauses.statement: `pin` maps a table name to a build identifier and resolves that table to the state the build published. An unnamed table resolves to the latest published state.

clauses.subject: unknown-build
clauses.statement: An unknown or collected build identifier raises `PinnedBuildUnavailable`, naming the oldest identifier still pinnable. A pin never widens to the latest state.
clauses.why: because a substituted build applied to every remaining query passes the consumer's cross-query comparison and stitches two states

clauses.subject: earlier-bound-wins
clauses.statement: A pin and the store's transaction-time bound are upper bounds on one clock; a table named by both resolves to the earlier.

clauses.subject: resolved-echo
clauses.statement: A response touching a published model carries `contextful.resolved`, mapping each such table to `{build_id, watermark}`, pinned or not.

clauses.subject: absent-watermark
clauses.statement: The watermark is null for a materialization carrying none, distinct from a watermark of zero.

clauses.subject: consumer-comparison
clauses.statement: A consumer compares resolved build identifiers across every query of one derivation and fails the derivation where two differ.

clauses.subject: default-embedder
clauses.statement: The embedding capability is a port whose default is deterministic and I/O-free: it hashes token term frequencies into an L2-normalized vector, needing no download, key or network call.

clauses.subject: default-embedder-reach
clauses.statement: The default is a lexical-vector baseline: a paraphrase is orthogonal under it and cross-lingual recall is undefined. Semantic reach comes from the learned in-process model or a caller-supplied query embedding.

clauses.subject: model-identifier
clauses.statement: Every stored vector lands in a {{store.reconcile.binary-and-vector}} column beside an `embedding_model` column naming the model that produced it; index identity and provenance resolve from the rows alone.

clauses.subject: build-identity
clauses.statement: The handshake reports the linked retrieval backends (`duckdb`, `fts`, `hnsw`), connector families (`m365`, `s3`, `wasm`) and faces (`http`, `eval`, `otlp`), composed from the same feature declarations the version output reads.

clauses.subject: required-face
clauses.statement: A client passing `require: [...]` is refused ahead of its first read with `RequiredFaceAbsent` for any name outside the reported set. An engine reporting no set satisfies no requirement.

clauses.subject: absent-read-backend
clauses.statement: Without the embedded SQL engine linked, both read tools raise `ReadBackendAbsent` rather than answering from a narrower path.

clauses.subject: canonical-column
clauses.statement: A table naming a shape and omitting one of its canonical columns raises `MemoryShapeColumnMissing` when the declaration loads.

clauses.subject: undeclared-relation
clauses.statement: A candidate edge whose `rel_type` falls outside the union lands in the dead-letter table and raises `MemoryUndeclaredRelation`; no row is written under the unknown type.

clauses.subject: extract-attempts
clauses.statement: A schema-invalid response is re-prompted with its validation feedback, at most 3 attempts per batch in total.

clauses.subject: dead-letter
clauses.statement: A batch exhausting {{read.synthesize.extract-attempts}} writes the response, template hash and drop reason to the dead-letter table, raises `MemoryExtractExhausted`, and leaves the cursor unadvanced.

clauses.subject: pass-cursor
clauses.statement: A pass reads the source's committed rows its cursor has not recorded, through the writing credential's own session, in batches under {{read.synthesize.prompt-bound}}, recording each batch once its claims commit.

clauses.subject: prompt-bound
clauses.statement: A batch packs fenced rows up to 32 KiB; a fenced row over that bound travels in a batch of its own.
clauses.why: because one oversized row neither stalls the pass nor drags its neighbours past the bound

clauses.subject: row-cap
clauses.statement: A row is fenced at 16384 chars under {{connector.infer.fenced-value-hygiene}}; a truncated row still reaches the model, its batch commits and advances the cursor, and the pass report counts it in `truncated`.
clauses.why: because a silent cut hides that a conclusion rests on a partial row

clauses.subject: attribution
clauses.statement: Every landed claim carries `grant_id`, the chain-final revocation identifier of the credential that wrote it, `agent`, that credential's agent member, and `_authored_by`, its on-behalf-of principal.
clauses.why: because a reader weighs a conclusion by which grant could have produced it

clauses.subject: tier
clauses.statement: `tier` is stamped from the write path and grounding, never the payload: a synthesis pass stamps `derived`, a direct write `curated`, a fetched result `researched`, and mixed grounding takes the lowest.

clauses.subject: supersede
clauses.statement: A claim of equal or higher tier retires a live prior of its subject, predicate and scope when both are open-ended or share a valid-from instant: the prior's `valid_to` becomes the claim's `valid_from`, and `superseded_by` names it.

clauses.subject: direct-write
clauses.statement: The direct write accepts claims alone. Naming `memory_episodes`, `memory_entities`, `memory_edges` or `memory_preferences` raises `MemoryDirectWriteShapeRefused`; an entity row enters through the entity upsert.

clauses.subject: evidence-unresolved
clauses.statement: An unreadable or masked source row, an unknown table, a reference into another memory row, or malformed lineage suppresses the claim and raises `MemoryEvidenceUnresolved`.

clauses.subject: evidence-references
clauses.statement: A claim naming more than 256 entries of evidence is suppressed unresolved, raising `MemoryEvidenceOverflow`.

clauses.subject: ranked-arm
clauses.statement: A `corpus.retrieve` arm over a `memory_facts` table serves only live claims — no `superseded_by`, and a `valid_to` null or past the read's anchor — whose evidence passes the gate.

clauses.subject: suppression-count
clauses.statement: A suppressed claim is absent from the rows; the `contextful.recall` block counts suppressions per error identifier and names no claim.
clauses.why: because a count discloses that a conclusion was withheld, never what it concluded

clauses.subject: ambiguous-mention
clauses.statement: A mention matching two canonical identities with no deterministic key separating them is recorded as an ambiguous skip, raises `MemoryEntityAmbiguous`, and dead-letters its candidate claim.

clauses.subject: edge-endpoint
clauses.statement: A candidate edge whose source or target resolves to no identity is dead-lettered, raising `MemoryEdgeEndpointUnresolved`.

clauses.subject: registration
clauses.statement: A registration names exactly one form (relative horizon, absolute deadline, open watch) and one source (`metric`, `adjudicator`, `manual`), with a comparator exactly when the source is `metric`; otherwise it raises `OutcomeRegistrationInvalid`.

clauses.subject: source-mismatch
clauses.statement: An observation carrying a verdict whose resolution source is absent or differs from the registration's raises `OutcomeSourceMismatch`.

clauses.subject: settling-citation
clauses.statement: An `adjudicator` or `manual` verdict without an `http` or `https` settling citation raises `OutcomeCitationMissing`; the citation rides the label view.

clauses.subject: grace-window
clauses.statement: The label join keeps an observation from the prediction instant through the deadline plus an inclusive grace of 86400 s.

clauses.subject: step-output
clauses.statement: A journaled step's value is recorded exactly once and its effect runs at least once: a crash between effect and write re-enters the effect, and every later call under the key returns the recorded value.
clauses.why: because exactly-once effects need the vendor's cooperation, and the recorded value is the one fact a replay can rely on

clauses.subject: entry-key
clauses.statement: An entry is keyed by `(execution_id, step_label, input_hash)`. The first caller claims the key with a pending row before entering the effect; a racing caller waits for the recorded value instead of computing.
clauses.why: because two racers computing one key issue two billed calls and spend two meter permits

clauses.subject: claim-takeover
clauses.statement: A pending claim whose run owner lease has expired, {{run.record.owner-lease}}, is taken over by the next caller under that key.

clauses.subject: idempotency-key
clauses.statement: Every outbound request a step makes carries an idempotency key derived from its entry key, identical on every re-entry of that effect.
clauses.why: because a vendor honoring the key turns an at-least-once effect into one billed call

clauses.subject: inline-cutoff
clauses.statement: A value of 1 MiB or smaller is stored inline in its row as bytes; a larger value lands in a content-addressed blob named by its sha256, and the row holds the reference.

clauses.subject: blob-write
clauses.statement: Concurrent writers of one blob hash converge on one stored value and none errors on another's write; no partial write survives beside it.

clauses.subject: missing-blob
clauses.statement: A row whose blob reference resolves to no stored blob raises `BlobMissing` carrying the reference, never an empty value in place of the recorded one.

clauses.subject: collection
clauses.statement: Retiring an execution owner deletes its journal rows in the retiring transaction.
clauses.why: because recorded work is needed only while a replay can reach it, and an uncollected journal grows with total ingest

clauses.subject: blob-sweep
clauses.statement: A mark-and-sweep pass every 24 h deletes each blob that no journal row or pending awakeable references and that is older than 1 h.
clauses.why: because the grace window covers a blob written ahead of the row that names it

clauses.subject: effect-boundary
clauses.statement: A body replays faithfully when every observable side effect passes through a recorded step, a cursor commit or an awakeable; the work between them is pure.

clauses.subject: recorded-batch
clauses.statement: A journaled pull records the batch as the source handed it over, after {{run.guard-secrets.placement}} and ahead of the land path.

clauses.subject: replay-lands
clauses.statement: A journal hit hands the recorded batch to the land path, so a resumed run lands bytes identical to an uninterrupted one, batch ordinal included.

clauses.subject: ledger-settles-first
clauses.statement: The outbound request ledger settles durably before the entry recording its batch commits.

clauses.subject: redacting-source
clauses.statement: A pipeline declaring write-path redaction over a source that journals its pulls raises `JournalRedactionConflict` at manifest validation and again at run open, before the first pull.

clauses.subject: opt-out
clauses.statement: Pull journaling defaults on. A source whose pre-pull cursor cannot name the content it reads opts out through one constant, pinned against each source's declaration by a test. An empty pull is never journaled.

clauses.subject: escape-hatch
clauses.statement: Two escape hatches exist and no third: `journal.unsafe(label, effect)` for an idempotent read, and a source declaring that it journals no pull. Each carries its idempotency argument at a greppable call site.

clauses.subject: substrate-port
clauses.statement: The run-path substrate is one interface: open or resume an execution under a scope for a content-hashed plan reference, record a step output, commit a cursor, suspend on an awakeable with a timeout, attach a retry schedule, describe capabilities.

clauses.subject: storage-ports
clauses.statement: Journal rows, blobs and awakeables persist through a journal store, a blob store and an awakeable store; every `run.journal` and `run.suspend` clause holds for each adapter, the file tree included.

clauses.subject: sqlite-stores
clauses.statement: `contextful-sqlite` serves the journal, blob and awakeable stores from one SQLite file in write-ahead-log mode over one connection, a blob as a row keyed by its sha256; an awakeable update commits with the journal writes inside it.
clauses.why: because a resolution recording its payload through a second connection waits on the write lock its own update holds

clauses.subject: plan-pin
clauses.statement: A run resolves the plan reference it started against for its whole life.

clauses.subject: unwired-capability
clauses.statement: Reaching for a capability the running profile does not wire raises `CapabilityUnwired` at the first reach, before any half-finished work.

clauses.subject: machine-state
clauses.statement: Journal rows, execution owners and awakeables are machine-local state that a catalog rebuild leaves untouched and the file tree never reconstructs.

clauses.subject: cursor-kind
clauses.statement: A cursor declares `monotonic` for a timestamp, autoincrement or watermark, `opaque-token` for a vendor continuation token, or `snapshot-id` for a log sequence number or version id. An undeclared kind resolves to `opaque-token`.

clauses.subject: concurrency-by-kind
clauses.statement: A `monotonic` position is concurrent-safe and commits the highest value observed. An `opaque-token` or `snapshot-id` position moves only under a single-writer lease. Last-write-wins governs no cursor.
clauses.why: because two writers resolving one continuation token by recency skip or duplicate records with no count showing it

clauses.subject: engine-owned
clauses.statement: A connector moves its position only by committing through the engine; that commit is a recorded step and replays as a resolved read.

clauses.subject: commit-with-rows
clauses.statement: A table's new position rides the run commit marker, {{store.lay-out.run-manifest}}, that publishes the rows behind it; the catalog cursor is a cache of the newest committed marker.
clauses.why: because rows and position committed in two stores leave a crash window that re-lands a batch

clauses.subject: cursor-bytes
clauses.statement: A position is opaque bytes the connector owns, and its kind is a manifest fact the engine reads. Each table carries its own position.

clauses.subject: inclusive-boundary
clauses.statement: A polled load admits a row whose clock value is at or after the stored position, re-landing the boundary instant's rows on every poll.
clauses.why: because a clock coarser than the row grain otherwise drops a sibling sharing the boundary value, permanently and invisibly

clauses.subject: declared-key-required
clauses.statement: The boundary re-land is idempotent on a table declaring a key; on a keyless table the repeats accumulate in its union view.

clauses.subject: watermark-shape
clauses.statement: A watermark position serializes as `{"field": "<name>", "at": <value>}`, naming the column it was measured against.

clauses.subject: field-rename
clauses.statement: Opening a position whose stored field differs from the declared `incremental` field raises `CursorFieldMismatch` before any request leaves the host.

clauses.subject: frontier
clauses.statement: The frontier counts every fetched row, landed or not. A committed position moves forward or holds; an empty or older window never rewinds it.

clauses.subject: unorderable-position
clauses.statement: A row with no orderable value in the clock field, or a stream switching between text and numeric positions mid-pass, raises `CursorPositionUnorderable`, terminal for the pull.

clauses.subject: turning-incremental-on
clauses.statement: Enabling `incremental` on a pipeline that holds a position starts from none, re-landing the source's current window once.

clauses.subject: skip-unchanged
clauses.statement: A snapshot-shaped source with `skip_unchanged = true` records its input's raw-byte digest as `{ sha256, rows }`; a matching digest returns zero batches, holds the position and closes a zero-row success. Undeclared, it is false.

clauses.subject: zero-row-commit
clauses.statement: A commit landing zero rows adds and replaces nothing, so a replacing table keeps its last non-empty state across a skip or an empty pull.

clauses.subject: awakeable
clauses.statement: An awakeable suspends a run durably: the engine mints an opaque single-use token and persists a `pending` row beside the journal; an external party resumes by posting the token back.

clauses.subject: resume-is-a-step-output
clauses.statement: A resume payload is recorded as the awaited step's output under key `sha256("awakeable:" + token)`, so a run that resumes and then crashes reads it back without suspending again.

clauses.subject: deadline
clauses.statement: A deadline is the creation instant plus a time-to-live, both caller-supplied RFC3339 Zulu strings; the core reads no wall clock.

clauses.subject: timeout-is-sticky
clauses.statement: Expiry is evaluated against an injected instant; a suspension past its deadline becomes `timed_out` and stays so under any later instant.

clauses.subject: idempotent-resolution
clauses.statement: Resolving a token again with the identical payload returns the recorded value.

clauses.subject: conflicting-resolution
clauses.statement: A second resolution with a different payload raises `AwakeableAlreadyResolved` and leaves the recorded value untouched.

clauses.subject: expired-token
clauses.statement: Resolving a token past its deadline raises `AwakeableTimedOut`.

clauses.subject: unknown-token
clauses.statement: A token with no row raises `AwakeableUnknown` and allocates no state.

clauses.subject: resume-route
clauses.statement: `POST /awake/:token` answers `200` with the recorded payload, `404` for {{run.suspend.unknown-token}}, `409` for {{run.suspend.conflicting-resolution}} and `410` for {{run.suspend.expired-token}}. `GET /awake/:token` reports state without resuming. Both authenticate before touching the registry.

clauses.subject: payload-offload
clauses.statement: A payload above {{run.journal.inline-cutoff}} lands in the journal's blob store, and the pending row references it.

clauses.subject: survives-restart
clauses.statement: The awakeable registry persists beside the journal; a restart drops no pending callback.

clauses.subject: failure-taxonomy
clauses.statement: One tagged failure type crosses every port: `Transient`, `Permanent`, `SchemaIncompatible`, `AuthExpired`, `RateLimited`, `Config`, `Storage`, `UnknownConnector`, `SecretNotFound` and `Canceled`. A caller branches on the tag, never on a message.

clauses.subject: schedule
clauses.statement: A schedule attaches to a step and carries a fixed or exponential backoff with base and factor, a total attempt count including the first, a per-delay clamp, a jitter ceiling and `retry_on`.

clauses.subject: default-policy
clauses.statement: The default schedule is exponential from a 100 ms base with factor 2, to 5 attempts in total, each delay clamped at 30 s, plus seeded jitter below 250 ms.
clauses.why: because zero jitter synchronizes every run that hit one shared throttle

clauses.subject: single-attempt
clauses.statement: A schedule of 1 attempts is the no-retry schedule.

clauses.subject: retryable-classes
clauses.statement: `Transient` and `RateLimited` retry; every other tag stands as the step's answer whatever budget remains. `retry_on` narrows that pair.

clauses.subject: unretryable-tag
clauses.statement: A `retry_on` naming any tag outside `Transient` and `RateLimited` raises `RunRetryTagUnretryable` at plan compile.

clauses.subject: step-failed
clauses.statement: A non-retryable failure, or a step exhausting its schedule, raises `StepFailed` carrying the step label and the underlying tag.

clauses.subject: deterministic-verdict
clauses.statement: A refusal whose check is pure over static input is terminal and consumes no attempt budget.

clauses.subject: retry-after
clauses.statement: A server-supplied `Retry-After` supersedes the computed delay up to 300 s; a longer one closes the step as `RateLimited` and the run is rescheduled instead of sleeping.
clauses.why: because an unclamped upstream delay holds a run slot for as long as the vendor asks

clauses.subject: one-layer
clauses.statement: The step's schedule is the only retry layer: an adapter, a credential mint and a meter acquire inside a step return their failure to it.
clauses.why: because nested retry layers multiply attempts and amplify a vendor outage

clauses.subject: decision-is-pure
clauses.statement: The retry decision is a pure function of the one-based attempt that just closed and the classified failure, jitter derived from an injected seed. The runner owns the sleep and the attempt counter.

clauses.subject: partial-failure
clauses.statement: A run that landed some batches and then failed closes `partial_failure`, naming how many landed; the journal holds the resume point.

clauses.subject: pressure-is-local
clauses.statement: Rate-limit pressure against one source paces only that source's runs.

clauses.subject: bound-hit-is-transient
clauses.statement: A connector striking one of its declared resource bounds answers `Transient`, and every bound decision is recorded on the run record.

clauses.subject: execution-owner
clauses.statement: One durable execution owner exists per scope; a table or chunk owner holds the connector identity with its component world, the pipeline `content_hash` and the input hash.

clauses.subject: host-scope
clauses.statement: The catalog keys every owner on its scope — live table, backfill chunk or host-declared id — a table owner keeping its stored key byte for byte, and a host owner pinning the plan reference and identities the host supplies.

clauses.subject: execution-id-keys-the-journal
clauses.statement: Recorded work keys on the execution id; a catalog run id is the provenance of one attempt, so attempts under one owner resolve the same recorded values.

clauses.subject: retirement
clauses.statement: Retiring an owner and caching its committed position share one catalog transaction; a later fire receives a fresh execution id even at a byte-identical position. A completed backfill chunk retires the same way.

clauses.subject: marker-reconciles
clauses.statement: At run open, a commit marker newer than the catalog's cached position retires the pending owner that produced it before any replay.
clauses.why: because a crash between marker and catalog otherwise replays a recorded pull into rows already committed

clauses.subject: pinned-plan-changed
clauses.statement: While an owner is pending, a changed pin — connector identity, component world, pipeline `content_hash`, or a host's plan reference or identities — raises `ExecutionPinMismatch` before replay, terminal and non-retryable, naming the scope and both pin sets.
scenarios: WHEN a host scope's pending owner pins plan reference `plan-a` and an open asks for `plan-b`, THEN the open refuses with `ExecutionPinMismatch` and its run row closes `failed`.

clauses.subject: pin-recovery
clauses.statement: Restoring the recorded build and resuming to completion clears a pending owner; an explicit chunk rewind retires the owners its window covers.

clauses.subject: scope-independence
clauses.statement: A finishing table releases nothing another table's unfinished execution holds, and a seeding scope carries its own source identity.

clauses.subject: unclosed-execution
clauses.statement: An execution handle dropped without close records no status; its owner stays pending, and the next open under its scope resumes it once {{run.record.owner-lease}} lapses.
scenarios: WHEN a host execution records two steps and its process dies mid-third, THEN the next open under its scope after the lease lapses replays both steps without running their effects.

clauses.subject: live-owner
clauses.statement: An open under a host scope whose pending owner has an attempt on an unexpired {{run.record.owner-lease}} fails `Transient` naming that attempt, and its run row closes `failed` without joining the owner.
clauses.why: because two live handles on one owner share its journal, and either one retiring it strands the other
scenarios: WHEN attempt `job-a` holds host scope `index-42` open and `job-b` opens under it, THEN `job-b` fails `Transient` naming `job-a`, and `job-a` alone holds the owner.

clauses.subject: pin-release
clauses.statement: `success`, and a failure that wrote no batch, release the owner; every other status holds it.

clauses.subject: admission-pin
clauses.statement: A run pins its connector identity at admission and a replay resolves the artifact from that pin; a connector rebuilt later reaches no in-flight or replayed run.

clauses.subject: backpressure
clauses.statement: A source yields a stream of batches the runner pulls; the run path holds no unbounded buffer between source and destination.

clauses.subject: one-commit-per-run
clauses.statement: One run produces one atomic commit per table; a crash mid-run leaves parts under that run's own directory, and a resumption continues from the last recorded step.

clauses.subject: catalog-channel
clauses.statement: A stop is written onto the run row as a requested-at instant, a scope and an optional reason; the catalog is the only channel.

clauses.subject: two-grains
clauses.statement: A `run`-scoped stop halts one run and the fire continues; a `pipeline`-scoped stop halts every in-flight run of the pipeline and every table or chunk the fire had left. An unrecognized stored scope reads as `run`.

clauses.subject: host-grain
clauses.statement: A `pipeline`-scoped stop on a host execution's run halts every in-flight run under the same host-declared scope and no run of another scope.

clauses.subject: one-token
clauses.statement: Each run holds one cancellation token that every await selects on: the pull, a retry sleep, an awakeable wait, a meter acquire and a subprocess wait.
clauses.why: because a stop observed only at the pull leaves sleeps and child processes running after the record reads canceled

clauses.subject: poll-interval
clauses.statement: The token is fed by one catalog read before the run's first await and then one every 500 ms, the cancellation arm evaluated ahead of the work arm.

clauses.subject: engine-keeper
clauses.statement: One keeper per engine renews every registered execution's owner lease and feeds its token, sleeping until the earliest deadline; opening an execution registers it, and close or drop deregisters it.

clauses.subject: land-path-uncut
clauses.statement: The land path carries no stop check; a run whose bytes are home finishes landing and records the stop it did not fulfill.

clauses.subject: abandoned-work
clauses.statement: Abandoned work surfaces as the `Canceled` tag through the ordinary failure path, which settles the request ledger, closes the record and leaves the position alone.

clauses.subject: child-reaped
clauses.statement: A stop signals a running subprocess chain's process group, and the record is written `canceled` only after the group is reaped.
clauses.why: because a record reading canceled while a child still runs misstates what the machine is doing

clauses.subject: storage-blip
clauses.statement: A failed poll read warns and keeps polling.

clauses.subject: not-in-flight
clauses.statement: Only a `pending`, `running` or `waiting` row accepts a mark; a stop matching none raises `CancelTargetNotInFlight`, answering `409` over HTTP and exiting non-zero at the terminal.

clauses.subject: re-mark
clauses.statement: Marking an already-marked row overwrites it with the newer request.

clauses.subject: distinct-terminal-status
clauses.statement: `canceled` is a terminal status apart from `failed`, and upstream health observations skip it.

clauses.subject: resumable-remains
clauses.statement: A stopped run's recorded pull keeps its owner and replays next attempt; a stopped pull that recorded nothing releases it. A stopped chunk returns to pending, its attempt count unchanged. A stop advances no position.

clauses.subject: authority-from-the-record
clauses.statement: A stop authorizes against the pipeline read off the run record, never off the request.

clauses.subject: reserved-table
clauses.statement: The durable run record is a reserved store table holding two append-only rows per run, one at plan and one at commit; the latest row per run and phase wins. The local catalog is a cache in front of it.

clauses.subject: columns
clauses.statement: A run row carries run id, pipeline id, site id, status, owner, start and end instants, row and byte counts, error kind and message, connector id, version and hash, trace id and phase.

clauses.subject: status-set
clauses.statement: A run status is `pending`, `running`, `waiting`, `success`, `partial_failure`, `failed` or `canceled`, spelled identically on the record and the wire snapshot; every surface classifying a run covers all seven.
clauses.why: because two vocabularies for one lifecycle leave a suspended or partly failed run without a reading

clauses.subject: row-at-open
clauses.statement: A row is written at run open, before the first pull, so a zero-row `success`, a `failed` row carrying its error kind, and no row at all read apart.

clauses.subject: time-travel
clauses.statement: Run history inherits the store's transaction-time bound, so one as-of selector rewinds it with every other table.

clauses.subject: owner-lease
clauses.statement: A `running` or `waiting` row carries an owner of process id, boot id and a lease expiry, renewed every 10 s with a 30 s time-to-live.
clauses.why: because a second process sharing the catalog needs a liveness signal to tell a live run from an orphan

clauses.subject: orphan-reap
clauses.statement: Startup marks `partial_failure` only a non-terminal row whose owner lease has expired; a row held by a live process is left alone.

clauses.subject: writing-site
clauses.statement: The writing site is an engine-injected provenance column beside the ingestion stamp and run id; a row written without one reads null and renders unattributed.

clauses.subject: site-id-length
clauses.statement: A site id matches letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen, from 1 chars to 64 chars.
clauses.why: because it is interpolated into run directories and request-ledger filenames

clauses.subject: site-id-unresolved
clauses.statement: A site id comes from the manifest or a named environment variable; an unset variable, or both sources declared, raises `SiteIdUnresolved` at startup.

clauses.subject: history-window
clauses.statement: History is read through a window, an inclusive start-instant lower bound plus a row ceiling, both applied in the storage adapter's `WHERE` clause, newest first.

clauses.subject: describe-window
clauses.statement: The describe surface answers with 5 rows by default and clamps a caller's ceiling at 500 rows.

clauses.subject: bound-spelling
clauses.statement: A window lower bound is `YYYY-MM-DD` or a UTC RFC3339 instant ending `Z`; any other spelling raises `HistoryBoundSpelling` at every caller-facing surface.
clauses.why: because a bound read under a guessed zone silently moves the window

clauses.subject: truncation-flag
clauses.statement: A history response echoes its window and flags truncation when the pipeline recorded more runs inside it than the ceiling returned.

clauses.subject: empty-window
clauses.statement: An empty window answers `[]` and raises nothing.

clauses.subject: history-export
clauses.statement: History leaves the machine as a process listing and an NDJSON export over one run projection; the export's first line carries store, window, count and truncation flag, then one run per line. It resolves no bucket.

clauses.subject: export-ceiling
clauses.statement: The export answers with 500 rows by default and clamps at 5000 rows, each pipeline's window taking the full ceiling before the merged result is clipped once.

clauses.subject: error-cap
clauses.statement: A recorded error is masked over credential-shaped spans and capped at 2 KiB with an ellipsis marker, on the one projection every surface serves.

clauses.subject: failure-publishes
clauses.statement: The bucket push runs on the failure arm as on the success arm, for every failure past run open.

clauses.subject: per-table-accounting
clauses.statement: A table failing inside a multi-table fire leaves one row with its error kind, a step-failure and a run-failure event, and a position where the next run resumes, under either `on_table_error` setting.

clauses.subject: counts-at-destination
clauses.statement: Row and byte counts are measured at the destination, not at the source.

clauses.subject: best-effort
clauses.statement: Live run state is a best-effort projection of events the runner emits after durable state changes; execution never reads it.

clauses.subject: wire-snapshot
clauses.statement: The wire snapshot carries run id, workflow id, a status from {{run.record.status-set}}, an ordered step list, an application metadata map, optional start and end instants, an optional tagged error and a version. Every deploy target emits it identically.

clauses.subject: step-view
clauses.statement: A step view carries its label, a status of `pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed` or `retrying`, its attempt count, optional instants, an optional output reference with byte count, and an optional tagged failure.

clauses.subject: stopped-step
clauses.statement: A stopped run reports its executing step `failed` with the `Canceled` tag and leaves the run-level error unset.

clauses.subject: emission-never-blocks
clauses.statement: Progress emission is no journal step: events reach an in-process observer over a bounded channel that drops when full and never blocks the runner.

clauses.subject: terminal-slot
clauses.statement: A terminal transition bypasses the lossy channel through a per-run slot that is never dropped; a projection reading non-terminal behind a terminal run record reconciles from the record.
clauses.why: because a dropped terminal event otherwise leaves a finished run reading running forever

clauses.subject: coalescing
clauses.statement: Snapshot broadcasts coalesce to at most one per 100 ms, keeping only the latest; a terminal transition flushes immediately. The clock is injected.

clauses.subject: metadata-too-large
clauses.statement: A metadata write whose serialized size exceeds 16384 B raises `RunMetadataTooLarge` naming size and bound, and the snapshot stands unchanged.
clauses.why: because a silently clipped map reads as the complete metadata

clauses.subject: version
clauses.statement: The snapshot version is `(epoch, counter)`, the epoch being the hub's start instant, compared lexicographically; a client discards any delta at or below the highest version it holds.
clauses.why: because a bare counter restarts at zero with the process and freezes every client's view

clauses.subject: reducer-is-total
clauses.statement: The reducer is total: nothing overwrites a terminal step or run status, a new step label appends, an existing one merges field-wise, and a stale delta is a no-op.

clauses.subject: outputs-by-reference
clauses.statement: A step output appears as a post-redaction reference and a byte count, never inline; fetching the payload is a separately authorized request.

clauses.subject: connect
clauses.statement: A subscriber receives the folded snapshot and its update receiver under one lock, missing and duplicating no update.

clauses.subject: broadcast-ring
clauses.statement: The per-run broadcast holds 256 entries; a subscriber that overruns it resynchronizes to the latest snapshot.

clauses.subject: unauthenticated-upgrade
clauses.statement: The run-stream socket authenticates on the HTTP request before the upgrade; a missing or invalid credential raises `RunStreamUnauthorized` with `401`, and an unseen run answers `404`.

clauses.subject: read-only-socket
clauses.statement: A subscription is read-only; a stop travels as an authenticated route.

clauses.subject: restart-discards
clauses.statement: A restart discards in-memory snapshots; a subscriber recovers history from the durable record.

clauses.subject: delegated-progress
clauses.statement: A heavy step delegated to another host reports progress by posting to the awakeable callback route, and the orchestrating run folds it into its own snapshot.

clauses.subject: pipeline-spec
clauses.statement: A specification carries `id`, `source` and `tables`, plus the optional `destination`, `schedule`, `incremental`, `transforms`, `redaction`, `normalize`, `backfill`, `seed`, `queries` and `on_table_error`.

clauses.subject: serialization
clauses.statement: TOML and JSON deserialize into one `PipelineSpec`; the JSON Schema derived from it is the contract, and `contextful schema export` writes it to `.contextful/schema/pipeline.json`.

clauses.subject: source-block
clauses.statement: A `source` is a connector name beside a free-form JSON config object; a `destination` carries the same two fields and defaults to the store.

clauses.subject: manifest-file
clauses.statement: Startup reads `contextful.toml` for project config and inline `[[pipeline]]` blocks, then `pipelines/*.toml` and `pipelines/*.json`; specifications are collected by `id`.

clauses.subject: duplicate-id
clauses.statement: One `id` declared twice raises `PipelineDuplicateId`, naming each file and the line its declaration starts on.
clauses.why: because a silent pick between two declarations hides which one runs

clauses.subject: spec-invalid
clauses.statement: A manifest file the canonical type cannot deserialize raises `PipelineSpecInvalid`, naming the file, the key path and the value found.
clauses.why: because a partly read manifest runs a pipeline its author did not write

clauses.subject: content-hash
clauses.statement: `content_hash` is the sha256 of the specification's RFC 8785 canonical JSON with every optional field at its default elided, so an explicit default hashes as its absence.
clauses.why: because a replay pin that moves on a no-op edit strands pending work

clauses.subject: table-name
clauses.statement: A destination table is named `<pipeline id>_<table name>`, each non-alphanumeric character folded to `_` and each ASCII uppercase letter lowered.

clauses.subject: table-name-collision
clauses.statement: Two tables whose destination names fold to one spelling, within one pipeline or across pipelines, raise `PipelineTableNameCollision` at validation, naming both declarations.
clauses.why: because two tables folding to one name land in one store table and interleave their rows

clauses.subject: unbound-table-name
clauses.statement: A job target or model reference naming a destination table in a spelling the fold does not produce raises `PipelineUnboundTableName`, printing the expected spelling.

clauses.subject: table-entry
clauses.statement: A `tables` entry is a bare name or an object carrying that table's configuration; the two forms mix in one array.

clauses.subject: order-by-default
clauses.statement: `order_by` defaults to the injected ingest stamp and is inert on a keyless table; key semantics are {{store.declare.unkeyed-union}}.

clauses.subject: write-mode
clauses.statement: `write_mode` is `append`, the default, or `replace`. Under `append` a run adds rows and no key retires; under `replace` the landing run is the table's whole current state.

clauses.subject: replace-unsupported
clauses.statement: `replace` beside a `monotonic` or `opaque-token` cursor, a backfill chunk plan or a seed ceiling raises `PipelineReplaceUnsupported`, naming the table.

clauses.subject: config-key
clauses.statement: A source config key outside the set that source enumerates raises `PipelineUnknownConfigKey` before any I/O, naming the key and the accepted keys; request headers and the forwarded guest table are exempt.

clauses.subject: lifecycle-verbs
clauses.statement: `plan` diffs desired state against the store with no side effect, `--json` emitting a structured diff; `apply` converges every pipeline or one; `run` fires one pipeline once; `serve` reconciles continuously.

clauses.subject: apply-fires-nothing
clauses.statement: Applying a manifest fires nothing of itself; a second `apply` over unchanged sources is a no-op modulo elapsed schedules.

clauses.subject: table-error
clauses.statement: `on_table_error` is abort, the default, halting the fire at the first failing table, or continue, landing every other table and reporting the failed run ids through {{run.declare.table-error-exit}}.

clauses.subject: table-error-exit
clauses.statement: Under continue, `run` exits non-zero naming the failed runs, `apply` prints a partial line, and a scheduled fire appends its failure count to its log line.

clauses.subject: chunked-load
clauses.statement: `on_table_error` governs the single-pass live pull alone; a seed or backfill chunk plan halts the fire on failure under either setting.

clauses.subject: incremental-field
clauses.statement: `incremental = "<field>"` names the stream clock on the pipeline. Declared, the source reports a `monotonic` cursor committing {{run.advance.watermark-shape}}; undeclared, it refetches in full.

clauses.subject: authoring-surface
clauses.statement: The authoring surface runs at build time only and emits a content-hashed plan; nothing from it executes where the engine serves, and no build profile embeds a scripting runtime.

clauses.subject: plan-node
clauses.statement: A plan is a flat node list with predecessor edges: `step` (connector, optional retry), `sleep` (duration string), `awaitEvent` (optional timeout), `branch` (predicate, label-to-node-id map) and `parallel` (node ids).

clauses.subject: plan-version
clauses.statement: A plan's version is the leading 16 chars of the sha256 over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of its `{id, nodes}`.

clauses.subject: plan-schema
clauses.statement: The plan type is defined once in a schema library; its JSON Schema is the contract every language binds to, and the run path deserializes plan JSON against it.

clauses.subject: inline-step-body
clauses.statement: A `step` body other than a connector reference raises `PipelineInlineStepBody`.

clauses.subject: control-flow
clauses.statement: A data-dependent conditional or loop in a workflow body raises `PipelineUndeclaredControlFlow`; branching travels as `branch` and fan-out as `parallel`.

clauses.subject: node-id-collision
clauses.statement: A node id repeated in one plan raises `PipelineNodeIdCollision`, naming the id and both positions.

clauses.subject: lowering
clauses.statement: A plan lowers node by node onto {{run.journal.substrate-port}}.

clauses.subject: chain
clauses.statement: The chain is an ordered list of `select`, `rename`, `cast` and a single-column `filter`, declared once per pipeline and bound to the root table.

clauses.subject: arity
clauses.statement: A chain operation emitting more rows than it consumed raises `PipelineTransformArity`.

clauses.subject: filter
clauses.statement: A filter dropping a root row drops that row's nested children with it.
clauses.why: because a child landing under a parent id no surviving row carries is a dangling reference

clauses.subject: column-missing
clauses.statement: A filter or cast naming a column the batch does not carry raises `PipelineTransformColumnMissing`, printing the column and the table.
clauses.why: because a cast over an absent column otherwise lands the batch untransformed

clauses.subject: cast
clauses.statement: A cast rewrites one column's type and keeps its name and position.

clauses.subject: projection
clauses.statement: `select` fixes the outgoing column set by name, and `rename` maps an incoming name onto an outgoing one.

clauses.subject: typed-cast
clauses.statement: A cast to `binary`, `binary(n)`, `float32[n]` or `float16[n]` keeps a value that type's JSON form reads, nulls any other, and lands the column in that type.

clauses.subject: type-carry
clauses.statement: A `rename` carries a pulled column type to the new name, a `select` drops it with its column, and a cast to a scalar type drops it.

clauses.subject: host-stage
clauses.statement: Type inference over deferred-typing JSON, struct flattening, list-to-child extraction and id assignment run in engine code; no connector reimplements them and no dataframe library participates.

clauses.subject: normalized-form
clauses.statement: The canonical form is nested Arrow structs and lists; relational shredding is a late projection at the sink, so a source landing in two sinks normalizes once.

clauses.subject: mode
clauses.statement: `native` keeps nesting up to the sink's capability and explodes the rest with a downgrade schema-diff event; `relational` flattens structs into parent-child column names and shreds lists into child tables joined by a foreign key.

clauses.subject: mode-resolution
clauses.statement: Mode resolves per stream per sink: explicit declaration, then sink capability, then `native`.

clauses.subject: mode-unknown
clauses.statement: A mode outside the two raises `PipelineNormalizeModeUnknown`, printing both spellings.

clauses.subject: identity-columns
clauses.statement: Normalize injects a content-hash row id on every table, a load id on the root, a parent id and list index on each child, and a root id on a child nested deeper than one level.

clauses.subject: row-id
clauses.statement: The row id hashes the row's own content, so a re-run of one input emits byte-identical ids.

clauses.subject: list-index-missing
clauses.statement: A relational child table emitted without the list index that makes its projection reversible raises `PipelineListIndexMissing`, naming the parent and the list.

clauses.subject: nesting-depth
clauses.statement: Recursion stops at the declared depth, default five levels, landing a deeper subtree as one deferred-typing JSON column.

clauses.subject: placement
clauses.statement: The secret guard runs at the one pull path streaming and backfill share, ahead of the recorded pull and the land path, so a replay reintroduces no credential.

clauses.subject: matchers
clauses.statement: Matchers are linear-time, regex-free forward scans, each anchored on a literal prefix; the credential catalogue lives in code under a precision and recall fixture test.

clauses.subject: mask-span
clauses.statement: The replacement covers only the matched byte ranges, widened to character boundaries; overlapping spans merge under the higher-priority pattern.

clauses.subject: mask-replacement
clauses.statement: The replacement is the fixed `[REDACTED:secret]` marker, never a shape-preserving transform; an assignment keeps its `key=` prefix.

clauses.subject: mask-only
clauses.statement: The guard is on by default and blocks no run; each pull logs the count of masked cells per column.

clauses.subject: coverage
clauses.statement: The guard reads pre-normalize string cells for plaintext shapes; encoded material and a credential split across two cells pass through.

clauses.subject: stage-order
clauses.statement: A batch passes pull, the secret guard, the recorded pull, normalize, the transform chain, write-path redaction, shredding and batch write; the run then commits rows and position together through {{run.advance.commit-with-rows}}.

clauses.subject: unknown-destination
clauses.statement: The local context store is the only destination, and synthesized artifacts write back through it; any other `destination` raises `PipelineUnknownDestination` at assembly, before any row moves.

clauses.subject: no-host-arm
clauses.statement: The destination world declares no host arm, so a guest supplies no destination.

clauses.subject: batch-write
clauses.statement: A landing table is created on first sight of its schema, {{store.reconcile.first-sight}}; each batch is written durably in its own call, optionally carrying its ordinal as the join key onto the run's request ledger.

clauses.subject: typed-pull
clauses.statement: A pull's `types` object maps a column to a type spelled as {{store.reconcile.typed-landing}} reads it, and the run commit lands that column in it; an unreadable spelling fails the pull as {{store.reconcile.incompatible}}.

clauses.subject: irreconcilable-schema
clauses.statement: An arriving schema the store cannot reconcile fails the batch as {{store.reconcile.incompatible}}.

clauses.subject: commit-visibility
clauses.statement: A commit makes a run's rows visible for one table in one step; a crash before it leaves a recoverable partial run.

clauses.subject: ingest-tally
clauses.statement: A fire reports `fetched`, `kept`, `skipped`, `failed`, `dropped_low_quality` and a per-source breakdown; a non-zero `failed` exits non-zero.

clauses.subject: unreadable-input
clauses.statement: Input a parser cannot read raises `PipelineUnreadableInput`, naming the path and the position inside it, permanent against the retry schedule and failing one table's pull.

clauses.subject: partial-parse
clauses.statement: A reader stopping partway through a multi-part input raises `PipelinePartialParse` over the whole input and lands none of its parts.

clauses.subject: parse-boundary
clauses.statement: A decode that can die runs outside the serving process, which bounds its wall clock and memory and makes it killable.

clauses.subject: parse-crashed
clauses.statement: A non-zero exit or fatal signal from the decode process raises `PipelineParseCrashed` naming the input; no input ends the serving process.

clauses.subject: table-failed
clauses.statement: A table whose pull fails raises `PipelineTableFailed` carrying the table, the error kind and the run id; the fire then follows `on_table_error`.
clauses.why: because a failure is answerable by name only when it carries its table and run

clauses.subject: phase
clauses.statement: The catalog records one phase per pipeline: `planning` computes the chunk plan with nothing fetched, `seeding` loads consumer-held history, `backfilling` runs chunks across ticks, `streaming` pulls the incremental delta.

clauses.subject: chunk-plan
clauses.statement: Plan shape follows cursor kind: `monotonic` plans independent time-window or id-range chunks, `opaque-token` one sequential chunk walked in order, `snapshot-id` version ranges sequential per stream and parallel across streams.

clauses.subject: chunk-parallelism
clauses.statement: A sequential chunk plan declared beside a parallelism above one raises `PipelineChunkParallelism`, naming the plan and the value.
clauses.why: because two workers walking one continuation token skip or duplicate pages silently

clauses.subject: chunk
clauses.statement: A chunk row carries pipeline id, chunk id, predicate, status, attempt count, start and completion instants and a cursor-committed flag; an interrupted plan resumes at the first chunk not done.

clauses.subject: chunk-lease
clauses.statement: A worker leases a chunk row, recording node id and attempt, for a 300 s time-to-live renewed every 60 s, and writes under a path segmented by run, node, chunk and attempt.
clauses.why: because an unquantified lease cannot be tested against a paused worker

clauses.subject: fenced-commit
clauses.statement: A chunk commits in one catalog update conditioned on `attempt = :mine AND status != 'done'`; an update matching no row leaves that worker's files uncommitted.
clauses.why: because an expired holder otherwise commits over its successor

clauses.subject: commit-signal
clauses.statement: The catalog row, not directory presence, is the commit signal; files under a path with no done row are collected by a retention window.

clauses.subject: attempt-isolation
clauses.statement: An expired lease lets a second worker claim the chunk, increment the attempt and write under its own path.

clauses.subject: tick
clauses.statement: While a pipeline backfills, a tick dispatches up to the per-tick chunk cap or no-ops when the queue is full; the declared cadence resumes once the position catches up.

clauses.subject: block
clauses.statement: `[pipeline.backfill]` declares `max_chunks`, the bound on a plan's chunk count; `chunk_size`, one clock-ranged chunk's width in cursor units; and `start_from`, the floor, default zero.

clauses.subject: rewind
clauses.statement: A rewind returns every chunk overlapping the half-open range to pending and appends one reason row per rewound chunk to an audit log a catalog rebuild leaves untouched.

clauses.subject: rewind-invalid
clauses.statement: An inverted, empty or scale-incomparable rewind window raises `PipelineRewindWindowInvalid`; a window overlapping no chunk is a no-op.

clauses.subject: block
clauses.statement: `[pipeline.seed]` attaches a bulk-load source with a ceiling `below` expressed on the seeded table's `order_by` scale.

clauses.subject: one-land-path
clauses.statement: Seeded rows travel {{run.land.stage-order}} unchanged; attribution survives only in the load id and a run recorded under the `seeding` phase.

clauses.subject: declaration-missing
clauses.statement: A seeded table without `primary_key`, or with `order_by` left at the ingest stamp, raises `PipelineSeedDeclarationMissing` at plan and validate.

clauses.subject: ceiling-breached
clauses.statement: A seeded row whose ordering stamp reaches `below` raises `PipelineSeedCeilingBreached` naming the value; its chunk lands nothing, and the stamp is neither clamped nor dropped.

clauses.subject: ceiling-point
clauses.statement: The ceiling is evaluated on the root batch after normalize and the chain, before the write.

clauses.subject: ceiling-unevaluable
clauses.statement: A batch missing the ordering column, or a stamp unorderable against the ceiling, raises `PipelineSeedCeilingUnevaluable`; a text stamp orders only when `Z`-suffixed at the ceiling's fractional width.

clauses.subject: scope
clauses.statement: Seed chunk and cursor state live under a `<table>#seed` scope apart from the live pipeline's.

clauses.subject: connector-pin
clauses.statement: A seeding run is exempt from {{run.own.pinned-plan-changed}} and records its connector identity as provenance.

clauses.subject: ceiling-binding
clauses.statement: On seed commit, an unset `monotonic` live position takes the ceiling when `below` parses as an integer; under the other cursor kinds the live position stays unset and starts from the source's beginning.

clauses.subject: fingerprint
clauses.statement: Each run probes the seed source for a cheap fingerprint, a stat or a HEAD and never a download, and compares it with the one stamped at commit.

clauses.subject: source-changed
clauses.statement: A differing fingerprint raises `PipelineSeedSourceChanged` naming both values; an equal one skips the load, and an unavailable one skips with a warning.

clauses.subject: commands
clauses.statement: `seed status` prints each seeded table's ceiling, commit state and fingerprint match; `seed reset <pipeline> [--table T]` clears the seed's chunk plan.

clauses.subject: parity
clauses.statement: Over keys the vendor still returns, seeding then running live across an overlapping window yields a pure live backfill's row count and per-key winners; a key the vendor stopped returning keeps its seeded value.

clauses.subject: parity-audit
clauses.statement: `validate` audits the seed ordering over every landed row, not over the deduped view.

clauses.subject: compaction-cadence
clauses.statement: A seeded pipeline declares a scheduled fold covering each seeded table.
clauses.why: because without a snapshot the seeded and live rows for one key both survive the union read

clauses.subject: manifest-commit
clauses.statement: A published table's contract identity, freshness and current build ride the snapshot manifest commit that publishes its data; no separate file is authoritative for any of them.
clauses.why: because separately written artifacts make a torn publication representable

clauses.subject: contract-identity
clauses.statement: A published table's identity is `contract_version` beside `schema_fingerprint`, taken over the declared columns, their types and the grain.

clauses.subject: contract-mismatch
clauses.statement: A materialization whose columns, types or grain miss the declared contract raises `PipelineContractMismatch`, naming the column and the expectation.

clauses.subject: staging
clauses.statement: A build materializes into staging and publishes through {{run.publish.manifest-commit}}; a refused build leaves the last published state serving.

clauses.subject: history-logs
clauses.statement: `contract-history.jsonl`, `builds.jsonl` and `holds.jsonl` are append-only history derived from committed manifests; a log disagreeing with a manifest is regenerated from it.

clauses.subject: build-entry
clauses.statement: A build entry carries build id, start and completion instants, a status of published, refused or partial, the contract identity, and the partition values it left unfilled.

clauses.subject: freshness
clauses.statement: Freshness carries the newest publishing build id, its watermark, `max_lag`, the last build status and a withheld-cells flag; staleness is derived from watermark against `max_lag` and never stored.

clauses.subject: hold
clauses.statement: A hold records build id, placing principal and expiry; collection skips a held build, and a hold confers no other authority.

clauses.subject: manifest-section
clauses.statement: The manifest section carries `{contract_version, schema_fingerprint, build_id, last_built_at, watermark, max_lag, last_build_status, partitions_failed?, semantics_version?, fingerprint_recipe?}` of the newest publishing build, an absent optional key omitted.

clauses.subject: semantics-version
clauses.statement: `semantics_version` advances when the engine adds an injected column, and `fingerprint_recipe` names the fingerprint's inputs, that column included.

clauses.subject: disclosure-digest
clauses.statement: A build records a digest over its declared disclosure policy, set-valued fields sorted, in the manifest and in the build log.

clauses.subject: required-key
clauses.statement: An absent or blank `engine`, `source_table`, `media_column` or `parent_id_column` raises `DeriveConfigKeyMissing`, naming the key and the pipeline.

clauses.subject: no-store-root
clauses.statement: A source built without a store root or without its pipeline id raises `DeriveNoStoreRoot`, naming which is absent.

clauses.subject: foreign-output-table
clauses.statement: The anti-join's pipeline id comes from the build alone; a config key naming another pipeline's output raises `DeriveForeignOutputTable`.

clauses.subject: rows-per-run
clauses.statement: `max_rows_per_run` truncates the outstanding list after the anti-join, at 25 rows by default; zero or below resolves to that default.

clauses.subject: attempts-per-unit
clauses.statement: `max_attempts` allows 3 attempts per unit by default, and a non-positive spelling means the same figure.

clauses.subject: seconds-per-run
clauses.statement: `max_seconds_per_run` bounds the serial unit loop at 300 s by default for `link_preview` and carries no default for `transcribe`.

clauses.subject: incomplete-unit
clauses.statement: A parent row whose key or media column is null, empty or whitespace raises `DeriveUnitIncomplete`; the row is skipped and counted on the run record.

clauses.subject: journaled-pull
clauses.statement: A derive pipeline configured to journal its pulls raises `DeriveJournaledPull`.

clauses.subject: unmetered-grant
clauses.statement: `task` alone decides whether a derive pipeline reaches vendors; a `transcribe` pipeline declaring a shared-quota grant raises `DeriveUnmeteredGrant`.

clauses.subject: metered-client
clauses.statement: A `link_preview` pipeline opening a socket outside the mediated client raises `DeriveMeteredClient`; every request it makes enters the run's request ledger.

clauses.subject: anti-join
clauses.statement: Each tick recomputes the outstanding set: every parent row holding neither a passage nor a settled marker in the pipeline's own output table.

clauses.subject: latest-marker
clauses.statement: A unit's standing is its latest marker by `_ingested_at`, `_run_id` and `_row_seq`, never its highest attempt count.
clauses.why: because an `empty` marker records 1 attempt, so ranking by count lets an older retry revive a settled unit

clauses.subject: unbound-engine
clauses.statement: An engine with no `[derive.<name>]` block raises `DeriveEngineUnbound`, naming the pipeline, the engine, the file to edit and every bound engine.

clauses.subject: command-in-manifest
clauses.statement: `command`, `preprocess`, `env` or `allow_hosts` inside `[pipeline.source.config]` raises `DeriveCommandInManifest`.

clauses.subject: unknown-task
clauses.statement: `task` is `transcribe`, the default, or `link_preview`; any other value raises `DeriveUnknownTask`, printing both.

clauses.subject: driver-mismatch
clauses.statement: `driver` is `exec` or `"none"` behind `transcribe` and `fetch` behind `link_preview`; any other pairing raises `DeriveDriverMismatch`.

clauses.subject: endpoint-host-bare
clauses.statement: An `endpoint_host` carrying a path, query, port or scheme raises `DeriveEndpointHostNotBare`.

clauses.subject: remote-url-unsupported
clauses.statement: An `http` or `https` media value for an engine declining remote addresses raises `DeriveRemoteUrlUnsupported`, naming the `when = "media_is_url"` preprocess step.

clauses.subject: media-unreadable
clauses.statement: A media value that is neither an address nor a readable local file raises `DeriveMediaUnreadable`, failing that unit alone.

clauses.subject: media-root
clauses.statement: A local media value resolves, canonicalized, under the binding's `media_root`, the working directory by default; a path escaping it raises `DeriveMediaOutsideRoot`, failing that unit alone.
clauses.why: because a parent row is third-party data, and an unconfined path reads any file the machine's user can

clauses.subject: confidence-range
clauses.statement: A `confidence` outside `0.0..=1.0` after adapter normalization raises `DeriveConfidenceOutOfRange` and lands null.

clauses.subject: upstream-excerpt
clauses.statement: An `Upstream` excerpt holds at most 4 KiB and no request body.

clauses.subject: engine-unavailable
clauses.statement: `EngineUnavailable` from a transcriber ends the run; from a `LinkReader` it raises `DeriveLinkEngineUnavailable` and costs that one unit.

clauses.subject: advisory-zone
clauses.statement: A row zone taken from the binding's advisory `zone` key raises `DeriveAdvisoryZone`.

clauses.subject: shell-command
clauses.statement: `command` is an argument array run with no shell; a `command` given as one string raises `DeriveShellCommand`.

clauses.subject: env-name
clauses.statement: An allowlist name that is not ASCII alphanumeric or underscore, or that leads with a digit, raises `DeriveEnvNameInvalid`.

clauses.subject: chain-deadline
clauses.statement: `timeout_secs` bounds one unit's whole chain at 1800 s by default.

clauses.subject: captured-output
clauses.statement: `max_output_bytes` bounds each step's captured standard output and error at 8 MiB by default.

clauses.subject: audit-entries
clauses.statement: A chain contributes at most 64 entries of captured output to the run record.

clauses.subject: step-error-excerpt
clauses.statement: A failing step's error text carries at most 4 KiB of its standard error.

clauses.subject: non-zero-exit
clauses.statement: A step exiting non-zero raises `DeriveStepExit` carrying its bounded error text into the run audit.

clauses.subject: deadline-elapsed
clauses.statement: A chain outrunning its deadline raises `DeriveStepTimeout`, naming the running step.

clauses.subject: output-cap
clauses.statement: Output past the bound is counted and discarded, never buffered; crossing it kills the step and raises `DeriveOutputCap` with the byte count, draining continuing so the child never blocks.

clauses.subject: silent-step
clauses.statement: A preprocess step exiting zero without writing its output file raises `DeriveStepProducedNothing`.

clauses.subject: missing-binary
clauses.statement: A `command[0]` that is not an executable file on this machine raises `DeriveBinaryMissing`, naming the binary and the step.

clauses.subject: unpinned-path
clauses.statement: A path-form `command[0]` without `sha256` raises `DeriveUnpinnedPath`, quoting the digest just computed; a bare search-path name carries none.

clauses.subject: digest-mismatch
clauses.statement: A pinned file whose bytes differ from its recorded digest raises `DeriveDigestMismatch`.

clauses.subject: no-shell
clauses.statement: A step runs as its argument array with no shell, in a process group of its own, under a cleared environment holding only the binding's `env` table.

clauses.subject: step-condition
clauses.statement: A preprocess step runs only while its `when` holds: `media_is_url` for an `http` or `https` input, `engine_requires_pcm16_wav` for an input other than 16-bit PCM WAV; another name raises `DeriveStepConditionUnknown`.
clauses.why: because a misspelled condition otherwise skips or runs its step silently

clauses.subject: verified-spawn
clauses.statement: Each spawn re-reads its step's binary and runs it only while those bytes match the digest resolved at run start, else {{run.exec.digest-mismatch}}.

clauses.subject: engine-id
clauses.statement: An `exec` engine id reads `exec:<name>@<prefix>`, the prefix being 12 chars of lowercase hex over every step's binary digest and arguments.

clauses.subject: scheme
clauses.statement: An address whose scheme is neither `http` nor `https` raises `DeriveSchemeUnsupported` before any socket opens.

clauses.subject: address-literal
clauses.statement: A host written as an address literal raises `DeriveAddressLiteral`.

clauses.subject: redirect-chain
clauses.statement: A redirect chain runs to at most 5 hops.

clauses.subject: binding-key
clauses.statement: `env`, `preprocess`, `engine` or `max_output_bytes` on a fetch binding raises `DeriveFetchBindingKey`, naming the key.
clauses.why: because a silently ignored key leaves an operator believing a fetch carries a credential or runs a process

clauses.subject: document-prefix
clauses.statement: `max_document_bytes` bounds the scanned document prefix at 1 MiB by default, dropping the remainder.

clauses.subject: probe-prefix
clauses.statement: `max_probe_bytes` bounds one picture range request at 64 KiB by default.

clauses.subject: hop-timeout
clauses.statement: `request_timeout_secs` bounds one hop at 20 s by default.

clauses.subject: retry-after-default
clauses.statement: A `429` without a usable `Retry-After` maps to `RateLimited` carrying 60 s.

clauses.subject: charset
clauses.statement: A declared character set other than UTF-8 raises `DeriveCharsetUnsupported`, naming the value.

clauses.subject: not-utf8
clauses.statement: A document declaring no character set and failing UTF-8 validation raises `DeriveBytesNotUtf8`; a character split at the byte bound is tolerated.

clauses.subject: failure-off-table
clauses.statement: Per-unit failure state recorded outside the output table raises `DeriveFailureOffTable`.

clauses.subject: unit-status
clauses.statement: `unit_status` is `ok`, `empty` where the engine established nothing to derive, `unavailable` where it returned nothing and stated no reason, or `failed` on a typed error; any other value raises `DeriveUnitStatusUnknown`.

clauses.subject: reserved-discriminator
clauses.statement: A derive table declaring a column named `kind` raises `DeriveReservedDiscriminator`.

clauses.subject: settled-revived
clauses.statement: A settled unit re-entering the outstanding set raises `DeriveSettledUnitRevived`.

clauses.subject: attempts
clauses.statement: `attempts` is the prior count plus one; `unavailable` and `failed` stop at {{run.select.attempts-per-unit}}, and `empty` receives 1 attempts in total.

clauses.subject: unredacted-error
clauses.statement: A non-null `last_error` write that has not passed address redaction raises `DeriveUnredactedError`.

clauses.subject: primary-key
clauses.statement: A derive output table without `primary_key` `["unit_ref", "cue_seq"]` raises `DerivePrimaryKeyMissing`.
clauses.why: because a re-derived unit otherwise lands duplicate passages beside the originals

clauses.subject: marker-row
clauses.statement: A unit yielding no passage lands one marker row, `cue_seq` -1 and `kind` `marker`, carrying its status, attempts, last error and whether it retries.

clauses.subject: empty-document
clauses.statement: Only a WebVTT document whose blocks are its header, notes and styles establishes nothing to derive; empty output, or blocks none of which parse, lands `unavailable`.

clauses.subject: canceled-unit
clauses.statement: A unit whose chain a run stop interrupts lands no row and charges no attempt; the pull ends `Canceled` once {{run.cancel.child-reaped}}.

clauses.subject: backward-cue
clauses.statement: A block starting before the last accepted block raises `DeriveCueOutOfOrder` and is dropped.

clauses.subject: passage-chars
clauses.statement: A passage stays open while it holds fewer than 600 chars.

clauses.subject: passage-span
clauses.statement: A passage stays open while it spans less than 60 s.

clauses.subject: passage-bytes
clauses.statement: One passage's text holds at most 8 KiB.

clauses.subject: passages-per-document
clauses.statement: One document yields at most 2000 rows of passages.

clauses.subject: grammar
clauses.statement: SubRip and WebVTT read through one grammar: a block's timing line, then its text lines joined by a space.

clauses.subject: unsupported-driver
clauses.statement: A `fetch` engine named to the verb raises `DeriveTestEngineUnsupported`.
clauses.why: because the verb drives a transcriber over media, and a link engine takes no media

clauses.subject: authoring-path
clauses.statement: Every connector implements one trait, as a component sandboxed in the host runtime or as a native sibling compiled into the binary. Dispatch carries no branch naming which of the two it calls.

clauses.subject: type-taxonomy
clauses.statement: The shared types interface carries a schema (name, fields, primary key) and a field (name, data type, nullability) over `boolean`, `int32`, `int64`, `float64`, `string`, `bytes`, `timestamp-millis` and `json`.

clauses.subject: batch-encoding
clauses.statement: A batch crosses the boundary as Arrow IPC bytes, and a position as opaque bytes beside a declared cursor kind.

clauses.subject: arrow-types
clauses.statement: The host reads an Arrow `Binary` or `FixedSizeBinary` column as bytes of that width and a `FixedSizeList` of `Float32` or `Float16` as that vector, each landing in its {{store.reconcile.binary-and-vector}} type, never as text.

clauses.subject: nested-value
clauses.statement: A nested value rides as `json` and takes its type at the normalize stage. The interface carries no recursive type definition.

clauses.subject: guaranteed-type
clauses.statement: A guest declares the type it guarantees after its own parsing — `int64` for a count, `float64` for money and a rate — and lands null, never zero, for a spelling it cannot read.
clauses.why: because a text column pushes a cast into every downstream read

clauses.subject: read-handle
clauses.statement: A source exports its cursor kind, a discovery call, and an open call taking a table and an optional position. The handle's `next` yields one batch or exhaustion; its `position` reports where it stands.

clauses.subject: write-handle
clauses.statement: A destination exports `prepare`, `write`, `commit` and `abort`. Source and destination are separate worlds sharing the types interface.

clauses.subject: optional-world
clauses.statement: Operator configuration and failure attribution are each an interface in an additional world, probed on the instance by name. A base-world guest instantiates untouched, and neither addition moves the world version.

clauses.subject: partition-attribution
clauses.statement: A guest exporting failure attribution answers with the byte-exact values of the outermost partition column a failed read belongs to. The host reads it on failure and success alike; an empty list keeps the unattributed refusal.
clauses.why: because a read holding one partition back and landing the rest returns success

clauses.subject: attribution-budget
clauses.statement: Failure attribution carries at most 512 entries per session, each value at most 512 B.

clauses.subject: native-read
