clauses.statement: A binary column masks by `drop` or by `hash` over its bytes, a vector column by `drop` alone; another strategy on either raises `EnforceStrategyOutsideType` at manifest load.

clauses.subject: absent-column
clauses.statement: A mask naming a column the table's schema omits raises `EnforceMaskOnAbsentColumn` at manifest load, refusing the whole manifest.
clauses.why: because a skipped declaration serves reads under a policy its author believed covered a column

clauses.subject: masks-per-table
clauses.statement: A table carries at most 128 entries in its column mask set.
clauses.why: because a table beyond it needs a drop, not a mask per column

clauses.subject: scope-denied
clauses.statement: A tenant-scoped credential reading another tenant's rows on a granted table raises `EnforceScopeDenied`, as wire code `scope_denied`, HTTP `403` or an in-band tool error, naming the table and both scopes.

clauses.subject: not-empty
clauses.statement: A scope refusal is a typed error, never an empty result.

clauses.subject: echo
clauses.statement: The requested scope in a refusal echoes the statement's value, never a stored value.

clauses.subject: ungranted-table
clauses.statement: A relation the caller holds no grant on, whether or not a table of that name exists, raises `EnforceUnknownRelation` and is absent from listings and descriptions.

clauses.subject: payload
clauses.statement: A refusal payload carries at most 512 B.

clauses.subject: scope-guard
clauses.statement: The scope guard walks the engine's parse once, deciding literal equalities and membership lists over the tenant column and bound template parameters destined for it.

clauses.subject: top-level
clauses.statement: The guard reads top-level conjuncts of a statement whose own FROM names a scoped table.

clauses.subject: guard-walk
clauses.statement: The guard visits at most 4096 entries of one parse tree.

clauses.subject: undecidable
clauses.statement: A constraint the guard cannot settle composes as an ordinary conjunct; the engine-applied equality isolates.

clauses.subject: drifted-scope
clauses.statement: A tenant value matching no partition reads empty, like a tenant that wrote nothing; the read path repairs no transformed scope value.

clauses.subject: withhold
clauses.statement: A cleared redistribution flag withholds every object of the table at push and omits the table's name from the bucket manifest.

clauses.subject: before-diff
clauses.statement: The exclusion applies before the object diff is computed.

clauses.subject: outranks-grants
clauses.statement: The bound holds against a credential granted everything.

clauses.subject: envelopes
clauses.statement: The bound covers the table's columnar files and each pull's verbatim record.

clauses.subject: root-allowlist
clauses.statement: While any table is withheld, a root-level object ships only when the allowlist in Shapes names it.

clauses.subject: root-not-allowlisted
clauses.statement: A root-level object absent from the allowlist raises `EnforceRootObjectNotAllowlisted` at push.

clauses.subject: left-behind
clauses.statement: Clearing the flag over a table an earlier push uploaded raises `EnforceStaleRedistributedObjects`, naming each object and the remedy, deleting none.

clauses.subject: manifest-is-an-index
clauses.statement: An object stays fetchable by its key after the manifest stops naming it; a manifest authorizes nothing.

clauses.subject: report
clauses.statement: A left-behind report names at most 100 files and states the total found.

clauses.subject: two-checks
clauses.statement: The left-behind check runs before and after the upload loop; the guarantee holds for one bucket under one pushing configuration.

clauses.subject: edge-filter
clauses.statement: A serving edge in front of the bucket filters a materialized replica by the pulling credential's grants.

clauses.subject: zone-string
clauses.statement: A zone string parses, after trimming, as `local:device`, `on-prem:<id>`, `private-cloud:<id>` or `public-cloud:<id>`; any other text is undeclared. The identifier is part of the value.

clauses.subject: allow-set-entry
clauses.statement: An allow-set entry is `*`, `local:device`, `on-prem:*`, `private-cloud:*`, `public-cloud:*`, or a category carrying a concrete identifier.

clauses.subject: unparsed-pattern
clauses.statement: An allow-set entry matching no entry form raises `EnforceZonePatternUnparsed`, naming the entry.
clauses.why: because an unparsed entry matching nothing hides a policy error; a new zone category updates the grammar first

clauses.subject: disjunctive
clauses.statement: A zone is admitted when any entry matches. A bare category matches every identifier in it; an entry carrying an identifier matches that identifier alone.

clauses.subject: undeclared
clauses.statement: Only `*` admits an undeclared zone.

clauses.subject: caller-zone
clauses.statement: The calling process declares its zone per request; the store carries none.

clauses.subject: asserted-zone
clauses.statement: A zone a request asserts stands only where it equals the zone its credential signs; any other assertion raises `EnforceZoneAssertionWidens`, naming both.
clauses.why: because an unsigned argument able to widen placement makes the signed zone decorative

clauses.subject: picks-no-model
clauses.statement: Placement selects no model and dispatches no inference; the engine's one invocation point is an operator-configured endpoint capability for synthesis.

clauses.subject: fail-closed
clauses.statement: A table declaring no zone policy resolves to the fail-closed pair `local:device` and `on-prem:*`, declared and discovered tables alike.

clauses.subject: permissive-default
clauses.statement: A default resolving an unlabeled table to `*` raises `EnforcePermissiveZoneDefault` where more than one principal owns the store.

clauses.subject: protected-floor
clauses.statement: A `phi` column or table carries a floor at the fail-closed pair; a wider declared set resolves down to it at serve time unless the override names that class or column.

clauses.subject: floor-widened
clauses.statement: A manifest widening a protected-class surface past its floor without an override naming that class raises `EnforceProtectedFloorWidened`.

clauses.subject: removal-with-public-cloud
clauses.statement: A surface declaring write-time removal on a column and an allow-set admitting a public cloud raises `EnforceRemovalWithPublicCloud`.

clauses.subject: narrowest-grain
clauses.statement: A column's set narrows its table's; a principal's set narrows both.

clauses.subject: excluded-row
clauses.statement: Where the table's effective set omits the session's zone, the row leaves the result.

clauses.subject: excluded-cell
clauses.statement: A cell whose effective set omits the session's zone arrives null, a mask exception notwithstanding.

clauses.subject: per-principal
clauses.statement: A principal's allow-set pins every row it authors wherever the row lands. A row with no verified author resolves as an undeclared zone.

clauses.subject: evidence-floor
clauses.statement: A synthesized row declaring a set wider than the intersection of its evidence tables' sets raises `EnforceEvidenceFloorExceeded` and resolves to that intersection.

clauses.subject: incognito
clauses.statement: Incognito pins the session to the fail-closed pair, the uncredentialed local owner's reads included.

clauses.subject: incognito-widening
clauses.statement: A session asserting a zone wider than the incognito pin raises `EnforceIncognitoWidening`.

clauses.subject: team-default
clauses.statement: A project declares a default zone, whether users widen it, and whether incognito is on by default.

clauses.subject: serve-outcome
clauses.statement: Serving one row yields a drop flag and the list of zone-masked columns.

clauses.subject: envelope
clauses.statement: A response envelope carries row counts removed by predicate and by zone, column names masked by policy and by zone, the asserted zone and the incognito flag, and no removed value.

clauses.subject: symbolic-inclusion
clauses.statement: Inclusion against a floor is decided over every constructor and identifier, never by probing sample zones.

clauses.subject: proxy-boundary
clauses.statement: A proxy replica resolves zones at the proxy boundary.

clauses.subject: allow-set-entries
clauses.statement: An allow-set holds at most 32 entries.

clauses.subject: identifier-length
clauses.statement: A zone identifier holds at most 128 chars.

clauses.subject: credential-shaped-value
clauses.statement: The write path raises `EnforceCredentialShapedValue` on a value matching a credential shape, before it reaches storage.

clauses.subject: read-only-face
clauses.statement: An organization-wide face serves the read subset of the tool surface; conversational writes are server-authored.

clauses.subject: write-tool
clauses.statement: Registering a write tool on an organization-wide face raises `EnforceWriteOnReadOnlyFace`.

clauses.subject: unbound-table
clauses.statement: On an organization-wide face, a table with no visibility block raises `VisibilityUnboundTable` from diagnose and from the serving guardrail at start, naming the table.

clauses.subject: incomplete-binding
clauses.statement: A binding at a servable level lacking a declared sweep for its source or a `max_acl_staleness` raises `VisibilityBindingIncomplete`.

clauses.subject: coverage-watermark
clauses.statement: A sweep run that failed or skipped any governed resource of its source and advances `watermark_at` raises `VisibilityWatermarkUncovered`, and the watermark stays where it stood.

clauses.subject: ungapped-stream
clauses.statement: Advancing `watermark_at` from an event stream the mapping has not declared gap-detectable raises `VisibilityUngappedStream`.

clauses.subject: orphan-grant
clauses.statement: A grant landing with no resource row, or on a resource of the unknown class, raises `VisibilityOrphanGrant` at commit and joins no reachable set.

clauses.subject: closure-walk
clauses.statement: The closure walks the group graph with a visited set, ending any cycle, to a depth of `max_group_depth`, default 8 hops, and a breadth of 10000 nodes.

clauses.subject: closure-overflow
clauses.statement: A closure reaching its depth or node bound raises `VisibilityClosureDepth` with the non-retryable HTTP status 422 and returns no set.

clauses.subject: cache-capacity
clauses.statement: The reachable-set cache holds at most 100000 entries and evicts the least recently used.

clauses.subject: degraded-uncached
clauses.statement: Retaining a reachable set or result produced past a budget, or under the narrowing posture, raises `VisibilityDegradedCached`.

clauses.subject: budget-grammar
clauses.statement: `max_acl_staleness` is a positive integer with one suffix from `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`. A compound form, a bare number or another suffix raises `VisibilityBudgetMalformed`, naming the table and the text read.

clauses.subject: access-stale
clauses.statement: A read raises `VisibilityAccessStale` (HTTP 503, carrying source, lag, budget and last observation) when a touched table's source lag exceeds its budget, the source has no completed full run, or the public-status watermark is past budget.

clauses.subject: budget-below-cadence
clauses.statement: A budget tighter than the sweep cadence its source sustains raises `VisibilityBudgetUnreachable` at diagnose, naming both figures.

clauses.subject: family-bound
clauses.statement: A `person-container` table at a servable level, or a `directory` table above `excluded`, raises `VisibilityFamilyBound`, and the manifest declaring it does not load.

clauses.subject: family-undeclared
clauses.statement: A mapping landing a table without naming its `family` raises `VisibilityFamilyUndeclared`.

clauses.subject: federated-registered
clauses.statement: Registering a `federated` table on a read face raises `VisibilityFederatedRegistered`.

clauses.subject: federated-cache
clauses.statement: Retaining a federated result under a key omitting the subject raises `VisibilityFederatedCacheShared`.

clauses.subject: computed-inputs
clauses.statement: A source that computes access with a sharing engine is queried live. A mapping projecting that engine's inputs into `access_grants` raises `VisibilityComputedInputsMirrored`, naming the source.

clauses.subject: roster-from-payload
clauses.statement: A mapping deriving grants from a people list inside content — attendees, invitees, recipients, contacts — rather than from the source's permission endpoint raises `VisibilityRosterFromPayload`.

clauses.subject: mapping-absent
clauses.statement: A pack landing a table with neither an access mapping nor `excluded` raises `VisibilityMappingAbsent` at diagnose, naming the pack and the table.

clauses.subject: asserts-access
clauses.statement: An access-shaped key the mapping schema does not define raises `VisibilityPackAssertsAccess` by name. Fields outside the mapping are fetch inputs and reach no authorization decision.

clauses.subject: any-of-allowlist
clauses.statement: An allowlist evaluated as any-of raises `VisibilityAllowlistAnyOf` at load.

clauses.subject: unsupported-coarse
clauses.statement: Declaring `coarse` where the source emits no container or workspace signal raises `VisibilityUnsupportedCoarse`.

clauses.subject: offline-diagnostic
clauses.statement: The single-operator diagnostic reads the manifest and each published model's statement text from local disk and issues 0 requests to the object store.

clauses.subject: policy-absent
clauses.statement: A published aggregate-shaped model carrying neither a disclosure policy nor a recorded opt-out fails the diagnostic with `DisclosurePolicyAbsent`.

clauses.subject: model-unreadable
clauses.statement: A published model whose referenced statement text does not read raises `DisclosureModelUnreadable`.

clauses.subject: clean-room-preconditions
clauses.statement: A cross-owner store carries per-owner signed manifest subtrees, per-owner write prefixes enforced by the object store's access policy, and per-owner signing keys; one missing, checked before any cross-prefix write, raises `DisclosureCleanRoomPreconditionUnmet`.

clauses.subject: hashed-join
clauses.statement: Two owners match on a key each hashes at write time under a per-pair pepper re-randomized per join; matched rows leave as an aggregate under a group-size floor. A static pepper raises `DisclosureStaticPepper`.

clauses.subject: budget-reservation
clauses.statement: Before computing, a release reserves each contributing unit's declared per-run spend against its lifetime cap in one catalog transaction. A failed reservation raises `DisclosureUnitBudgetExhausted`, and the release publishes nothing.

clauses.subject: duplicate-grain
clauses.statement: A non-numeric, non-grain column rides the grouping, and one not constant within its group raises `DisclosureDuplicateGrain`.

clauses.subject: group-key
clauses.statement: A group key not a subset of the permitted grouping columns raises `DisclosureGroupKeyNotPermitted`.

clauses.subject: contributor-key
clauses.statement: A governed statement omitting the contributor key raises `DisclosureContributorKeyAbsent`.

clauses.subject: forbidden-column
clauses.statement: A contract declaring a forbidden column, or a materialization producing one, raises `DisclosureForbiddenColumnPublished`. The check runs after the contributor key leaves the published columns.

clauses.subject: min-group-size
clauses.statement: `min_group_size` counts distinct contributors and is at least 2 subjects. A group whose noised distinct-contributor count falls under it is suppressed, and a smaller declared value raises `DisclosureMinGroupSizeBelowFloor`.

clauses.subject: contributor-share
clauses.statement: `max_contributor_share` lies above 0 percent and at most 100 percent of a group's sign-insensitive metric mass; a value outside raises `DisclosureShareOutOfRange`.

clauses.subject: dominance-unverifiable
clauses.statement: A group under a share constraint whose per-contributor masses are unavailable raises `DisclosureDominanceUnverifiable` and is suppressed.

clauses.subject: empty-policy
clauses.statement: A policy setting neither threshold, or only a share ceiling at a whole group's mass, raises `DisclosurePolicySuppressesNothing`.

clauses.subject: grouping-allowlist
clauses.statement: An empty permitted-grouping list, or a permitted name that is not column-shaped, raises `DisclosureGroupingAllowlistEmpty`.

clauses.subject: single-statement
clauses.statement: A declaration holding more than one statement raises `DisclosureTemplateMultiStatement`.

clauses.subject: overfetch
clauses.statement: A capped result sets the envelope's truncation flag by reading exactly 1 rows past the effective ceiling.

clauses.subject: cohort-widening
clauses.statement: A read recovering an under-floor group by merging it into a coarser key raises `DisclosureCohortWidening`.

clauses.subject: per-individual-row
clauses.statement: Reading a per-individual row from a cohort table without an explicit grant on the reader's token raises `DisclosurePerIndividualUngranted`.

clauses.subject: singleton-cohort
clauses.statement: A cohort key whose grain resolves to one person raises `DisclosureSingletonCohort` at declaration, before any row lands under it.

clauses.subject: exact-figures
clauses.statement: A policy declaring `figures = "exact"` on a `per-person` table raises `DisclosureExactPerPerson`. `figures` defaults to `"noised"`, and exact figures publish only from a `cohort` table.

clauses.subject: segment
clauses.statement: Entries append to a numbered segment file in ascending `seq`, and a segment closes at 4096 entries under one signed root.

clauses.subject: group-commit
clauses.statement: Between segment opens, an append group, the appends one sync covers, issues 1 sync, of its segment file; the signed tip writes at segment close, on idle and at export.

clauses.subject: unpersisted-entry
clauses.statement: A read whose entry fails to reach local durable storage raises `AuditEntryUnpersisted` and returns no rows.

clauses.subject: single-writer
clauses.statement: One process holds a directory's audit log at a time; opening a log another holds raises `AuditLogHeld`.
clauses.why: because two writers caching one tip append the same seq twice, and every later verification breaks there

clauses.subject: projection
clauses.statement: The projection answers which agent read which table under which policy across a rolling 24 h window, within 1 s.

clauses.subject: no-row
clauses.statement: An explanation returning a row, field value or excerpt from the resource it decides about raises `VisibilityDiagnosticRow`.

clauses.subject: empty-window
clauses.statement: A window holding no observations raises `VisibilityNoObservations` and states that no claim is available.

clauses.subject: unqualified-assurance
clauses.statement: A negative assurance answer emitted without its coverage block raises `VisibilityUnqualifiedAssurance`.

clauses.subject: groups-not-members
clauses.statement: A reader-facing explanation rendering the member identities of a group on the path raises `VisibilityIndividualNamed`.

clauses.subject: broken-chain
clauses.statement: A disagreeing digest, a sequence gap, an absent chain beside `chain.tip` or a signed root, or, under the signed check opening a log runs, an absent or unverified tip or root raises `AuditChainBroken` at the earliest failing index.

clauses.subject: root-replication
clauses.statement: Signed roots reach the replication bucket asynchronously every 10 min.

clauses.subject: privilege
clauses.statement: Erasure sits outside the default grant set, and a caller without the forget grant raises `ErasureUngranted`.

clauses.subject: subject-column
clauses.statement: A table names its subject column as `subject_id = "<column>"` under `[[pipeline.tables]]`. A subject erasure against a table without one raises `ErasureSubjectUndeclared`, naming the table.

clauses.subject: cascade
clauses.statement: In the same operation the cascade invalidates every derived fact whose provenance reaches the subject key or a tombstoned identifier within 16 hops.

clauses.subject: cascade-unbounded
clauses.statement: A provenance chain deeper than the cascade bound raises `ErasureCascadeUnbounded`, and the erasure commits nothing.

clauses.subject: physical-removal
clauses.statement: Every file holding an erased row, a superseded snapshot still inside {{store.fold.retention}} included, is rewritten or collected within 24 h of the erasure's commit.

clauses.subject: restaging-gate
clauses.statement: `--fail-closed` writes a row-free `{subject_hash, executed_at}` marker at the store root after the cascade. While it stands, every fact read raises `ErasureRestagingRequired`, naming the owed re-synthesis and the clearing verb.

clauses.subject: tenant-column-type
clauses.statement: A tenant column of a non-string type raises `PurgeTenantColumnType`.

clauses.subject: tenant-undeclared
clauses.statement: A purge finding no model declaring an outermost partition key raises `PurgeTenantUndeclared`.

clauses.subject: owner-only
clauses.statement: A purge presented with a capability token raises `PurgeRequiresOwner`, evaluated before anything reveals store contents.

clauses.subject: pseudonym
clauses.statement: `tenant_hash` is SHA-256 over a random per-receipt `salt` and the tenant identifier. A receipt carrying the identifier in cleartext raises `ReceiptIdentifierLeak` before signing.

clauses.subject: widened-claim
clauses.statement: A coverage block naming a scope broader than its `receipt_version` declares raises `ReceiptClaimWidened`.

clauses.subject: replayed
clauses.statement: Returning the byte-identical earlier artifact in place of a freshly signed one raises `ReceiptReplayed`.

clauses.subject: no-rewrite-engine
clauses.statement: A purge where the columnar rewrite engine is unavailable raises `ReceiptWithoutRewrite` and signs nothing.
clauses.why: because a receipt over a rewrite that did not run states a false claim

clauses.subject: unreadable-schedule
clauses.statement: A schedule string the grammar cannot read, including `L`, `W`, `?`, `#` and `@` macros, raises `ScheduleUnreadable` for that entry alone, naming the diagnostic; every other entry of the document arms.

clauses.subject: unknown-trigger
clauses.statement: An unrecognized trigger value raises `TriggerAdapterUnknown` at startup and downgrades onto no adapter.

clauses.subject: trigger-face-missing
clauses.statement: `external` selected on a deployment serving no HTTP face raises `TriggerFaceMissing` at startup.

clauses.subject: wake-answer
clauses.statement: A wake answers within 25 s with what fired, what failed, what stays armed and the next due instant, naming each fire still in flight as pending.
clauses.why: because a platform request timeout otherwise ends the call before the caller learns anything

clauses.subject: tick-interval
clauses.statement: The in-process adapter evaluates the armed set every 500 ms.

clauses.subject: poll-cadence
clauses.statement: `poll` takes a schedule string, and a `[control]` block declaring none polls every 30 s.

clauses.subject: pointer-malformed
clauses.statement: A pointer body that is not wholly a version raises `ControlPointerMalformed`.
clauses.why: because an integer read out of leading bytes arms a version nobody applied

clauses.subject: fail-static
clauses.statement: An unreadable pointer, an unparseable snapshot or a control plane answering `5xx` raises `ControlSnapshotUnreadable`, logs a diagnostic, and leaves the armed set in place running.

clauses.subject: loopback-only
clauses.statement: A control URL whose host is not a loopback address raises `ControlSourceNotLoopback` and arms nothing; a poll follows no redirect and routes through no proxy.

clauses.subject: job-kind-unknown
clauses.statement: A block naming a kind outside the union, an argument vector or a host command raises `JobKindUnknown` at validation.

clauses.subject: target-unbound
clauses.statement: A `fold` target naming no produced table, or a `build` target naming no declared model, raises `JobTargetUnbound` at validation.

clauses.subject: cycle-control-source
clauses.statement: A configured control source that does not resolve under `cycle` raises `CycleControlSourceUnresolved`.

clauses.subject: not-a-head
clauses.statement: Where entries are landing steps of one dependent run, the run is the unit and cadence rides its head entry. A due id that is a step raises `DispatchUnitNotAHead` and starts nothing.

clauses.subject: step-result
clauses.statement: A checkpointed step returns a pointer, an object-store key or a catalog row id, under a 1 MiB step-result cap.

clauses.subject: in-band-tool-error
clauses.statement: A step driving the engine over the tool protocol judges the tool result, not transport status: a `200` carrying a protocol error or a result flagged `isError` raises `StepToolError`.

clauses.subject: callback-skew
clauses.statement: The relay accepts a callback timestamp within 300 s of its own clock.

clauses.subject: callback-rejected
clauses.statement: A callback whose attempt is below the step's current attempt, or whose timestamp falls outside {{surface.dispatch.callback-skew}}, raises `DispatchCallbackRejected` and changes no step.
clauses.why: because a partitioned worker's late result otherwise overwrites its successor's, and a captured callback replays indefinitely

clauses.subject: heartbeat-beat
clauses.statement: A worker heartbeat runs every 15 s.

clauses.subject: heartbeat-lapse
clauses.statement: A heartbeat lapse past 60 s reschedules that worker's in-flight work onto another matching worker under the next attempt number.

clauses.subject: secret-in-document
clauses.statement: A credential value typed into a configuration field raises `SecretMaterialInDocument`; the document holds references and the backend holds material.
clauses.why: because a value in the document reaches every daemon and replica that reads a snapshot

clauses.subject: connector-upload
clauses.statement: An artifact uploaded through the operator surface raises `ConnectorUploadRefused`; the surface references registered connectors by id and version.
clauses.why: because publishing into the registry runs a separate signed path

clauses.subject: version-race
clauses.statement: An apply whose compare-and-swap loses raises `ManifestVersionConflict`, reloads the winning version and reapplies its pending edits onto it, overwriting no applied version.

clauses.subject: validation
clauses.statement: A document failing engine validation raises `ApplyValidationRefused` and claims no version.
clauses.why: because a snapshot store holding a version daemons refuse to arm stalls every daemon reading it

clauses.subject: owner-unconfigured
clauses.statement: An owner with no storage configured or no credential raises `ConfigOwnerUnconfigured`, answered `503`; no local writer substitutes for the store-scoped API.

clauses.subject: weak-conditional-backend
clauses.statement: A configuration owner or catalog backend whose conditional replacement is not linearizable raises `ConditionalWriteUnsupported` at startup or open.

clauses.subject: uninitialized-store
clauses.statement: An edit or apply against a store that has taken no explicit guarded import, an empty store included, raises `StoreNotInitialized`, answered `409`.

clauses.subject: region-entries
clauses.statement: A residency allow-set holds at most 16 entries.

clauses.subject: region-mismatch
clauses.statement: A configured resource resolving to a region the policy omits raises `EnforceRegionMismatch` at startup, and the runtime serves nothing.

clauses.subject: registry-unreadable
clauses.statement: A `CONTEXTFUL_STORES_JSON` value that does not parse raises `StoreRegistryUnreadable` at startup, and no built-in store stands in for the configured set.

clauses.subject: malformed-entry
clauses.statement: One entry that does not decode raises `StoreEntryMalformed` naming it, and is dropped while its siblings are served.

clauses.subject: reserved-id
clauses.statement: A configured entry claiming either built-in id raises `StoreIdReserved`.
clauses.why: because the entry otherwise reads the fixture's rows under its own name

clauses.subject: authored-name
clauses.statement: An entry carrying its own credential or binding name raises `StoreNameAuthored`.

clauses.subject: listing-page
clauses.statement: One listing call answers at most 1000 entries, flags truncation, and counts the keys the read route declines to serve.

clauses.subject: stdio-credential
clauses.statement: Over the process transport a credential is mandatory, a capability token or an explicit owner flag; an unset one raises `StdioCredentialMissing` and does not resolve to the owner context.

clauses.subject: store-selector
clauses.statement: The child's working directory selects the store by walking up to the project manifest; finding none raises `StoreSelectorAbsent` and exits before writing any protocol framing.

clauses.subject: redactor-lookahead
clauses.statement: The streaming redactor buffers 128 chars across each chunk boundary, and no denylist entry is longer than the buffer.
clauses.why: because an identifier split between two chunks otherwise passes unredacted

clauses.subject: unanswerable-suggestion
clauses.statement: A suggested prompt whose answer under these rules is a decline raises `ConsoleSuggestionUnanswerable` when the suggestion set is built.

clauses.subject: ungrounded-answer
clauses.statement: A path composing answer prose in a turn holding no tool result raises `ConsoleUngroundedAnswer`.

clauses.subject: unadmitted-tool
clauses.statement: A call naming a tool the turn's packs do not admit raises `ConsoleToolNotAdmitted` and dispatches nothing.

clauses.subject: mutating-tool
clauses.statement: The visitor-facing endpoint admits a read subset: a client-reachable path naming a write raises `ConsoleMutatingToolRequested`. The one write a turn performs is authored on the server.

clauses.subject: org-face-read-only
clauses.statement: A pack registering a write tool on an organization-wide face raises `ConsoleWriteToolOnOrgFace` at startup, naming the pack and the tool, and the face serves nothing.

clauses.subject: direct-file-read
clauses.statement: A table function resolving a path straight against stored bytes raises `ConsoleFileAccessDirect` on this surface.

clauses.subject: mint-refused
clauses.statement: A refused mint raises `ConsoleTokenExchangeRefused`. A store carrying a shared credential falls back to it; one carrying none surfaces the refusal to the reader.

clauses.subject: sources-per-turn
clauses.statement: A source list carries at most 8 entries.

clauses.subject: planner-reached-memory
clauses.statement: Scaffolding and every deterministic fallback cover data tables; scaffolding naming a memory relation raises `ConsolePlannerReachedMemory`.

clauses.subject: code-path-bounds
clauses.statement: The code path reads at most 5000 rows per data table and stops after 10 s.

clauses.subject: overlay-cache
clauses.statement: The overlay caches for 5 min, a miss included.

clauses.subject: overlay-length
clauses.statement: An overlay is truncated at 8000 chars.

clauses.subject: unparseable
clauses.statement: A vantage that is neither a calendar day nor an instant raises `ConsoleVantageUnparseable`, answered `400`.

clauses.subject: web-bound-unparseable
clauses.statement: A web leg whose bound fails to parse fails that leg and raises `ConsoleWebBoundUnparseable`.

clauses.subject: sample-labels
clauses.statement: A table's arrivals contribute at most 3 entries of sampled label.

clauses.subject: distillation
clauses.statement: After the answer streams, a second pass distils the exchange into at most 3 entries shaped `{subject, key, learning}`, zero included.

clauses.subject: unscoped
clauses.statement: A distilled conclusion landing without the reading-session scope raises `ConsoleLearningUnscoped`.

clauses.subject: client-authored-view
clauses.statement: A view specification arriving from a client, or composed by the model, raises `ConsoleViewNotServerBuilt`.

clauses.subject: component-choice
clauses.statement: One row with one measure draws a metric; a date column with a measure over 3 rows on distinct days draws a line; anything else draws a table offering a bar view.

clauses.subject: absence-is-earned
clauses.statement: The card needs a session with no turns, at present time, a live conclusion, an arrived row matching an interest, and a derivation inside its budget. An error or timeout raises `ConsoleBriefUnavailable`, and no card renders.

clauses.subject: topic-tier
clauses.statement: The topic tier needs at least 2 tokens shared between the conclusion's subject and text and the row's label and topics, one of them naming the subject.

clauses.subject: card-subjects
clauses.statement: A card carries at most 3 subjects.

clauses.subject: articles-per-subject
clauses.statement: A subject carries at most 3 entries of matched article.

clauses.subject: catchup-window
clauses.statement: The backend caps the requested window at 7 d.

clauses.subject: share-affordance
clauses.statement: A surface offering a share control on access-explanation output raises `VisibilityShareAffordance`.

clauses.subject: askerless-audience
clauses.statement: A scheduled job posting to an audience under a service identity raises `VisibilityAskerlessAudience`, naming the destination; a scheduled post's corpus is narrowed in the reviewed manifest to what the destination reaches.

clauses.subject: package
clauses.statement: The policy model is a Lean package rooted at `formal/`: `lakefile.toml` declares one `lean_lib` target and no `require` stanza, and `lean-toolchain` names one exact release string.

clauses.subject: declared-dependency
clauses.statement: A `require` stanza in the policy package's `lakefile.toml` reaching any external library raises `FormalPackageDependency`, naming the library.

clauses.subject: toolchain-drift
clauses.statement: A build whose resolved toolchain string differs from the pinned one raises `ProofToolchainDrift`, printing both strings.

clauses.subject: build-cost
clauses.statement: A cold elaboration of the package completes within 60 s and writes at most 512 KiB of artifacts.
clauses.why: because the check runs on every change

clauses.subject: build-command
clauses.statement: `lake build` at the package root elaborates every declaration and writes the environment the audit reads.

clauses.subject: module-layout
clauses.statement: Three modules carry the package — the layer algebra, placement with the floor, and the authority mapping — and the library root re-exports all three.

clauses.subject: layer
clauses.statement: A layer is a total function from a row identifier to `Bool`; `composed` folds a list of layers by conjunction, admitting a row when every member admits it.

clauses.subject: floor
clauses.statement: An allow-set is a decidable predicate over a placement value; `floor` intersects a list of allow-sets pointwise, and `floor []` admits every caller as the unit of that fold.

clauses.subject: placement-inductive
clauses.statement: The declared placement is an inductive type carrying its identifier inside the constructor, with one case per category the manifest admits and one case for an absent declaration.

clauses.subject: unmodelled-constructor
clauses.statement: A category the manifest admits with no case in the placement inductive raises `UnmodelledConstructor` at elaboration, naming the category.

clauses.subject: total-definitions
clauses.statement: Every definition is total and computable: none is marked `partial`, `noncomputable` or `opaque`, and decidable equality on each finite enumeration is derived.

clauses.subject: from-the-spec
clauses.statement: Each definition is written from the specification text and derived from no engine source.
clauses.why: because a definition copied from code makes every theorem restate the code instead of checking the specification

clauses.subject: out-of-model
clauses.statement: The policy package defines no credential bytes, signature verification, SQL semantics, journal write, process state or attacker observation, and no theorem reaches one.

clauses.subject: protocol-package
clauses.statement: The protocol model is a second Lean 4 package rooted at `formal/protocol/`, beside the policy package, pinned to the same `lean-toolchain` string, with one `lean_lib` and one `lean_exe` target; its `lakefile.toml` may `require` a pinned proof-automation library.

clauses.subject: protocol-model
clauses.statement: The protocol model is a total, computable step function over lease acquisition, renewal, expiry and release, the fenced compare-and-swap on the catalog row and the cursor object, holder pause, message delay and crash.

clauses.subject: protocol-safety
clauses.statement: Four invariants are Lean theorems over every reachable state: one lease holder per fence, fences only increase, no commit lands carrying a fence below the highest granted, and release keeps the lease object and its fence.

clauses.subject: protocol-theorems
clauses.statement: Each protocol invariant theorem is a required constant in the protocol package's inventory, audited by {{assurance.audit-assumptions.check-command}} against the same allowlist.

clauses.subject: protocol-check
clauses.statement: The gate evaluates every invariant on each state reached by every step sequence over three nodes and four lease generations; a breaking state raises `ProtocolInvariantViolated`, printing the shortest sequence reaching it.

clauses.subject: protocol-pins
clauses.statement: {{store.lease.stale-fence}} and {{store.fold.partial-snapshot}} pin to the protocol model's invariant theorems.

clauses.subject: composition-sound
clauses.statement: `composed_sound`: a row the fold over a list admits is admitted by every member of that list.

clauses.subject: narrowing
clauses.statement: `composed_narrows`: a row admitted by `l :: ls` is admitted by `ls`.
clauses.why: because appending a layer then removes rows and adds none

clauses.subject: order-is-specified
clauses.statement: The composition theorem ranges over the single order {{authority.compose.relation-order}} fixes, and filtering then masking is a different relation from masking then filtering.

clauses.subject: commutation-claim
clauses.statement: A claim that the enforcement stages commute raises `CommutationClaimed`.

clauses.subject: placement-is-a-layer
clauses.statement: `zone_layer_sound`: with the placement check as one more list member, a row the whole list admits was admitted by that check, with no bridging hypothesis.

clauses.subject: floor-no-downgrade
clauses.statement: `floor_no_downgrade`: a floor admitting a caller forces every member of its evidence list to admit that caller.

clauses.subject: fail-closed
clauses.statement: An evidence list holding one fail-closed member yields a floor admitting no public-cloud caller, and the fail-closed allow-set rejects both cloud categories.

clauses.subject: symbolic-inclusion
clauses.statement: Zone inclusion is decided by subsumption over patterns, quantified over every constructor and every identifier, the named provider and the undeclared case included.

clauses.subject: sampled-inclusion
clauses.statement: Inclusion decided by evaluating a fixed set of example values raises `ZoneInclusionSampled`.

clauses.subject: effective-policy
clauses.statement: An effective policy computed from two allow-sets is included in both.

clauses.subject: proof-targets
clauses.statement: The authority mapping of {{authority.profile.delegation-profile}} carries two proof targets: inclusion, and narrowing — for a fixed trusted environment, permission under an attenuated child implies permission under its parent.
clauses.why: because both are pure decision functions; the other candidate targets need an execution relation no clause specifies

clauses.subject: target-binding
clauses.statement: A proof target is bound to one authenticated query path, recorded beside it as a module path and a test, before the claim names it.

clauses.subject: unbound-target
clauses.statement: A target the claim names with no binding raises `ProofTargetUnbound`, naming the target.

clauses.subject: negative-space
clauses.statement: Beside each theorem, its negative space states what it leaves open: that the required members were in the list, that a member removes rather than tests, and that execution reaches the fold before an effect.

clauses.subject: no-negative-space
clauses.statement: A theorem published without its negative space raises `TheoremWithoutNegativeSpace`, naming the constant.

clauses.subject: mediation-from-composition
clauses.statement: A filter-composition theorem offered as a mediation theorem raises `MediationClaimedFromComposition`.
clauses.why: because mediation quantifies over the reachable states of an execution; composition quantifies over a list

clauses.subject: names-carry-reach
clauses.statement: A constant's name states the object it ranges over, not the property a reader hopes for.

clauses.subject: assumption
clauses.statement: An assumption is a declaration the Lean kernel accepts without proof: the set `#print axioms` reports for a constant, which the audit reads through `collectAxioms`.

clauses.subject: allowlist
clauses.statement: The assumption allowlist holds 2 entries, `propext` and `Quot.sound`, and every theorem's footprint is a subset of it.
clauses.why: because no required constant draws on `Classical.choice`

clauses.subject: transitive-audit
clauses.statement: Each required constant's assumption footprint is read transitively off the elaborated environment, naming every assumption reached.

clauses.subject: verdict-input
clauses.statement: A verdict is a function of the elaborated environment and the inventory alone; source text, declaration counts and the build's exit status decide nothing.
clauses.why: because elaboration reports a hole as a warning and exits zero, and a character pattern misses a hole spelled in parentheses

clauses.subject: assumption-outside-allowlist
clauses.statement: An assumption in a footprint and absent from the allowlist raises `AssumptionOutsideAllowlist`, printing the constant and the assumption.

clauses.subject: hole-assumption
clauses.statement: A footprint containing the hole assumption raises `ProofHoleAssumption`, naming the declaration, whatever its syntax spells.

clauses.subject: native-evaluation-assumption
clauses.statement: A footprint containing a per-declaration native-evaluation assumption raises `NativeEvaluationAssumption`, naming the declaration that minted it.

clauses.subject: inventory
clauses.statement: `formal/inventory.toml` holds one row per required constant — name, module, expected statement text, admitted assumptions, binding, negative space — edited apart from the declarations satisfying it.

clauses.subject: missing-constant
clauses.statement: A required constant absent from the elaborated environment raises `TheoremConstantMissing`.

clauses.subject: statement-drift
clauses.statement: A required constant whose elaborated statement differs from its expected text raises `TheoremStatementDrift`, printing both.

clauses.subject: inventory-change
clauses.statement: A change to a required statement lands in the commit carrying the proof it admits.

clauses.subject: report
clauses.statement: The report names the commit, the resolved toolchain, the allowlist and inventory revision applied, and for each required constant its statement match and the assumptions it reaches.

clauses.subject: check-command
clauses.statement: `contextful formal check` elaborates the package, matches every inventory row, audits every footprint, writes the report, and exits non-zero naming the first failing constant.

clauses.subject: two-phase
clauses.statement: A recheck rebuilds the package from the commit's own source and pinned toolchain into an empty artifact directory, fetching nothing, and re-runs the audit against the rebuilt environment.

clauses.subject: credential-free
clauses.statement: A recheck environment exposing a token, a signing key or a registry login raises `RecheckEnvironmentCredentialed`, naming the variable or file carrying it.

clauses.subject: report-mismatch
clauses.statement: A recheck whose per-constant statement text or assumption set differs from the first phase's raises `RecheckReportMismatch`, naming the constant.
clauses.why: because `.olean` output is not byte-reproducible across hosts and paths, while the per-constant report is the fact under check

clauses.subject: wall-time
clauses.statement: A recheck completes within 600 s.

clauses.subject: claim-sentence
clauses.statement: The assurance claim reads: these named decisions satisfy these named Lean specifications under these stated translation and runtime assumptions; each list resolves to code paths, constants and components in the tree.

clauses.subject: beyond-named-decisions
clauses.statement: A claim that the enforcement engine, or any object wider than the named decisions, is verified raises `ClaimBeyondNamedDecisions`.

clauses.subject: trusted-dependencies
clauses.statement: The claim names the delegation library, its cryptography, its parser and the translator as trusted dependencies, and proves none of them.

clauses.subject: unnamed-dependency
clauses.statement: A claim resting on a component absent from its trusted-dependency list raises `TrustedDependencyUnnamed`, naming the component.

clauses.subject: translation-chain
clauses.statement: A statement about translated code inherits four links: the compiler's lowering, the translator, hand-written models of external definitions, and the production build configuration.

clauses.subject: unstated-chain
clauses.statement: A theorem claimed over translated code without its translation chain raises `TranslationChainUnstated`.

clauses.subject: refinement-scope
clauses.statement: Refinement covers the decision functions behind the two proof targets, whose inputs are values and whose outputs are decisions.

clauses.subject: refinement-exceeded
clauses.statement: Translation reaching cryptography, a parsing adapter, a database call or concurrency raises `RefinementScopeExceeded`, naming the module.

clauses.subject: reference-model
clauses.statement: The reference model is an executable Lean rendering of the decision functions, built to a binary that reads one case on standard input and prints one decision.

clauses.subject: harness
clauses.statement: The harness drives the reference binary and the engine's decision function over each generated case and compares the two decisions field by field.

clauses.subject: case-classes
clauses.statement: Each run generates malformed inputs, boundary values and well-formed requests, and its report names the classes it drew from.
clauses.why: because a green run is evidence over the generated classes, not an equivalence proof

clauses.subject: minimized
clauses.statement: A disagreement is shrunk until removing any further field makes the two agree, and the minimized case is recorded.

clauses.subject: corpus-replay
clauses.statement: Every counterexample-corpus case replays before any freshly generated case.

clauses.subject: corpus-entries
clauses.statement: The counterexample corpus retains at most 256 entries, evicting the oldest case a fresh seed reproduces.

clauses.subject: run-budget
clauses.statement: One invocation, corpus replay included, completes within 300 s.

clauses.subject: disagreement
clauses.statement: A case on which the two decisions differ raises `ReferenceModelDrift`, printing the minimized case and both decisions.

clauses.subject: discarded-counterexample
clauses.statement: A run reporting a disagreement and writing no corpus entry raises `CounterexampleDiscarded`.

clauses.subject: seed
clauses.statement: Each run records its generator seed, and re-running with that seed reproduces the same case sequence.

clauses.subject: protocol-cases
clauses.statement: Protocol cases are operation sequences and node interleavings a `proptest-state-machine` generator draws over acquire, renew, release, expire, commit, pause, delay and crash steps across three nodes.

clauses.subject: protocol-harness
clauses.statement: The harness drives the protocol package's compiled executable and the Rust store through each protocol case, comparing lease holder, fence, pointer ETag and commit outcome after every step.

clauses.subject: protocol-drift
clauses.statement: A step after which the model's state and the store's projected state differ raises `ProtocolConformanceDrift`, printing the minimized operation sequence and both states.

clauses.subject: command
clauses.statement: `contextful formal differential --seed <n> --cases <n>` replays the corpus, then runs the generated cases, exiting non-zero on the first disagreement.

clauses.subject: one-home
clauses.statement: Enforcement, control-plane state, credential resolution, statement guarding and visibility each resolve to one implementation in the engine; a surface reaches one through the engine route or the registered view compiling it in.

clauses.subject: duplicated-capability
clauses.statement: A surface or crate carrying a second implementation of an engine capability, in any language, or a hand-written copy of an engine constant, raises `CapabilityDuplicated`, naming both sites.

clauses.subject: decision-module
clauses.statement: One module owns the enforcement decision; a gateway and the engine reaching the same verdict execute it, compiled native and to WebAssembly from one pinned source.

clauses.subject: adapter
clauses.statement: A surface with no engine process on its request path implements an adapter against the engine's ports.

clauses.subject: derivation-check
clauses.statement: A generated artifact declares the check that fails once its source moves, and the gate's schema stage runs that check.

clauses.subject: mirror-exemption
clauses.statement: A review-time restatement of a build-time rule is admitted where its site carries a `mirrors: <clause id>` comment naming the clause it restates; an unannotated restatement stays {{assurance.structure-tree.duplicated-capability}}.
clauses.why: because a reviewer-facing check sometimes restates a rule, and the annotation keeps the engine its one home and the copy traceable to it

clauses.subject: mirror-unresolved
clauses.statement: A `mirrors:` comment in a tracked file under `crates/`, `tools/` or `apps/` naming no clause of `spec/spec.lock.json` raises `MirrorUnresolved` in the schema stage, naming the file and line.
clauses.why: because an annotation naming nothing exempts a copy while tying it to no rule it could drift from

clauses.subject: typed-subcommand
clauses.statement: An automation step carrying a branch, a loop or a retry, or running past 5 lines, is a typed subcommand shelling out to compiled binaries.

clauses.subject: subcommand-surface
clauses.statement: A subcommand exposes typed options, generated help and an entry point a test calls directly.

clauses.subject: one-path
clauses.statement: The gate invokes the subcommand a contributor invokes.
clauses.why: because a local reproduction and a gate run then execute one code path

clauses.subject: unchecked-shell
clauses.statement: A shell file in the tree that `shellcheck` rejects raises `ShellCheckFailed` in the toolchain stage.

clauses.subject: build-time-toolchain
clauses.statement: The automation toolchain links into no build profile and enters no release artifact.

clauses.subject: presence-before-absence
clauses.statement: A test whose central claim is an absence first constructs the condition it names and verifies that condition obtains.

clauses.subject: vacuous-exclusion
clauses.statement: An exclusion assertion evaluated over an empty collection raises `VacuousAssertion`.

clauses.subject: guard-fires-both-ways
clauses.statement: A guard is validated against the fixture that motivated it and against the state it stands against, passing on the first and failing on the second.

clauses.subject: one-integration-binary
clauses.statement: A crate's integration tests compile in one target, `tests/integration/main.rs`, which declares each suite as a module selected by path.
clauses.why: because each file directly under `tests/` links its own static binary, hundreds of MiB for an engine-linked crate

clauses.subject: feature-gated-suite
clauses.statement: A feature-gated suite carries a module-level `cfg` attribute at the head of its module file and compiles to nothing while its feature is off.

clauses.subject: own-process
clauses.statement: A test needing its own process sits in a top-level file stating why at its site; a thread-scoped log capture is such a test.

clauses.subject: connector-kit
clauses.statement: The connector authoring toolkit ships a conformance suite — discovery returns valid schemas, an opened table yields a finite stream, a position round-trips — plus recorded-HTTP fixture replay and property tests over position monotonicity.

clauses.subject: test-first
clauses.statement: A change altering Rust source under `crates/` or `tools/` adds or alters a test under a package's `tests/` that fails against the base commit's source; a change without one raises `TestNotFirst`.

clauses.subject: test-first-scope
clauses.statement: The test-first stage builds each changed test file's target against the base source, then runs exactly the tests under that file's top-level module; a target failing to compile there counts as failing.

clauses.subject: base-run-bound
clauses.statement: One test-first execution against the base, its build excluded, runs for at most 300 s; a run past the bound is killed with its process group and counts as failing.

clauses.subject: base-unrunnable
clauses.statement: A base invocation whose output reports a full disk, an unloadable manifest or an unfetchable dependency raises `TestFirstBaseUnrunnable` instead of a verdict.
clauses.why: because such a fault fails at base whatever the tests assert, and reading it as red admits an untested change

clauses.subject: refactor-trailer
clauses.statement: A commit carrying the trailer `Test-First: refactor` exempts the source it alters from {{assurance.test.test-first}}; the rest of the range stays held, and the workspace stage alone holds that commit.
clauses.why: because a behavior-preserving change has no failing test to write, and the existing suite is its specification

clauses.subject: acceptance-surface
clauses.statement: An acceptance test drives a built binary through its command line, MCP or HTTP surface; a workspace package among the acceptance package's dependencies raises `AcceptanceLinksEngine`.

clauses.subject: target-dir-per-stage
clauses.statement: Each cargo stage builds into a target directory of its own, reclaimed once the stage passes.
clauses.why: because stages under different feature unification share no artifacts, and peak disk is then one stage

clauses.subject: one-engine-build
clauses.statement: The engine-linked packages build in one cargo invocation over the union of their features, compiling the bundled SQL engine once per gate run.

clauses.subject: staged-feature-runs
clauses.statement: A defect appearing under one feature combination alone is reached by a staged run, one command per container.

clauses.subject: linked-query-functions
clauses.statement: Columnar file reading and statement serialization link into every build linking the SQL engine, and the read path loads no extension while serving.

clauses.subject: runtime-extension-load
clauses.statement: A read path loading an extension into a binary that statically links the SQL engine raises `ExtensionAutoloadRefused`.

clauses.subject: debug-info
clauses.statement: Development and test profiles carry line-tables-only debug information.

clauses.subject: targets
clauses.statement: All three profiles cross-compile to `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`; edge and full also build for `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`; edge also targets `wasm32-wasip2`.

clauses.subject: release-artifact
clauses.statement: Each profile ships a release archive with a SHA-256 checksum and an SBOM, a package-manager formula and an independently tagged container image; the bare formula name and the install script resolve to the full profile.

clauses.subject: licence-field
clauses.statement: Every workspace package under `crates/` or `tools/` declares `license = "Apache-2.0"`, inherited from `[workspace.package]`; a package declaring another value or none raises `PackageLicenceMissing`, naming its manifest.
clauses.why: because cargo-deny, cargo-about and SBOM generators read the manifest field, not the `LICENSE` file, so an unlicensed package fails a consumer's licence check

clauses.subject: dependency-allowlist
clauses.statement: The connector authoring dependency allowlist carries a linear-time regular-expression engine and bounded-depth deserialization, and admits no backtracking regex engine and no unbounded recursive parser.

clauses.subject: stage-sequence
clauses.statement: The gate runs its stages in order — pins, toolchain, schema, test-first, workspace, acceptance, evaluate, features, crate graph, connectors, TypeScript surfaces, formal, budget — and a subset is selectable by name.

clauses.subject: remote-check
clauses.statement: The pull-request workflow dispatches every stage the gate subcommand defines to a remote runner, each as one status check labelled with the stage's name.

clauses.subject: fork-dispatch
clauses.statement: The pull-request workflow dispatches only a head commit pushed to the repository itself; a pull request from a fork dispatches no stage and so carries none of the required checks.
clauses.why: because a dispatch carries the org's signing secret and runs the commit on the org's runner, and an absent required check fails closed

clauses.subject: stage-reports
clauses.statement: Each stage prints the environment it leaves and its memory limit, peak and event counts, and a failing stage prints its diagnostics before propagating its exit code.
clauses.why: because memory exhaustion is silent, and a kill then reads as a number in the log

clauses.subject: pins-stage
clauses.statement: The pins stage resolves every pinned artifact identity a run depends on before any compilation.

clauses.subject: evaluate-stage
clauses.statement: The evaluate stage runs every gate-tier ledger entry and the native case set in the deterministic tier, and reports the floor and baseline verdicts.

clauses.subject: schema-stage
clauses.statement: The schema stage regenerates each derived artifact into a scratch location, compares it byte for byte against the committed copy, and runs `contextful-spec lint`.

clauses.subject: secret-ciphertext
clauses.statement: In the schema stage, a key other than `DOTENV_PUBLIC_KEY*` in a git-tracked `.env*` file other than `.env.example` holding a value without the `encrypted:` prefix, or a tracked `.env.keys`, raises `SecretPlaintext`, naming file and key.
clauses.why: because a tracked file reaches every clone, and only dotenvx ciphertext is safe there while its private key stays untracked

clauses.subject: secret-scope
clauses.statement: In the schema stage, a key other than `DOTENV_PUBLIC_KEY*` in a git-tracked `.env*` file whose block — the assignments above it, up to the first blank line — opens with no comment carrying text raises `SecretScopeMissing`, naming file and key.
clauses.why: because a provider token cannot report its own grants, so the comment above it is the one record of what it reaches

clauses.subject: crate-graph
clauses.statement: A test over `cargo metadata` holds run-path crates to reaching read-path crates through the three crossing crates alone; another edge raises `CrateGraphViolation`, naming both crates.

clauses.subject: row-token
clauses.statement: Every row-returning function of the store crate takes the enforcement token type, whose constructor is private to the enforcement module; a row path outside a registered relation raises `EnforceUnmediatedPath`, naming the function.

clauses.subject: dependency-deny
clauses.statement: The crate-graph stage runs cargo-deny over each profile's resolved graph, with a deny list holding every crate a dependency refusal of another contract names; a hit raises that clause's error.

clauses.subject: unconfigured-egress
clauses.statement: An outbound call reachable under the default configuration — usage ping, license check, update probe — raises `UnconfiguredEgress` in the crate-graph stage, naming the call site.
clauses.why: because some deployments run with no external reach, and a call nobody configured moves data outside every grant, zone and audit record

clauses.subject: interpolated-claim
clauses.statement: A source lint over the runtime crates finding a subject claim formatted into SQL text raises `EnforceInterpolatedSubjectClaim`, naming the file and line.

clauses.subject: formal-stage
clauses.statement: The formal stage runs {{assurance.audit-assumptions.check-command}}, {{assurance.differential-test.command}} and {{assurance.model.protocol-check}}; a non-zero exit from any reds the run.

clauses.subject: container
clauses.statement: The gate container carries four ceilings — processor count, 12 GiB of memory, 18 GiB of usable disk, and a per-stage wall clock — and a run dies on any one.

clauses.subject: parallel-jobs
clauses.statement: Parallel build jobs number the memory ceiling divided by 3 GiB.

clauses.subject: free-disk
clauses.statement: A stage starting with less than 2 GiB of free disk raises `BuildDiskPrecondition` and exits 28 before doing work.

clauses.subject: build-size
clauses.statement: The budget stage holds total build size to 12 GiB, printing that size, the free space and the largest artifacts; a larger build raises `BuildSizeCeilingExceeded`, naming the head of that list.

clauses.subject: edge-budget
clauses.statement: The edge profile holds to 50 MiB compressed and 60 MiB idle resident set.

clauses.subject: full-budget
clauses.statement: The full profile holds to 150 MiB compressed and 180 MiB idle resident set.

clauses.subject: control-budget
clauses.statement: The control profile holds to 60 MiB compressed and 80 MiB idle resident set.

clauses.subject: footprint
clauses.statement: Per change and per profile, the footprint step builds the static-linked Linux target, compresses it, and holds its size to the profile's budget and its dynamic dependencies to the platform C library.

clauses.subject: footprint-exceeded
clauses.statement: An artifact over its profile's budget, or carrying a dynamic dependency beyond the platform C library, raises `FootprintBudgetExceeded`, naming the profile.

clauses.subject: typescript-surfaces
clauses.statement: The TypeScript surfaces run typecheck, unit tests and framework build in one stage, and a surface declaring no script for a check skips that check.

clauses.subject: surface-check-failed
clauses.statement: A surface whose typecheck, unit tests or framework build fails raises `SurfaceCheckFailed`, naming the surface and the script.

clauses.subject: real-read-path
clauses.statement: An evaluation run ingests, indexes, retrieves, reads, judges and scores through the surfaces a caller uses, and the harness adds no storage or runtime primitive.

clauses.subject: through-the-store
clauses.statement: The corpus loads through the real store, and the retriever under test calls {{read.retrieve.ranked-call}} with the options a caller passes.
clauses.why: because an unordered full-scan retriever cannot go red when ranking breaks

clauses.subject: policy-labels
clauses.statement: An evaluation corpus carries zone and row-policy labels, and a run reads it through the access-control path.

clauses.subject: unlabeled-corpus
clauses.statement: A run over a corpus carrying neither labels nor an explicit local zone raises `EvalCorpusUnlabeled`.

clauses.subject: case-format
clauses.statement: A case carries an id, a corpus reference, a question, tags, and an expected block of answer, artifacts, edges, entities, must-cite, must-abstain and time anchor.

clauses.subject: converter
clauses.statement: Each benchmark and application ground truth converts once into the case format through its own converter, and the runner reads nothing else.

clauses.subject: deterministic-tier
clauses.statement: Recall@k, R-precision, hit-rate@k, reciprocal rank and nDCG@k run with no model call, reported per leg — lexical, vector, hybrid — and per slice.

clauses.subject: distinct-top-k
clauses.statement: Membership in the top k is distinct, and a repeated id counts once.

clauses.subject: absent-truth
clauses.statement: A ranked metric over a case with no relevant set is NaN and drops out of every aggregate; an empty ranking against a non-empty relevant set scores zero.

clauses.subject: precision-floor
clauses.statement: Precision at rank min(k, R), R being the relevant-set size, holds at or above 60 percent.
clauses.why: because precision@k caps at R/k, below the floor whenever R is small

clauses.subject: forbidden-row-rate
clauses.statement: A row named in a must-not-retrieve set holds at 0 percent of a regression case's returned rows.

clauses.subject: duplicate-row-rate
clauses.statement: A repeated table-and-row-key pair holds at 0 percent of the ranking.

clauses.subject: in-window-rate
clauses.statement: A case declaring a recency bound holds its in-window rate at or above 95 percent.

clauses.subject: abstention
clauses.statement: A must-abstain case returns zero rows.

clauses.subject: truth-per-surface
clauses.statement: Expected artifacts score the artifact retriever and expected edges score the edge retriever, reported apart; edge truth with no edge surface configured counts in an unscored tally.

clauses.subject: judged-dimensions
clauses.statement: The reading stage adds four judged dimensions: answer accuracy; abstention, as correct-refusal and hallucination-on-unknown rates; citation faithfulness; and temporal correctness against the bitemporal columns.

clauses.subject: grounded-reader
clauses.statement: The harness reader answers from retrieved rows alone, and the deterministic tier substitutes a stub reader.

clauses.subject: model-endpoint
clauses.statement: The judge and the reader reach a model through {{connector.infer.model-endpoint}}, and the harness holds no credential.

clauses.subject: judge
clauses.statement: The judge is one pinned open-weights instruct model, called once per judged item at temperature zero; a judge swap is a full re-baseline.
clauses.why: because a majority vote at temperature zero samples one mode and adds cost without reducing variance

clauses.subject: systems-metrics
clauses.statement: Tokens per query, latency and cost report beside the quality figures, bucketed by corpus size in tokens relative to the reader's context window.

clauses.subject: checkpoint
clauses.statement: A run appends each case's result as JSONL, and a crash re-runs the in-flight case.

clauses.subject: run-report
clauses.statement: A run report carries one field per gated metric, the sample count behind each mean, the run block, the per-slice breakdown, and the tally of cases sampled, dropped and unscored.

clauses.subject: file
clauses.statement: A baseline file carries a reserved run block `{k, tier, model, samples}` and one entry per gated metric: a bare number at the run's dead band, or an object overriding the band.

clauses.subject: default-dead-band
clauses.statement: A rate-valued entry with no override gates at a 2 percent dead band.

clauses.subject: rank-quality-dead-band
clauses.statement: The ranked-quality entry gates at a 3 percent dead band.

clauses.subject: band-units
clauses.statement: A band carries its metric's own units, and a count entry is pinned at zero with no band.

clauses.subject: metric-path
clauses.statement: An entry names a metric by the report's field path: `retrieval.<modality>.<metric>`, `edge_retrieval.<modality>.<metric>`, `judge.<dimension>`, `latency_ms`, `n_cases`, or `slices.<tag>.` before a bare `<metric>` or any of these but `latency_ms`.

clauses.subject: sample-count
clauses.statement: Every mean-valued path takes a `.n` suffix naming its sample count.
clauses.why: because blanking one case's truth lifts a NaN-filtered mean without moving the case count

clauses.subject: unresolvable-path
clauses.statement: A path resolving to nothing, a mean over fewer than 30 cases, a malformed entry or a non-finite band raises `BaselinePathUnresolved` before the suite runs.

clauses.subject: run-stamp-drift
clauses.statement: A run block differing from the run's own configuration raises `BaselineRunStampMismatch` before the suite runs.

clauses.subject: interval
clauses.statement: Each judged figure reports a 95 percent percentile-bootstrap interval over cases from 1000 resamples.

clauses.subject: raise-only
clauses.statement: A baseline update runs after every gate and floor passes, moves each improved entry to its measured value, moves none in the worse direction, and adds no path.

clauses.subject: floors-are-absolute
clauses.statement: An absolute floor gates independently of every committed value.

clauses.subject: floor-coverage
clauses.statement: A report lacking a floor's figure on any leg of its `retrieval` surface breaches that floor; only a forbidden-row or in-window rate over no case holds.

clauses.subject: offline
clauses.statement: The gate is a local command comparing the report against in-tree baselines and floors, reporting both verdicts, with or without a trace store reachable.

clauses.subject: trace-store
clauses.statement: A trace store records run history and curation staging, and decides no verdict.

clauses.subject: golden-custody
clauses.statement: Version-controlled JSONL under `evals/cases/` is the canonical golden set, one loader is its only ingestion door, and a reviewer's edit reaches the gate as a change to the tree.

clauses.subject: answer-key-in-the-store
clauses.statement: An artifact path normalizing under the evaluation directory, reached by a manifest lint or a connector, raises `GoldenSetIngested`.

clauses.subject: generated-redaction
clauses.statement: A golden mined from a live query or promoted from a labeled outcome passes {{authority.redact.write-time}} before commit; a case it cannot redact raises `GoldenRedactionFailed`.

clauses.subject: promotion-source
clauses.statement: Only an adjudicated outcome label promotes into a golden set; a self-rated row does not.

clauses.subject: generators
clauses.statement: Three generators draft candidate cases from the deployment's store — entity-to-fact-to-edge walks, composed edge chains, and questions about absent entities — and a human approves each before commit.

clauses.subject: held-out
clauses.statement: Retrieval and synthesis are tuned on no gate input.

clauses.subject: rotation
clauses.statement: The native set rotates on a cadence, a sample of its truth is reviewed on each rotation, and a comparison across generations resolves through the pinned run stamp.

clauses.subject: native-gate
clauses.statement: A native benchmark generated from a real corpus is the red or green gate; public benchmark sets run beside it as held-out comparison and decide nothing.

clauses.subject: trace-export
clauses.statement: A run touching a deployed store with a hosted trace endpoint configured raises `TraceExportOutOfPerimeter`; hosted collection serves runs over public or synthetic fixtures alone.

clauses.subject: ledger
clauses.statement: `evals/ledger.toml` holds one entry per tracked target: an id, an owning clause id, a run-report metric path, a tier, a method naming one integration test, case set or probe, and a threshold.

clauses.subject: unresolved-entry
clauses.statement: An entry whose owning clause, method or metric path resolves to nothing raises `MeasureEntryUnresolved` before any measure runs.
scenarios: WHEN an entry names `run.journal.entry-keys`, THEN the run raises `MeasureEntryUnresolved` and no test runs.

clauses.subject: open-entry
clauses.statement: An entry naming an issue in place of a method reports open and gates nothing, and `evals/ledger.md` carries every entry's computed status.
scenarios: WHEN an entry's method is `{ issue = 43 }`, THEN `evals/ledger.md` lists it open and the evaluate stage ignores it.

clauses.subject: tier
clauses.statement: A gate-tier entry decides the evaluate stage, a trend-tier entry records on every run and decides nothing, and a scheduled-tier entry runs on the scheduled job alone.

clauses.subject: count-first
clauses.statement: A gate-tier entry measures a count, a ratio within one run or a size under a locked resolve; a wall-clock or resident-memory figure is trend-tier.
clauses.why: because a shared container moves wall-clock figures past any band narrow enough to catch a regression

clauses.subject: record
clauses.statement: A measure writes one JSON record carrying its entry id, value, sample count, seed and run stamp; a gate-tier method finishing without one raises `MeasureRecordMissing`.

clauses.subject: seeded
clauses.statement: Every generated fixture and randomized schedule derives from the record's seed, and replaying that seed reproduces a count-valued entry's value.
clauses.why: because a failure that cannot replay cannot be fixed

clauses.subject: seed-mismatch
clauses.statement: A record whose seed differs from its entry's declared seed raises `MeasureSeedMismatch`, and the entry counts as red.
clauses.why: because a figure measured under another seed replays nothing the ledger names

clauses.subject: timing-iterations
clauses.statement: A timed batch reports p50 and p95 over 200 repeats of its operation, each after warm-up.

clauses.subject: timing-batches
clauses.statement: A timed figure is the median of 5 repeats of its timed batch.

clauses.subject: trend-band
clauses.statement: A trend figure more than 25 percent worse than its baseline annotates the run report and fails no stage.
scenarios: WHEN a trend p95 moves from 40 ms to 52 ms on a matching runner stamp, THEN the report carries a +30 percent annotation and the stage passes.

clauses.subject: runner-stamp
clauses.statement: The run block carries the runner's processor model, processor count and memory limit, and a trend figure compares only against a baseline with the same stamp.

clauses.subject: absolute-threshold
clauses.statement: A threshold is an absolute figure of this system's own measure, and it tightens only through {{assurance.baseline.raise-only}}.

clauses.subject: history
clauses.statement: A run on the default branch attaches its run report to the measured commit under `refs/notes/measures`, and no verdict reads a note.

clauses.subject: scheduled
clauses.statement: A nightly job runs every tier against the default-branch head and reports one check per run.

clauses.subject: measured-basis
clauses.statement: A bound with a measured basis names a trend-tier or scheduled-tier ledger entry id as its benchmark.

ledes.assurance.audit-assumptions: The assumption allowlist, the transitive footprint audit over the elaborated environment, the inventory and the report.
ledes.assurance.automate: Typed subcommands over compiled binaries, and the boundary shell keeps.
ledes.assurance.baseline: Holding a run against committed baselines and absolute floors, intervals, golden custody and case generation.
ledes.assurance.build: Target directories, the engine-linked invocation, linked query functions, build targets, release artifacts and the dependency allowlist.
ledes.assurance.differential-test: The executable reference models, the case generators, the minimized counterexample corpus and the command running them.
ledes.assurance.evaluate: The read-path quality harness: case format, deterministic metrics and floors, judged dimensions, the reader and the judge.
ledes.assurance.gate: Stage order, secrets of record, the crate-graph, row-token, egress and dependency rules, the formal stage, the container's ceilings, disk, footprint budgets and surface checks.
ledes.assurance.measure: The target ledger: each tracked target, the clause it serves, how it is measured and its record per commit.
ledes.assurance.model: The Lean policy package and the Lean protocol state machine, their pins, and the definitions theorems and checks range over.
ledes.assurance.prove: The theorem inventory: layer composition, placement, the evidence floor, and the proof targets over the authority mapping.
ledes.assurance.recheck: Rebuilding and re-auditing from pinned source in a credential-free environment.
ledes.assurance.scope-claim: The sentence the assurance claim is allowed to be: named decisions, trusted dependencies, translation chain, refinement reach.
ledes.assurance.structure-tree: One home per capability, the one enforcement decision module, adapters, mirror annotations and derived-artifact checks.
ledes.assurance.test: Assertion construction, guard validation, suite placement, test-first and acceptance tests, and the connector test kit.
ledes.authority.attenuate: Deriving a narrower child offline, and the narrowing legality of each grant dimension.
ledes.authority.bound-redistribution: The per-table licence bound applied at push, the root-object allowlist, and the per-credential edge filter.
ledes.authority.compose: The three layers as one reference monitor, and the order a registered relation applies.
ledes.authority.exchange: Trading a verified external assertion for a scoped credential under injected verifying material and a declared policy.
ledes.authority.filter-rows: The typed row-predicate grammar, subject binding, the tenant equality and the project default.
ledes.authority.grant: What a credential says a holder does: actions, table patterns, tenant scope, the template allowlist, ceilings, and resources answering by name.
ledes.authority.identify: The subject tuple, its per-member attestation, hygiene at the mint, and the identity links connecting a subject to a source's principals.
ledes.authority.issue: Minting: the persisted lifetime ceiling, the principal a row-landing grant needs, signing custody, and the authoring posture.
ledes.authority.mask: Column classes, strategies and combines, guardrails over an exhaustible value space, the pepper, and masked behavior under caller SQL.
ledes.authority.place: Inference zones: grammar, composition across grains, floors, incognito, and the serve-time outcome.
ledes.authority.profile: The versioned delegation profile over the attenuable-credential library: admitted elements, reserved facts, the bounded evaluator, the scoped session.
ledes.authority.redact: Removal and transformation inside the writer, ahead of columnar bytes and the run path's durable record.
ledes.authority.refuse: The two shapes an unauthorized read takes, the scope guard, and what a refusal discloses.
ledes.authority.resist: The paths that stay closed to an injected instruction.
ledes.authority.revoke: Ending a credential's usefulness ahead of expiry: short lifetimes, the denylist, the scoped epoch, key rotation, format withdrawal.
ledes.authority.verify: Admission at a checkpoint: signatures, audience, timestamps, possession proof, key sets, and the admitted-authority value.
ledes.connector.attach: Host mediation of an outbound request: the transport port, the bound host, address vetting, header templates, origin pinning and URL scrubbing.
ledes.connector.declare-capability: The manifest's statement of host access and the scope probe judging a bound credential's grant.
ledes.connector.export: The calls a connector offers across the boundary: the shared types, the source and destination worlds, the optional worlds, the compiled-in sibling.
ledes.connector.import: What crosses inward: the three host imports and the forwarded guest configuration table.
ledes.connector.infer: Model egress: the single endpoint, the data fence and the trust label of model output.
ledes.connector.lease: The declaration-scoped lease provider at the head of the chain: endpoint, expiry, failure classes and bootstrap.
ledes.connector.meter: Reservation against a shared vendor quota and the one pre-send hook it implements: declaration, binding, the hook's position and intent, permits, denial and the usage report.
ledes.connector.package: Distribution form, digest pinning, per-connector resource bounds and world versioning.
